jobs.title: AML/CFT & Fraud Analyst - Internship
jobs.description:
ABOUT BITSTACK

It all started with an idea in 2021. Initially built to democratize Bitcoin in France, Bitstack has gone from a simple product that invests spare change in bitcoin, to a crypto-native bank bringing a better way to save, spend, and grow money to our 300K+ users. We want to rebuild finance from the ground up to empower people to achieve financial freedom by participating in a more open and inclusive financial system. We’re a small, ambitious team of operators. We believe in moving fast, sweating the details, and creating products people truly love. At Bitstack, you’ll have the opportunity to shape not just our products, but the culture and practices of our entire organization. Bitstack is backed by YC, leading VCs like 13books Capital, Stillmark, Serena, and many more. We are building a product our users love and we are just getting started!

The Role

Bitstack is a crypto-asset service provider authorised under the MiCA Regulation. As such, we are subject to strict requirements relating to anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and fraud prevention.

As part of the Compliance team, you will contribute to the day-to-day implementation of our compliance framework. You will review alerts and customer cases across three key areas: transaction monitoring, screening and KYC.

What You'll Be Doing

1. Transaction Monitoring (Fiat & Crypto)

 - Analyse and investigate transaction monitoring alerts across euro payment flows (card payments and SEPA transfers) and crypto flows (on-chain deposits and withdrawals).

 - Examine transaction patterns, counterparties and wallet exposure to assess each alert and determine whether it is a false positive or should be escalated.

 - Detect fraudulent activity, including payment fraud, account takeovers and scams targeting our users.

 - Document your findings and, where appropriate, prepare the supporting information for a suspicious activity report to TRACFIN, the French financial intelligence unit.

 - Contribute to improving detection scenarios and monitoring alert metrics.

2. Screening: PEPs, Sanctions & Adverse Media

 - Review screening alerts and determine whether a match is genuine or a false positive.

 - Implement enhanced due diligence measures for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including checks on the source of funds and source of wealth.

 - Escalate confirmed matches against sanctions lists or adverse media findings in accordance with internal procedures.

3. KYC (Know Your Customer)

 - Review and validate customer supporting documents, including proof of identity, proof of address, proof of income, source of funds and source of wealth.

 - Detect identity theft attempts and forged documents.

 - Assess consistency between the customer's profile, declared information and observed activity.

 - Request additional documentation and follow up on cases through to their final decision.

You will also contribute to updating internal procedures and monitoring emerging fraud and money laundering typologies within the crypto ecosystem.

You will gain hands-on experience with an AML/CFT framework at a regulated crypto-asset service provider. You will learn how alerts are handled from initial detection through to the final decision, how a risk-based approach is applied, how blockchain analytics tools are used, and how the Compliance team collaborates with Product, Operations and Customer Support.

What We're Looking For

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Compliance, Law, Finance, Risk Management or a related field, and looking for an internship or work-study placement.

 - Previous exposure to AML/CFT, KYC or fraud prevention through an internship, coursework or certification is a plus, but not required.

 - Highly organised, rigorous and detail-oriented.

 - Able to draw well-reasoned conclusions and clearly document findings in writing.

 - Comfortable using spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets), with a strong interest in crypto-assets and blockchain technology.

 - Discreet and meticulous when handling sensitive personal data.

 - Fluent in French and comfortable working in English.

Perks & Benefits
💻 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely

🕑 Flexible working hours

🏄Team activities and annual offsites

🍉 Swile meal vouchers

DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

We hire talented and passionate people from all kinds of backgrounds, we don’t care about your age or where you studied. If you’re excited about the role but your past experience doesn’t match every bullet point in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. What matters most is that you’re a builder at heart, you share our values, and you’re enthusiastic about our mission.

We’re excited to continue the momentum working alongside our investors and advisors from Andreessen Horowitz, Emergence Capital, Y Combinator, Avra, and Ardent. To learn more about us, check out our blog https://methodfi.com/resources/company-updates!

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring Method's first Design Engineer. This is someone who spends most of their time in the code, but with an elite eye and talent for product, visual, and motion design. You'll partner with our Head of Design to own the craft layer across all of Method's web properties: website, design system, demos, and product. You'll work as a duo to set the aesthetic direction, make the technical calls, and ship the work.

Method is a developer-first financial connectivity platform, and our visual identity should feel like it. We want our products to feel precise, technically credible, and genuinely interesting to look at.

We're rebuilding our entire visual and interactive layer at once: a token system covering color (built on perceptual color science), typography, and spacing, a design system from the ground up, a new marketing site, a dashboard with generative UI and charting, and the embedded experience our partners put in front of their own users. Because the embedded product runs inside our partners' apps, it needs to adapt to match their brand, automatically.

You'll work closely with engineers and our Head of Design to bring a level of frontend craft to Method that the current team can't fully own, and oversee a ton of green-space to up-level how customers and end-users interact with Method. Open source is part of this role. We want to build things worth sharing and give Method a point of view the design and creative-coding communities respect.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the visual and interactive quality of Method's design system including component states, motion, and consistency across surfaces.

 - Build shader-based experiences for the website using Three.js and WebGL: hero sections, ambient motion, branded interactive moments.

 - Redesign and elevate the dashboard beyond a reskin; considered transitions, polished data visualization, generative UI components driven by JSON.

 - Architect a component library that supports dynamic, on-the-fly UI construction (charts, layouts, elements assembled from structured data).

 - Make judgment calls on when to invest in bespoke work versus leveraging existing tooling, and communicate those tradeoffs clearly.

 - Reduce reliance on contractors for production design and front-end UI work.

 - Collaborate with engineers and Head of Design on design direction; eventually help scope and hire adjacent design talent as the team grows.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have shipped interactive web work that required writing shaders; Three.js, WebGL, GLSL. Your portfolio shows it!

 - You understand the full stack from GPU rendering to React component architecture; you know why it matters that this runs in-browser and not as a video.

 - You have strong aesthetic opinions and the technical range to execute them without a dedicated designer handing you comps.

 - You've built production design systems and component libraries that others actually use.

 - You're an individual contributor by nature and default to building.

 - You've worked at or contributed to places with genuine design craft: design studios, developer tooling companies, creative agencies, or strong indie dev work.

 - You're comfortable being the only person in this specialty for a while; you don't need structure to make progress.

 - Depth and quality of your experience matter more than years. Apply even if you've never carried the Design Engineer title.

EXTRA AWESOME

jobs.title: Group Product Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

THE PROBLEM YOU'LL SOLVE

Prosus is building an AI-first future across a global portfolio that spans food delivery, e-commerce, fintech, and education. We invest over $100 million annually in AI, run 800+ models in production, and have deployed Toqan — our internal platform for building, testing, and deploying GenAI and agentic workflows — across the organisation. The scale of ambition is real; the challenge now is focus, coherence, and velocity.

As Group Product Manager for our AI Platform, you will own the multi-year product strategy for the platform that underpins every AI initiative across Prosus. This means defining and sequencing the roadmap for agent infrastructure, evaluation frameworks, model deployment pipelines, and the shared capabilities that internal teams — from applied science to application engineering — rely on to build and ship AI products. You will balance long-term platform investments against the immediate, high-impact needs of teams across the portfolio who are racing to deliver.

You will lead and mentor a team of product managers, instilling product discipline and building the PM talent pipeline that scales with the platform. You will partner closely with engineering and applied science leadership to shape the technical strategy — making the hard trade-offs between model performance, latency, cost, and reliability that determine what we can promise the business.

And you will be the connective tissue: the person who turns ambiguous, fast-moving business needs into clear requirements, who aligns stakeholders across functions and geographies, and who ensures that what we build is not just technically impressive but adopted, trusted, and measurably impactful.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a senior product leader who has lived through the messy reality of building platform products for internal teams — and loved it. You measure your success not by features shipped but by the velocity and quality of the teams who build on top of your platform.

You are deeply technical. You can engage substantively with engineering and applied science teams on model lifecycle, MLOps, evaluation frameworks, and infrastructure trade-offs — not as a bystander, but as a thought partner. You understand agentic architectures, LLM capabilities and limitations, and the operational realities of running AI in production at scale.

You are a people leader. You have managed and mentored product managers, and you take genuine pride in their growth. You set strategic direction, coordinate overlapping roadmaps into a coherent plan, and create the clarity that lets your team operate with autonomy and purpose.

You thrive in ambiguity. You have worked in fast-paced, high-scale environments where priorities shift and the path forward is not always clear. You do not wait for perfect information — you run rapid experiments, test hypotheses, and let data and user feedback guide the next step.

You are a communicator. You can simplify complex technical concepts for executive leadership one hour and dig into detailed requirements with an engineering team the next. You build trust across functions and geographies, and you are as comfortable pushing back as you are building consensus.

You are customer-obsessed — even when your customers are internal teams. You connect frequently with the people who use your platform, validate solutions through product discovery, and treat adoption as a first-class metric.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years in product management, with at least 3–5 years in formal people-management roles leading a team of product managers.

 - Demonstrated success owning platform-level or infrastructure products used by internal teams — ideally including AI/ML platform capabilities, MLOps tooling, or developer-facing services.

 - Hands-on experience with generative AI, LLMs, and the model lifecycle (training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring) in production environments.

 - Track record of defining and executing multi-year product strategies in fast-moving, high-scale environments.

Technical Depth

 - Ability to engage substantively with engineering and applied science teams on architectural decisions, infrastructure trade-offs, and AI system design.

 - Familiarity with agentic workflows, agent frameworks, and the operational patterns that make AI agents reliable at scale.

 - Strong data-driven decision-making: comfortable with analytics tooling, A/B testing, defining and tracking KPIs, and using metrics to measure adoption, accuracy, latency, and ROI.

 - Experience with modern product and engineering tooling (e.g., Databricks, Jira, Confluence, Figma) and agile methodologies.

Leadership & Influence

 - Proven ability to mentor and grow product managers, instilling PM best practices and building talent pipelines.

 - Stakeholder management across functions and geographies

jobs.title: Product Expert
jobs.description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

THE ROLE:

A developer is getting ready to launch their first subscription app. A growth team wants to improve its paywalls. A founder has heard about Daily Payouts and wants to understand whether it could help. They all reach out to RevenueCat, and they all deserve a useful conversation. You’re that conversation.

As a Product Expert, your job is to understand what someone is trying to accomplish, explain and demo the relevant parts of RevenueCat, and help them take a sensible next step. Sometimes that means helping them get started themselves. Sometimes it means bringing in an Account Executive, a Sales Engineer, Support, or someone else.

This is a new role at the intersection of inbound sales, product education, and helping developers get started. You’ll own the inbound conversations that don’t go directly to our Account Executives or Sales Engineers, and help us build a great experience for the people behind them.

You might be early in your career, building apps on the side, or looking to turn your product knowledge into a more customer-facing job. You don’t need to have held this exact role before. You do need to know RevenueCat well, enjoy talking to people, and have good judgment about what would actually help them.

We’re initially hiring one person in EMEA and one in the Americas. You’ll initially report to our Sales Engineering lead and learn alongside teammates who have been handling these conversations for years. You’ll also help shape how the Product Expert team works as it grows.

What you’ll be responsible for:

 - Make a great first impression. Respond to inbound interest, run useful discovery conversations, and understand the app, the people building it, their goals, and what they need from us.

 - Turn product knowledge into practical guidance. Give clear demos, answer questions, and connect the relevant parts of RevenueCat to someone’s situation. Help them understand the product, its limits, and what getting started involves.

 - Help straightforward adoption move forward. Guide people through the next steps they can take themselves, share useful resources, and follow up so a good conversation turns into progress.

 - Recognize the right next step. Bring qualified commercial opportunities to an Account Executive and involve a Sales Engineer for deeper technical discovery, complex migrations, or solution design. Connect support questions and people who aren’t ready yet with the appropriate team or follow-up. Understand (and tell people) when RevenueCat is not right for them.

 - Make handoffs easy for the customer. Keep clear notes on goals, requirements, open questions, and next steps. Stay responsible for follow-through until the next owner has picked up the conversation, so the customer doesn’t have to start over.

 - Help us improve the experience. Share recurring questions and feedback with the team. Turn what you learn into better demos, resources, and playbooks, and help us see where conversations or handoffs get stuck.

jobs.title: Senior Applied Data Scientist
jobs.description:
A little bit about us:

We are Belvo, an open finance API platform with the bold vision of democratizing access to financial services in Latin America. We enable any financial innovator to access and interpret financial data, as well as initiate payments from their end-users accounts. We’re turning the messy complexities of the Latin American financial ecosystem into a modern set of tools to access and interpret data and move money in a seamless and secure way.

We’re a highly-technical, passionate, and driven team. We are more than 90 people and our team currently represents 20 nationalities. We have offices in São Paulo and Mexico City – while a large portion of us work remotely.

We are tackling a very stimulating problem: connecting fintech innovators with legacy financial infrastructure. We strive to go beyond the limits of what is possible today and to do so in an elegant and developer-first way.

Since starting our adventure in May 2019, we have raised $71m from the leading VC investors globally.

You can read more about our company here https://belvo.com/about/ and about our team and culture here https://belvo.com/careers/. Also, head to our blog https://belvo.com/blog/ for more news about what we’re building and how we work https://belvo.com/blog/category/working-belvo/.

About the team:

 - We work in cross-functional, autonomous teams. We follow continuous delivery best practices executed on top of a modern technology stack. 

 - Our products are built for developers, by developers. Technological excellence is at the heart of what we do. 

 - We are pragmatic and customer-focused. We strive to find the right set of trade-offs in order to validate our hypothesis as early as possible, iterating on our products based on customer feedback. 

 - We communicate transparently. We do weekly all-hands where we get together to discuss company performance and goals.

 - While we are global and remote-friendly, we also operate from our vibrant offices in CDMX and Sao Paulo. To accommodate the various time zones in which we are based, we ensure we’re always synced up for at least 3 hours per day.

 - Also, we are backed by some of the leading investors in Silicon Valley and Latin America, including Founders Fund, Kaszek Ventures, and YCombinator.
 
 
 

The challenge

The Intelligence Squad is Belvo's AI enabler team. One part of the squad builds the platforms and patterns that let every team at Belvo ship AI. This role sits in the other part: turning the financial data and payments we aggregate across Latin America into models that make real decisions, who looks creditworthy, which transaction is fraudulent, what category a payment belongs to, whether an income statement checks out. That data drives real financial outcomes for the people and businesses on the other end, so the bar for rigor is high.

You'll be the data science reference in the squad. We're not hiring someone to execute a modeling backlog someone else wrote. We want someone who decides which problems are worth modeling, defines how we know a model is good enough, and raises the data science bar for everyone they work with. You'll be deep enough in statistics and ML to defend a modeling choice to anyone, whether this is a set of rules to simplify a problem or a complex model that you build. You'll be close enough to the business to turn a commercial problem into a modeling roadmap and a business case. And you'll be a strong enough engineer to take your models from notebook to production and own them there.

Responsibilities

 - Model development and selection: Lead the design of statistical and ML models (classification, regression, ranking, NLP or LLM-based) for problems like risk scoring, fraud detection and transaction categorization. Choose approaches on their merits and defend those choices with data, not habit.

 - AI-leveraged delivery: Use agentic coding and research tooling as a core part of how you work: exploring data, generating and testing feature hypotheses, scaffolding pipelines, writing the service around the model. We care about the decisions you ship, not hours at the keyboard, and we expect you to keep compressing the gap between the two.

 - Feature engineering with business context: Work with Product and the business teams to figure out which signals in Belvo's financial data actually explain the outcome you're modeling, and translate an ambiguous business question into a well-scoped modeling problem.

 - Productionization and ownership: Take models past the notebook. Build or shape the pipelines, APIs and services that run them reliably in production, and own them once they're live: monitoring, drift, retraining, and retirement when the evidence says so.

 - Experimentation: Design and run experiments (A/B tests and offline evaluation) to confirm that a model change actually moves the metric it's meant to move.

 - Cross-functional partnership: Work closely with Engineering, Data Research, Product, and the rest of the Intelligence Squad to ship end to end, and with stakeholders across the business to keep your models grounded in what actually matters to them.

 - Business and customer partnership: Work directly with stakeholders and, when needed, customers. Translate ambiguous business questions into well-scoped problems, and explain trade-offs and impact clearly to non-technical audiences, executives included.

 - Staying current: GenAI moves weekly. We expect you to be genuinely plugged in: model releases, papers, and tooling, to hold an opinion on what's real versus hype, and to bring the useful parts back to the squad as a demo, a doc, or a session for our company-wide AI Chapter.

 - Framing the problem: Decide what's worth modeling. Push back when a rule, a heuristic, or a better data pipeline solves the problem without a model, and be willing to kill or retire your own model when the evidence says so.

jobs.title: Founding Growth Marketer
jobs.description:
ABOUT PLOY

Ploy is the marketing platform that turns a company’s website into its growth engine.

We help everyone from early-stage founders to growth agencies (Tonik, TNT Growth) and growth-stage marketing teams (Clay, Hex) run their digital marketing channels, managing everything from SEO/AEO, paid acquisition, conversion rate optimization, and ABM, with the flexibility to build custom marketing workflows around their own data, tools, and goals.

We’re building toward a future where Ploy can give marketing teams of any scale the leverage of a world-class marketer that’s proactive and always on. We’re backed by First Round Capital and Y Combinator, among other great investors and operators.

We work in person, with teams in San Francisco and New York. Two principles guide how we work: build momentum and build trust. We keep things simple and ship quickly, while taking seriously the responsibility of running a customer’s website and marketing.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our founding Growth Marketer will use Ploy to grow Ploy. You’ll become a true power user: building creative marketing workflows, connecting tools and data, and pushing the product to its limits. You’ll bring a practitioner’s perspective to our engineering, product, and design teams, helping shape new features and improve the workflows (Ploybooks) our customers rely on.

You’ll own the digital marketing channels that build awareness and bring in new customers. You’ll work closely with our founder and go-to-market team to run campaigns, improve acquisition, and grow both self-serve signups and qualified sales pipeline.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own acquisition across paid search, paid social, and SEO/AEO. Set channel goals, manage budgets, and grow qualified traffic, signups, and demo requests.

 - Run conversion experiments across ad creative, audiences, offers, and landing pages. Drive your workflow in Ploy: develop a clear hypothesis, launch the test, and use the results to improve campaign performance.

 - Build targeted email campaigns that help new users get started, convert free users to paying customers, and re-engage users who have gone quiet.

 - Track channel performance through to activation, paid conversion, and sales pipeline. Use acquisition costs and customer quality to decide where to increase investment, make changes, or stop spending.

 - Partner with engineering, product, and design on new capabilities. Test them in live campaigns and share specific feedback on what works and what needs refinement.

BACKGROUNDS WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of relevant experience in growth marketing, performance marketing, or demand generation, ideally at a startup.

 - A track record of measurable growth: increasing qualified signups or marketing-sourced pipeline, improving conversion rates, or lowering customer acquisition costs.

 - Deep experience in at least one digital acquisition channel, with hands-on ownership of campaigns, budgets, targeting, and optimization.

 - Hands-on experience building marketing automations and AI workflows. You can connect tools and data, orchestrate agents, and evaluate and improve the results.

 - Strong analytical skills. You can set up tracking, analyze funnels, and design experiments that produce useful answers.

LOCATION

San Francisco, CA (our office is in the Financial District). We work in-office a minimum of three days a week.

 Based in San Diego, California, Tempo develops thermochemical energy storage (TCES) systems designed for energy-intensive industries. The platform enables industrial operators to shift energy use over time by sourcing power when it is most cost-effective and enables the electrification of high-temperature industrial heat at a cost advantage to using fossil fuels. By storing electricity thermochemically, the system delivers a continuous stream of combustion-free, high-temperature air at up to 1,200°C. 
 Tempo is backed by leading climate and energy investors, including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Prelude Ventures. 
 For more information, visit www.tempoenergy.com . Job Description

 Working at Tempo

 Clear, direct communication: You professionally say what you mean, lead with empathy, use tact, ask when you're unsure, and keep the people around you informed without being asked. At a company our size, communication gaps are expensive, and good communicators add to success and efficiency!

jobs.title: FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Ambition has no passport. That belief is why LemFi https://lemfi.com/en-gb/careers exists. We're the financial engine for people the world wasn't built to serve, the millions who move countries to build something better and find the financial system hasn't caught up with them yet. We started with remittances: the money people send home to the people they love. Now we run multi-currency accounts, Savings, eSIMs and Credit. Because staying connected to home and building somewhere new are not two separate things. They never were.

ABOUT THE ROLE

LemFi is building the financial home for the world's immigrants - multi-currency accounts, remittances, savings, credit and eSIMs across 21 countries and growing. Strategic Finance sits at the centre of that growth: we hold the forecast, challenge the numbers and make sure leadership and investors see a clear, honest picture of the business.

This is the first hire into the FP&A function, reporting directly to the Head of Strategic Finance and FP&A. You will own the full engine: the integrated model, the monthly forecast and BvA cycle, the management pack, and investor and lender reporting. Your numbers go in front of the Board, our investors and our lenders. You will work hand-in-hand with department heads across Growth, Product, Operations and Risk, and have direct exposure to the executive team on commercial and strategic decisions.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD AND OWN

 - Run the monthly forecast and integrated three-statement model - cash runway, revenue, headcount and provider costs - keeping every model reconciled to actuals and documented to a standard anyone can follow.

 - Own the BvA cycle end to end: gather commentary, challenge variances, and hold budget owners accountable for their numbers every single month.

 - Produce the monthly management pack and KPI reporting for the executive team and Board, and prepare investor and lender reporting including covenant and facility tracking.

 - Partner with budget owners across Growth, Product, Operations and Risk on their plans, forecasts and spend - be the finance voice that pushes back with data, not just a service desk.

 - Build robust business cases for new products, corridors, markets and partnerships, including scenario and sensitivity analysis for leadership and the Board.

 - Support fundraising, M&A modelling and diligence as needed - your models will be in the data room.

 - Pull, structure and automate recurring data from NetSuite, the data warehouse and operational systems, using AI where it saves you time and improves accuracy.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

 - 3-5 years in FP&A, strategic finance, transaction services or a modelling-heavy consultancy role (Big 4, strategy or deals).

 - Excellent three-statement modelling skills: driver-based forecasting, scenario and sensitivity analysis, built cleanly and to best-practice standards.

 - Solid accounting foundations: you can link P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, and reconcile a forecast to the ledger without hand-holding.

 - Strong data skills and confidence with large datasets; comfortable pulling and structuring data independently.

 - Clear, direct communicator: you can explain the numbers to non-finance stakeholders and push back where the numbers do not support a decision.

 - High ownership and attention to detail - you do not wait to be asked and you do not let things fall through the cracks in a fast-moving environment.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Capital markets exposure: equity fundraising, debt facilities, investor reporting or M&A diligence.

 - Experience in payments, remittance, lending or another regulated financial services business.

 - NetSuite, BI tools, SQL or automation experience (Python or similar); professional qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or CFA).

WHY JOIN LEMFI?

Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down.

Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours.

Follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/lemfi/ and Instagram https://www.instagram.com/uselemfi/ and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/lemfi/id1533066809 or Google Play https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en&id=com.lemonadeFinance.android. 

Don't feel that you're right for this role, but want to submit your interest in working for LemFi? You can join our talent community https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/lemfi/form/talent-community to stay in touch for future opportunities.

LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee.

jobs.title: Creative Video Producer / Motion Designer
jobs.description:
About Hyperbound

Sales is messy. Closing deals is hard. Multiple stakeholders, hours of calls, and endless emails. At Hyperbound, we're building the AI Agent that will help sales teams untangle that mess.

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform: an agentic OS for sales that connects what happens to what should happen next.

We came out of YC S23 and went viral with Voice Agents that reps could call to put their skills to the test. Today, we’re building AI that understands sales conversations, coaches in real time, reasons across deals, and takes action to move them forward.

We are trusted by companies like LinkedIn, Amazon, Intel, Notion, and Vanta. We raised a $15M Series A in October 2025, grew ARR 5× over the past year, and are growing nearly 20% month over month.

The team you'll build with

We’re assembling a cracked team of builders and operators. You’ll be working alongside former founders, early customers that loved the product so much they decided to join, and folks that worked for our competition before joining us. We like hard problems, strong opinions, and getting something into customers’ hands while the idea is still fresh.

We work with high trust and real autonomy. 

You’ll have the context to make decisions, the freedom to choose your approach. We trust you to spot problems, challenge assumptions, and move things forward without waiting for step-by-step direction.

We have each other’s backs. When something goes wrong, we focus on fixing it and learning, not pointing fingers. You’ll have teammates who share what they know, tell you what they think, and jump in to help. We move quickly because we trust each other, give direct feedback, and make decisions together.

We’re optimistic enough to take ambitious swings and willing to change our minds when the evidence comes back. We ship quickly, learn from customers, and keep improving.

About the role

We're hiring our first dedicated Creative Video Producer and Motion Designer to bring Hyperbound's products, customers, and stories to life through video. You'll own the creative process from concept to final cut, working closely with Marketing, Product, Sales, and Leadership to create videos that make complex technology easy to understand and hard to ignore. This is a hands-on opportunity to build our video production capability from the ground up, with flexibility for a part-time or full-time arrangement.

What we need from you

 - Storytelling instinct: You know how to turn a complex product, customer conversation, or rough idea into a compelling story. You have a strong creative point of view and a portfolio that shows you can make videos people actually want to watch.

 - End-to-end production skills: You're comfortable owning the entire process, from creative concepts, scripts, and storyboards to filming, editing, sound, color, and motion graphics. You're proficient with tools like Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or and modern AI tooling

 - Technical craft: You know your way around cameras, lighting, audio, and on-location production. You can direct interviews, make people comfortable on camera, and capture high-quality footage.

 - Motion and design craft: You can animate product UI, build titles, lower thirds, end cards, and explainer graphics, and design static assets (thumbnails, ad variants, social graphics) that match our brand. You’re comfortable in After Effects and Figma or Adobe Creative Suite.

 - Ownership and resourcefulness: You can take a brief and run with it, manage multiple projects, and deliver polished work without someone managing every step. You know when to do things yourself and when to bring in outside help.

 - Creative collaboration: You can work with marketers, founders, and product teams to turn feedback into better work without losing the creative vision. You communicate clearly, move quickly, and care about getting the details right.

Highly preferred

 - Experience producing video content for B2B SaaS, technology companies, or startups, particularly product demos, customer stories, founder content, and marketing campaigns.

 - Experience animating SaaS product interfaces or building reusable motion templates and brand systems.

 - Experience building video production workflows from scratch and managing freelance creatives, agencies, or production partners.

What your regular Thursday looks like:

 - You're on set filming a customer interview or working with our founders to capture a story worth sharing. You're directing the conversation, managing the equipment, and making sure you get the shots you need.

 - You’re creating short & long form content for LinkedIn, X, YouTube (ads), and Meta (ads) that people actually want to watch and share.

 - You're turning raw footage into a sharp, engaging video for an upcoming product launch. 

 - You're collaborating with Marketing and Product on the next campaign, turning a rough brief into a creative concept, storyboard, and production plan.

 - You're delivering final edits and shorter cuts for social, web, and sales, incorporating feedback and making sure everything is polished, accurate, and ready to ship.

What this role is not

 - A role where you just execute someone else's vision. We want someone who brings creative ideas, challenges briefs, and helps shape how Hyperbound tells its stories.

 - A role where you only do one part of production. You'll be hands-on from planning and filming through editing and delivery, especially as our first dedicated video hire.

 - A role with a big production team behind you. You'll be building the function from scratch, figuring out how to create great work efficiently and bringing in external partners when it makes sense.

Interview Plan

 - Portfolio review

 - Intro call with James, Founding Recruiter (30 min)

 - Conversation with Garrett, Marketing Lead (45 min)

 - Final onsite with marketing team and Co Founders (90 min)

We move fast, from first conversation to decision in 1-2 weeks.

jobs.title: Offensive Security RL Researcher
jobs.description:
ABOUT IDLER

idler is a frontier data research lab. We build the evals and environments that the world's leading frontier labs use to measure and train their models.

After raising a $9m seed round led by Paradigm, we spent the last year developing coding evals for top coding models you know and love. At the same time, we've expanded into other domains besides coding: RSI & Auto-Research, Law, Enterprise Business, Cybersecurity, and others. Now, we are facing more lab demand for our data than we can serve, and are rapidly scaling the team to grow the business.

Our approach to creating training data scales using technology, and all of our data products are built on a unified self-reinforcing platform that learns through experience.

You would be joining a close-knit team that has reached product market fit, and your work would directly help to multiply our revenue.

You can see some of our work here: https://idler.ai/collections

About the role

idler is looking for an elite security researcher who can also build. You'll lead idler's cybersecurity work: deciding which environments we build, building and running the systems that produce them, recruiting and managing the part-time experts who review them, and working directly with researchers at frontier AI labs to understand what they need and sell them what we build.

You're a security researcher first. We need someone whose judgment about what counts as a real vulnerability, what makes a task fair, and where the field's genuine skill hierarchy actually sits, we can trust without double-checking. Software development is the tool you use to put that judgment into a production pipeline — it's not a second, parallel discipline we're hiring for separately.

One note on scope: if idler stops investing in cybersecurity, you'd move to a different project inside the company rather than leave — we want to say that plainly now rather than have it be a surprise later.

What you'll do

 - Drive the roadmap for idler's cybersecurity evals and environments, and decide — using our cybersecurity capability map — which environments we build next and where we put engineering resources.

 - Build and run the systems that produce those environments yourself; you'll write production code where it matters, not just spec it out for someone else to build.

 - Recruit, onboard, and manage the part-time cybersecurity experts who review our environments for fairness, correctness, and quality.

 - Work directly with researchers at frontier AI labs to understand what cybersecurity capabilities and data they want, and sell them the environments that meet it.

Requirements

 - 3+ years of experience in a professional cybersecurity role, with a track record that puts you in the top 5% of your peers by reputation.

 - Deep hands-on experience in at least one of: web app pentesting, bug bounty hunting, vulnerability/zero-day research, hacking agents, or AI security.

 - Well-connected within the security community — this makes recruiting and evaluating the part-time experts you'll manage far easier.

 - Comfortable writing and shipping production code (Python, TypeScript, or similar). You don't need a decade of software engineering experience, but you need to build and maintain the systems your research depends on, not hand that off entirely.

 - Strong written communication — you'll justify prioritization calls to researchers and explain findings to people who didn't do the work themselves.

You might excel if you…

 - Have a public bug bounty track record, live-hacking-event invitations, Pwn2Own placements, or published original research — send us a writeup of some of the best bugs you've ever found.

 - Have managed or mentored other security researchers or hackers before.

 - Have thought seriously about how to measure or grade security work that isn't simply pass/fail.

 - Have built tools or automation to support your own research, even if you wouldn't call yourself a software engineer.

Details

 - In-person in San Francisco

 - $200K–$500K base salary + meaningful equity.

 - We'd sponsor and co-publish AI security research under your name.

 - Healthcare, 401(k), 15 days of PTO per year.

 - Relocation assistance

 - Small, ambitious team.

We're a tight-knit founding team and we play to win. Join us if you like to win too.

You will be responsible for corporate FP&A functions, including 3 financial statement forecasting and consolidations, business partnering, and GTM optimizations. YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

HOW WE’RE DIFFERENT

We prioritize mission over ego and collaborate openly with a strong sense of shared purpose. We dream big, yet we execute with a love of detail. We’re looking for scientists, engineers, and operators to forge new paths with us at the intersection of quantum and AI.

CULTURE & BENEFITS

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, Ledger
jobs.description:
New York (SoHo) · Hybrid, 3 days/week onsite · Full-time

ABOUT FORMANCE

Formance builds open-source financial infrastructure. Our core product is a programmable double-entry ledger. Fintechs, crypto platforms, and financial institutions use it as the source of truth for their balances: every movement of money is recorded as a transaction between accounts, and every balance can be traced back to the postings that produced it.

Around the ledger, we connect to banks and payment providers and reconcile what the ledger records against what actually moved.

We are a team of 30+ people, mostly engineers, working across New York and Paris. Our systems support real money movement, so correctness is not optional.

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

Our customers are engineering teams building financial products. They come to us with questions like “how do we track user wallets, pending funds, and fees so that every cent is accounted for?” or “what happens to our balances when a payment fails halfway through?”

You help them answer those questions, from the first technical conversation through proof of concept and into a successful transition to implementation.

 - Design money flows. Turn a customer's product into a ledger model: which accounts exist, how funds move between them, and how balances are queried. Typical use cases include user wallets, pending vs. settled funds, fees and revenue sharing, refunds and chargebacks, and multi-currency.

 - Lead the technical sale. Partner closely with our NYC sales team to run technical discovery and architecture sessions with CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and Heads of Payments. Build proofs of concept around real customer use cases and explain architectural trade-offs clearly, including what the ledger guarantees and what remains the customer's responsibility.

 - Build trust with technical buyers. Challenge assumptions, answer complex engineering questions, and help prospective customers evaluate how Formance fits into their existing infrastructure. You are comfortable engaging directly with senior technical decision-makers.

 - Support the transition to production. Work with our implementation team to ensure a smooth handover, sharing technical context, architectural decisions, and customer requirements. Stay involved when your expertise is needed to resolve complex technical questions.

 - Bring the field back to the product. Turn recurring customer patterns into reference models, examples, and documentation, and share structured feedback with our engineering team in Paris.

 - Support customers beyond the initial sale, helping with technical onboarding, implementation, and a smooth transition to ongoing customer support.

You will join a small Solutions Engineering team and work closely with our founders, NYC sales team, and engineers.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions engineering, or technical implementation, ideally within payments, banking, fintech infrastructure, or digital assets.

 - A strong understanding of how money is tracked in software. You know what double-entry means in practice, or you have worked on systems where balances, transactions, and reconciliation matter.

 - Familiarity with real payment flows, including settlement delays, returns, partial failures, and mismatches between internal records and external providers.

 - Hands-on technical experience with APIs, databases, and at least one programming language.

 - Confidence working with technical buyers. You are comfortable leading technical conversations with engineering leaders, challenging architectural assumptions, and building credibility with highly technical stakeholders.

 - The ability to explain complex systems clearly to engineering, finance, and product stakeholders, and an interest in working directly with customers.

 - An independent approach to problem-solving. You learn unfamiliar systems quickly and use modern development tools, including AI, where they improve your work.

STRONG SIGNALS

 - You have built or maintained a ledger, wallet system, or reconciliation process.

 - You have worked with a banking-as-a-service provider, card issuer, or core banking system.

 - You have supported technical evaluations, proofs of concept, or architecture discussions with prospective customers.

 - You have moved from a software engineering role into a customer-facing technical position.

HOW WE INTERVIEW

Part of the process is a working session in which you walk us through how you would track money for a simple product, such as a marketplace with fees, refunds, and delayed payouts.

We look at how you reason about accounts, edge cases, and architectural decisions, as well as how clearly you communicate your approach.

No prior knowledge of Formance is expected.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - $165–175k OTE 

 - Equity

 - 401(k) with 4% employer match

 - Health insurance (medical, dental, vision)

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Annual team offsite in Europe

Our AI agents can execute complex workflows across any application, browser, desktop, or legacy system—free from the limitations and fragility of traditional automation tools. jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.description:
ABOUT SOLIDROAD

Building something great is addictive. It's like discovering your favorite TV show mid-season, except you're helping write the next episode. It's like unboxing a new gadget, except you're the one designing it. You shape how it feels, how it works, and how people react when they use it.

At Solidroad we're solving a big, messy, exciting problem: how do you scale customer support without losing what makes humans amazing? Warmth, empathy, intuition. We're using AI, generative tech, and real-time simulations to make this happen. It's ambitious, difficult, and genuinely new.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for BDRs who want to do more than just hit quota — someone who wants to shape the way we sell and grow the company from the ground up. You'll be one of the first hires on our sales team and will work directly with the founders. Your day-to-day will revolve around personalized email outreach, LinkedIn social selling, and cold calling to book meetings with CX and support leaders at fast-growing companies.

This is a role for someone who loves the thrill of getting a response from that cold prospect, who geeks out on subject lines, and who sees rejection as part of the game. If you want to break into SaaS sales, make a name for yourself, and grow into an AE or manager role fast — this is the place.

 

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO DAY-TO-DAY

 - Drive top-of-funnel activity: personalized email outreach, LinkedIn messaging, and cold calls.

 - Book qualified meetings with CX leaders — think Heads of Support, VP of Ops, Directors of Enablement.

 - Collaborate with the sales and marketing teams on outbound campaigns and messaging experiments.

 - Keep HubSpot updated and clean — pipeline discipline matters.

 - Work closely with the founders to refine our ICP and sales process.

 - Learn what it takes to take a startup from $1M to $10M ARR.

OUR TEAM & CULTURE

We're a small, focused group working full-time in our Dublin & San Francisco offices. We're here five days a week because building something ambitious means collaborating closely, solving problems together, sharing ideas spontaneously, and occasionally challenging each other to padel matches, cold plunges, or karaoke evenings. We're intentional about creating a culture that's mature, supportive, and fun. You'll be joining experienced founders who've done this before, alongside a tight-knit team genuinely excited about building something impactful.

 

WE HOPE YOU

 - Are confident picking up the phone and cold calling strangers.

 - Write tight, clear, and compelling emails.

 - Love experimenting with messaging and learning what works.

 - Are ambitious and want to grow into a closing role fast.

 - Want to work in-person with a close-knit, fast-paced team in San Francisco.

 - No prior sales experience needed - once you have grit.

THE GOOD, THE BAD, AND THE HONEST TRUTH

The highs are real: you'll close deals that move the needle, learn directly from experienced founders, and help build the next category-defining company. The lows? You'll need to hunt for deals, get creative to break into accounts, and wear a lot of hats while we figure things out together. This isn't a place to coast — it's a place to grow fast, fail fast, and get better every day.

If that sounds exciting, don't overthink it. Reach out. Send us a note about who you are, what you've sold, and why you think you could win here. Curiosity, hustle, and coachability matter more to us than a perfect CV.

jobs.title: T&S Investigator
jobs.description:

This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

This role is open to nurses!

This role focuses on two core outcomes: providing an exceptional, empathetic experience for customers during high-stakes situations, and decisively removing bad actors when appropriate to keep our platform safe.

 - Develop and implement safety initiatives, tools, and processes that reduce incidents and strengthen platform integrity.

 - Assess safety and compliance risks; design strategies to close gaps and prevent recurrence.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Ability to resolve customer incidents with empathy and action

 - Possess an “I can handle anything” mentality and extremely sound judgement in ambiguous situations

 - Opportunity to make a significant impact with our customers on both sides of the marketplace.
 
 

HIRING PROCESS

 7. Offer!

Quick Note on Scammers: 

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6.

jobs.title: Developer Success Engineer
jobs.description:
Location: San Francisco / Remote Okay

AgentMail gives AI agents their own email inboxes. We’re looking for a Developer Success Engineer to own the front line between developers using AgentMail and the team building it.

This isn’t a role where success means closing as many tickets as possible. We want someone who can solve technical problems independently, understand what a developer is actually trying to do, and recognize when the same problem keeps showing up.

Your job is to answer the question, figure out why it had to be asked, and make sure we learn from it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own technical support for developers building with AgentMail.

 - Debug API requests, webhooks, product issues, and integrations.

 - Reproduce issues and determine whether something is expected behavior, developer error, a documentation gap, or a product bug.

 - Resolve the large majority of issues independently without needing to pull in another engineer.

 - When something is broken, isolate the problem and give engineering a high-quality reproduction - or open a PR and fix it yourself.

 - Notice recurring questions and friction across support conversations and surface those patterns to the team.

 - Identify inconsistencies and confusing behavior across our API, documentation, and developer experience.

 - Jump on calls with developers when async debugging isn’t enough.

 - Write concise, technically precise responses that make developers feel like they’re talking to someone who actually understands their problem.

YOU WILL BE A FIT IF

 - You have 2-6 years of experience in technical support, developer experience, solutions engineering, or engineering, ideally working with a developer-facing or API-first product.

 - You’re comfortable reading API documentation, inspecting requests and responses, working with logs, and reproducing technical issues.

 - You can distinguish between a bug, expected behavior, and incorrect API usage without immediately escalating to engineering.

 - You can write code to investigate issues and ship small fixes.

 - You’re an unusually clear and concise communicator.

 - You’re resourceful. When you don’t know the answer, your instinct is to investigate rather than hand the problem to someone else.

 - You have strong interpersonal instincts and genuinely care about understanding why a customer is frustrated or confused.

 - You notice patterns. Answering the same question for the fifth time makes you want to fix the underlying problem.

WHAT THIS ROLE ISN’T

This isn’t traditional customer success or account management. You won’t spend your day running check-in calls or forwarding technical questions to engineers.

You’ll be expected to understand the product deeply enough to investigate most problems yourself - and to turn what you learn from customers into signal for the people building AgentMail.

jobs.title: Strategic GTM, Manager
jobs.description:
STRATEGIC GTM, MANAGER

New York City · On-site

THE VOICE AI WORKFORCE FOR HEALTHCARE

Healthcare runs on phone calls and loses $450B a year to the administration around them. Patients wait on hold, staff spend hours calling insurers, and revenue leaks at every handoff.

 

At Prosper, we're building the AI workforce that runs healthcare operations end to end. Our voice AI agents answer patient calls, schedule appointments directly in the EHR, verify insurance benefits, automate billing, and get payors on the phone when humans would otherwise wait on hold. We've grown revenue 5x in the last year, partnered with 100+ healthcare organizations covering more than 150,000 providers, and raised $35M, including a $30M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a Strategic GTM, Manager to own a segment of the largest provider organizations in the country: national MSOs, PE-backed platform groups, and multi-region specialty organizations.

 

Think of it as running a business rather than working a patch. You'll own the segment the way a GM would. You decide how it's defined, which organizations belong in it, what the thesis is for winning each one, and what Prosper has to build, say, and do to get there. Then you go make it happen: a named account list you built yourself, run from first touch to signature, with marketing, product, solutions, and the founders working against the plan you set.

 

Prosper is at an inflection point. Revenue is up 5x on a lean sales team. It's early enough that the strategy is yours to write, and consequential enough that writing it well changes the trajectory of the company.

 

If you've spent years building strategy for other people's businesses, this is the version where you own the thesis, run the execution, and see the number move. This is the best opportunity for someone who wants a path to be a founder or learn the entrepreneurial joruney

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own a segment of the market

 

 - Build the strategy from a blank page: market map, account segmentation, prioritization logic, and a defensible point of view on where Prosper wins and why

 - Construct the named account list, a finite and deliberately chosen set of organizations, along with the entry hypothesis for each one

 - Set the commercial architecture for the segment: pricing posture, pilot design, and land-and-expand paths from a single site or specialty to the full organization

 - Bring the rest of GTM with you. Marketing, outbound, solutions, and product should be executing against your plan, not adjacent to it. You'll define the campaigns, content, and product priorities the segment needs and drive them cross-functionally

 

Run the outcome of the deals

 

 - Own long-cycle, multi-stakeholder deals end to end: account planning, prospecting, discovery, pilot, negotiation, and close

 - Build durable relationships with the people who decide. The best strategic sellers are trusted before they're needed. You'll invest in multi-year relationships with CFOs, COOs, CIOs, and VPs of Revenue Cycle, arriving with a point of view on their business rather than a pitch

 - Multi-thread across revenue cycle, finance, IT, security, compliance, clinical operations, and procurement, and hold every thread yourself

 - Author the ROI case. Every strategic deal at Prosper is won on a quantified business case: cost-to-collect, denial rate, days in A/R, FTE hours redeployed, cash recovered. You'll build these models from the customer's own data and defend them in front of a CFO

 - Navigate the enterprise gauntlet of RFPs, security reviews, HIPAA and BAA diligence, legal negotiation, and phased multi-site rollouts without losing momentum

 

Build the playbook

 

 - Codify what works into an outreach strategy, business-case templates, and qualification criteria the next five hires on this team will run

 - Feed the top of the market back into roadmap, and turn roadmap into commercial advantage

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MBB or top-tier strategy consulting experience (McKinsey, Bain, BCG) is strongly preferred, specifically, 2-6 years of experience. You've demonstrated you can take an unstructured market, break it into a defensible framework, and turn that into a prioritized plan to execute, and iterate on

 - Relationship-building as a core competency. You build trust with senior operators over years, and people who've worked with you once seek you out again. You can win a room of C-suite executives and excel at building trust and product knowledge

 - Entrepreneurial eagerness. You're eager to build, comfortable getting in the mud, and just as comfortable stepping back to decide what actually deserves your time. If you want to find the ceiling of what you're capable of, or build a billion dollar company of your own one day, this is where you learn how
 
 

BONUS POINTS

 - Healthcare or PE/provider-services practice experience in consulting

 - Experience selling AI, automation, or voice technology into regulated industries

 - Fluency with EHR and practice management ecosystems (Epic, athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks) and clearinghouse/RCM stacks

 - An existing network across provider group leadership or PE-backed provider platforms

 - Early-stage or hypergrowth startup background

WHY PROSPER

 - A trillion-dollar problem, real customers, and revenue growing 5x

 - A segment you own outright: the strategy, the accounts, and the number

 - Direct access to founders, product, and engineering. Deals get unblocked in hours

 - Competitive base, commission, and meaningful equity

jobs.title: Part-time BDR
jobs.description:
About Proof of Human
Proof of Human is building the global standard for human verification across the internet. As the line between human and machine behavior becomes harder to discern, establishing who or what is behind every interaction is becoming foundational to the integrity of a digital world. Founded by Princeton PhD Scientists, Mayank Agrawal and Matt Hardy, Proof of Human is a research and technology company developing the science, products, and infrastructure required to meet this challenge at global scale.

About the role

We’re looking for a part-time Business Development Representative (BDR) who loves selling and wants a flexible work role. You’ll work directly with the founders and staff to win new customers for Proof of Human, owning the sales process from finding prospects and starting conversations to negotiating and closing deals.

With a flexible 20-hour workweek and uncapped commission, this role offers the opportunity to build something yourself and grow our business. You’ll have agency to develop your own approach, build repeatable sales systems, and use automation to keep your pipeline moving so each hour becomes more productive. We’re looking for someone who gets a thrill from closing a deal, takes ownership of their results, and sees the opportunity to help shape Proof of Human’s growth.

What you’ll do:

 - New Business Generation: Find and pursue customers who have a real need for Proof of Human. Build prospect lists, pick up the phone, run outbound campaigns, and use your network to create opportunities. Take responsibility for keeping your pipeline full.

 - Customer Conversations: Lead discovery calls and demos that move prospects toward a purchase. Understand what matters to the buyer, make a compelling case for Proof of Human, handle objections, and ask for the business.

 - Deal Execution: Own the sale from first contact to signed agreement. Navigate decision-makers, negotiate commercial terms, follow up with purpose, and work through the obstacles that stand between interest and commitment. Bring in the founders and technical team when their involvement helps you close.

 - Sales Systems & Automation: Build a sales operation that makes every hour more productive. Use prospecting tools, automated outreach sequences, CRM workflows, and follow-up systems to consistently generate opportunities and give yourself more time to sell.

 - Pipeline & Revenue Ownership: Know where every deal stands, what it could be worth, and what needs to happen to win it. Prioritize the opportunities most likely to convert, reengage stalled conversations, and hold yourself accountable for bringing in revenue.

You’ll be a good fit if:

 - You love the sale. You enjoy opening doors, earning someone’s trust, and getting a deal across the finish line. Winning business is satisfying to you, and you’re motivated by the financial rewards that come with doing it well.

 - You create your own momentum. You can find a starting point, take initiative, and keep moving without someone directing every step. You’re resourceful when an approach stalls and persistent about finding one that works.

 - You’re curious and persuasive. You ask good questions, listen closely, and understand what matters to the person across from you. You can explain an unfamiliar product clearly and connect its value to a customer’s specific needs.

 - You make every hour count. You’re organized about your pipeline, disciplined about follow-up, and thoughtful about where you spend your time. You look for ways to improve your results and build systems that make you more effective.

jobs.title: Talent & People Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT DILIGENCESQUARED

DiligenceSquared is the AI-native consulting firm. We deliver investment-grade market research and commercial due diligence, powered by AI agents and led by experienced consultants. Our founding team brings deep experience from Blackstone and BCG, and we're backed by Y Combinator and Relentless. Our clients include 6 of the 10 largest private equity firms in the world and represent more than $4T in combined AUM.

 

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Talent & People Lead to help us hire exceptional people and build the foundations of our people function. You'll work directly with the founders to identify the talent we need, bring great candidates into the business and create an excellent experience from first conversation through onboarding and beyond.

Recruiting will be your primary focus. You'll personally source candidates, run hiring processes and help close hires across consulting, GTM, engineering and operations. Alongside that, you'll own the day-to-day people processes that help a growing team work well together.

This is a hands-on builder role with broad ownership. You'll need to be equally comfortable persuading a strong candidate to take a first meeting, helping a founder make a hiring decision and making sure a new teammate has everything they need on day one.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own recruiting from start to finish: Partner with founders and hiring managers to define roles, source candidates, run interviews, coordinate feedback and move offers through to acceptance.

 - Find exceptional people: Build targeted candidate pipelines through thoughtful outreach, referrals and relationships. Develop a clear view of where to find strong talent for each function.

 - Make hiring more effective: Create clear role scorecards, practical assessments and consistent interview processes that help us make better decisions quickly.

 - Deliver a strong candidate experience: Keep candidates informed, prepare interviewers and ensure every interaction reflects the quality and ambition of the business.

 - Help close hires: Understand what matters to candidates, communicate the opportunity clearly and partner with founders on offers and negotiations.

 - Build excellent onboarding: Coordinate everything from signed offer to first weeks on the team, with clear ownership, thoughtful preparation and regular check-ins.

 - Own people operations: Manage day-to-day people administration in Rippling, including employee records, payroll, benefits, onboarding and offboarding, with support from Rippling's team and our external advisers. Keep our handbook and policies current and make sure employee questions and administrative tasks are resolved promptly.

 - Coordinate work authorization and immigration: Work with employees and external counsel to coordinate documentation, visa-related processes and important deadlines.

 - Support performance and development: Partner with founders and managers to run practical performance reviews, support regular feedback and turn development priorities into clear actions.

 

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Relevant experience: You have at least five years of recruiting experience, with a strong track record of personally sourcing, assessing and closing exceptional candidates. You have owned searches from start to finish and are excited to remain hands-on as we grow.

 - A strong recruiting track record: You can point to difficult hires you personally delivered, including candidates who were not actively looking. You know how to build a targeted pipeline, earn candidates' trust and close competitive offers.

 - Hands-on execution: You enjoy doing the work yourself and can manage several searches without losing momentum or attention to detail.

 - Good judgment about people: You ask thoughtful questions, assess evidence carefully and help hiring managers distinguish an impressive background from a strong fit for the role.

 - Excellent communication: You write compelling outreach, build trust with candidates and represent DiligenceSquared credibly.

 - Operational discipline: You are organized, responsive and reliable with the details that make recruiting and people processes work.

 - Discretion and maturity: You handle sensitive information carefully and know when an issue requires specialist advice.

 - High initiative: You identify what needs to happen, propose a practical approach and take ownership of following through.

 - Fluency with AI tools: You use AI to improve research, preparation and administration while applying your own judgment to decisions about people.

 

EXPERIENCE THAT WOULD BE A PLUS

 - Recruiting at an early-stage or rapidly growing company

 - Hiring across consulting, commercial and technical roles

 - Experience building a recruiting or people function from the ground up

 - Practical ownership of onboarding, benefits administration or other HR processes

 - Familiarity with Ashby, Rippling or similar systems

 

WHY DILIGENCESQUARED

 - Build the talent and people function at a YC-backed company with real revenue and strong client traction

 - Work directly with founders who bought this research at Blackstone and delivered it at BCG

 - Have a direct impact on the quality of the team and the company's ability to grow

 - Grow your responsibilities as the business and people function develop

 - Join a small, senior team that enjoys working together, with regular offsites, team dinners and meals together at the office

 - High ownership, close founder access and very little bureaucracy

Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Job Title: Senior Optomechanical Engineer

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

 - We are hiring a Senior Optomechanical Engineer to own the optics-related subsystems on our robotic weapon platforms: the cameras, thermal imagers, rangefinders, and sensor heads that let our systems find and engage small drones, and the windows, housings, and mounts that keep them working. This role exists because our optics have to hold alignment and image quality on a machine that fires shotguns, slews hard, and lives outdoors in Texas heat, dust, and rain.

 - This is not an optical design role. Our lens trains are designed by others, inside and outside the company. Your job is everything that happens to those optics once they leave the designer: how they are held, aligned, sealed, kept clean and dry, protected from shock and vibration, and made to perform the same at 0 °F as they do at 140 °F. You are the person who makes sure we get every bit of performance the optical designer put on paper, and you are the person who tells the designer early when a prescription will not survive the mount it needs.

 - The person we want thinks in degrees of freedom. You know where an optic is constrained and where it is free to move, how much it will move with temperature and load, and what that does to focus, boresight, and MTF. You have strong opinions on bonded versus clamped versus flexure mounts, and the experience to back them. You know what Invar, titanium, and stainless buy you over aluminum, and you know when aluminum is the right answer because the error budget allows it and the price does not.

 - This is a hands-on role. You will build and align your own assemblies, put them on the shaker and in the thermal chamber, take them to the range, and measure what moved.
 
 

Essential Duties

 - Own the optical subsystems. Be the responsible engineer for every sensor head, camera module, and optical window on the platform, from concept and requirements through production and field support. Own the optomechanical error budget and the drawings, ICDs, and test procedures that go with it.

 - Mount optics properly. Design kinematic, semi-kinematic, flexure, bonded, and retained mounts for lenses, windows, mirrors, filters, and focal plane assemblies. Control preload, bond line thickness, and stress birefringence. Make mounts that can be aligned once and stay aligned.

 - Choose materials on purpose. Select housing, cell, spacer, and fastener materials to balance CTE match, stiffness, mass, machinability, corrosion, and cost. Run the athermalization math for focus and boresight, and make the cost-versus-stability call with numbers behind it.

 - Manage shock and vibration. Design for weapon recoil, gunfire shock, and gimbal slew loads. Drive structural modes away from excitation, specify or design isolation where it helps, and keep line-of-sight jitter and boresight shift within budget. Run modal and structural FEA and correlate it to test.

 - Keep it clean and dry. Design sealed, purged, and desiccated housings that keep moisture, dust, and contaminants off the glass for years in the field. Specify seals, breathers, purge and fill procedures, window coatings, and anti-fog and window-clearing approaches. Set up the clean assembly practices and handling procedures our technicians will follow.

 - Align and boresight. Develop alignment and co-boresighting methods and fixtures for multiple sensors on a common mount and to the weapon. Make alignment repeatable on a production floor, not just on your bench.

 - Work with the optical designers. Turn lens prescriptions into buildable assemblies. Feed tolerance sensitivities and mechanical constraints back early. Support integrated structural-thermal-optical (STOP) analysis where it earns its keep.

 - Test and prove it. Plan and run thermal cycling, vibration, shock, humidity, and water-ingress testing on optical assemblies. Measure what moved, in focus, boresight, and image quality, and close the loop into the next revision.

 - Make it manufacturable. Work with our machine shop and suppliers on tolerances, surface finishes, and process capability. Qualify optics, coating, and window vendors. Write the assembly and inspection procedures that get us repeatable units.

 - Support the field. Go to the range. Watch the sensors under fire. Bring back what you learn.

Requirements

 - 10+ years of optomechanical engineering experience, with optical assemblies you designed that shipped and held up in the field, ideally in harsh environments.

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in kinematic and exact-constraint mounting. You can explain where every degree of freedom in your mounts goes, and you have designed flexures, three-point and semi-kinematic mounts, bonded cells, and retaining-ring mounts. We will ask you to walk us through mounts you designed and what went wrong with them.
