jobs.title: Account Executive, Service
jobs.description:
ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE, SERVICE

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

Role in one line: Turn the gap between what a customer bought and what they now need into a clear recommendation and a closed change.

The policy is sold. Then the customer comes back with a certificate of insurance request, or a contract whose insurance requirements look very different from what was originally discussed. That moment is not a service ticket. It is a second commercial conversation, and you own it.

Harper's systems keep the account history, the bound policy, and the new request together. You read the documents, find the gap, lead the customer conversation, and close the right coverage.

WHY NOW

Harper's growing policy book creates a commercial moment after the sale. Customers return mid-term with certificate requests and contract requirements that do not match the coverage they bought. That gap needs a dedicated sales motion, not a service queue.

Harper has four Account Executive lanes: New Business, Renewals, Partnerships, and Service. Service is not renewals, and it is not the recovery work inside New Business. It is a smaller team than the other lanes and more brokerage-heavy. You read policies, certificates, and contract insurance requirements, then own the customer decision.

WHAT YOU OWN

 - Pick up the account after the sale. Take the customer who comes back with a certificate of insurance request or requirements that differ from what was originally discussed.

 - Read the source documents. Compare the bound policy, the certificate request, and the contract insurance requirements line by line.

 - Name the gap. Identify exactly what the requirement asks for that the current coverage does not provide.

 - Build the coverage plan. Decide with placement and insurance experts how to close the gap credibly.

 - Lead the customer conversation. Explain the requirement, the current coverage, the options, the price, and the deadline in plain language.

 - Close the change. Ask for the business, collect the required decision and completion items, and keep ownership through bind.

 - Protect accuracy. Work within your license and authority. Never let a certificate or a promise overstate what the policy covers.

 - Record the outcome. Capture what the customer needed, why the gap appeared, and whether they bought, waited, or left.

 

THE SERVICE OUTCOMES YOU OWN

 - Accounts that come back with a certificate request or new requirement have a verified comparison against the bound policy and a next customer action.

 - Recommendations make the current coverage, the requirement, the gap, the option, and the deadline clear.

 - Bound changes move forward with the accepted option and completion steps recorded.

 - Accounts that do not buy preserve the customer's stated reason, or an honest unknown when the reason is not available.

 - Mid-term conversion, retention, and booked revenue improve without selling coverage the requirement does not call for.

 

WHO THRIVES HERE

 - You have worked in commercial insurance brokerage or account management and can read a policy, a certificate of insurance, and a contract's insurance requirements.

 - You can tell a customer who thought they were covered that their requirement asks for more, and keep their trust.

 - You treat an existing customer's request as the start of a commercial conversation.

 - You use the policy, the certificate, and the contract instead of relying on one status.

 - You can earn and maintain the required commercial insurance licenses.

 - You are based in New York or San Francisco, or ready to relocate.

 

WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

 - You want the highest quota and the most variable pay on the sales team.

 - You treat a certificate request as a service ticket.

 - You would rather issue a certificate than tell a customer their coverage falls short.

 - You avoid direct closing conversations.

 - You need a remote or hybrid default.

 

COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS

 - Salary: $150,000 to $200,000 OTE, with the mix weighted toward base relative to New Business and Renewals. Top performers earn more.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, New York, Atlanta, or San Francisco. Based here or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday to Friday, roughly 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. or 8 p.m., in-office 5 days a week.

 - Licensing: Commercial insurance producer license required within ~30 days of start; Harper pays for training and licensing.

BENEFITS

Harper offers health, dental, and vision insurance. Office-specific benefits are set by working location.

TO APPLY

Send your resume and a short post-sale case. Explain the account, what the customer came back with, how the requirement differed from the bound coverage, how you handled the conversation, and the result.

The process has three steps: a 30-minute Zoom to meet the team, about two hours in the office to meet more people, and a super day, after which Harper decides. It moves as fast as you do.

jobs.title: Carrier Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
CARRIER PARTNERSHIPS LEAD

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

THE ROLE

One appointment can open an industry. One weak escalation path can leave hundreds of accounts stuck behind the same underwriting desk. Harper's AI is generating more qualified demand than most brokerages see in a decade, and demand only matters if there are carriers, wholesalers, MGAs, and programs willing and able to take it. You own those relationships at the portfolio level: access, appointments, capacity, economics, senior relationships, and the escalation channels that get a stuck account moving.

This is a relationship job, done on foot. You are the face of Harper to each carrier, and you stomp the ground with them day in and day out. You send carriers their urgency list — what we need quoted this week, what's stuck, what's about to be lost. You track outstanding binds and upcoming renewals across every market and make sure the carrier sees them before they become a problem. You know who controls appetite, capacity, and operations at each partner, and they know you. What you do not do is place accounts: the licensed account team selects the market, negotiates terms, and makes the recommendation on each one. You build the doors they walk through and the phone number they call when a door sticks.

Why now: Harper is expanding its insurance reach across offices and lines, and the constraint is shifting from demand to market access. Carrier trust, appointments, and capacity get more important as the machine gets better at producing submissions, not less.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and keep the market map. Know Harper's carriers, wholesalers, MGAs, programs, appointments, constraints, and real production path by line, class, and state — and keep relationship history, agreements, appetite changes, contacts, and commitments current.

 - Open the right doors. Win appointments, preferred access, new programs, and senior relationships where Harper has credible demand, and take each effort to a real decision instead of leaving it open.

 - Be the face of Harper to each carrier. Own the relationship with the people who control appetite, capacity, operations, and distribution strategy. Show up, in person and on the phone, until they think of Harper first.

 - Run the urgency list. Send each carrier what needs attention now — pending quotes, outstanding binds, upcoming renewals, stuck submissions — and track it until it's cleared.

 - Turn demand into a carrier case. Show carriers the volume, risk mix, submission quality, conversion, and operating capability that justify deeper access, then negotiate the commissions, fees, service expectations, data exchange, and escalation paths Harper can support.

 - Manage portfolio performance. Track what Harper sends, what markets quote, what binds, where service breaks, and which relationships deserve more investment. Carrier reviews tie relationship effort to sent, quoted, bound, response, and service outcomes.

 - Create clean escalation paths. Make sure account-level teams know exactly who to call and how to move a stuck issue, without taking over their ownership of the account.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You've built carrier, wholesaler, MGA, or distribution partnerships in commercial insurance, and you've personally opened and developed senior insurance relationships.

 - You know how appointments, programs, commissions, capacity, and distribution economics actually work.

 - You understand the difference between a signed agreement and a relationship that produces, and you measure yourself on the second.

 - You can turn operating data into a credible carrier-development case and negotiate from it.

 - You're commercially aggressive without making promises the operation can't keep.

 - You treat AI as leverage — it builds the urgency list, pulls the production data, and preps the carrier review — and you spend the time it saves in front of the carrier.

 - You can work closely with account teams, underwriters, and market partners while keeping portfolio relationship ownership clearly yours.

THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY

This job is on-site in San Francisco, Monday through Friday, long days, with travel to carriers, wholesalers, and industry events when the relationship calls for it. Much of the week is unglamorous: chasing an outstanding bind, re-sending an urgency list, tracking a renewal nobody else is watching, and doing it again tomorrow with a different carrier. Relationships here are built on showing up consistently and producing, not on dinners. You will have a production scoreboard, and it will be visible.

If you want to be a relationship manager without a scoreboard, if you measure success by meetings, logos, or signed agreements that don't change placement outcomes, if you want to own individual account negotiation instead of the carrier portfolio, or if you expect the underwriting or brokerage teams to maintain your relationship records for you, this seat will frustrate you. This is not a consumer acquisition or demand-generation role, and it does not come with a remote or hybrid default. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.

COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS

 - Salary: 150,000–220,000 base, plus variable tied to carrier outcomes, plus equity.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based there or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, long days. Exact cover

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT APTIBLE

 

Large language models are transforming software engineering — developers can now go from idea to code faster than ever. But that just shifts complexity downstream: deployment, observability, cost, security, reliability — all of that has to scale too, and LLMs don't yet solve the problem.

That's where Aptible comes in. Since 2014, our cloud delivery platform has been automating security, compliance and reliability for engineering teams whose apps handle the most sensitive data, in the most highly regulated industries.

The need for a platform like Aptible has never been greater. If you're passionate about cloud infrastructure and ensuring DevOps evolves to meet the pressure of AI-assisted development — and you're excited to join a small and highly talented team — we’d love to hear from you.

NEW! Aptible is part of Opti9 Technologies, a cloud solutions provider specializing in managed cloud, security, disaster recovery, and compliance. Joining forces with Opti9 gives Aptible the resources to invest more aggressively in the platform — expanding what we can deliver to the engineering teams who depend on it.

 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

We see great value in bringing together a team with different perspectives, educational backgrounds, and life experiences, and we prioritize diversity within our team. We encourage people from underrepresented backgrounds to apply.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

OVERVIEW

In this role, you'll lead on projects that improve defense and hardening for a platform that regulated companies build their businesses on. This is a hand-on engineering role where you'll architect and build secure-by-default infrastructure, run our vulnerability management and pentesting programs, and lead incident response when things go wrong.

This role reports to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), but will work day-to-day as a member of our Platform Engineering team, and in close collaboration all engineers at Aptible.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Engineering

 - Architect and ship projects that make a meaningful improvements to our security posture and the security posture of our customers. These improvements span the full stack, from AWS and Docker to CloudFormation, Terraform, Ansible, Ruby, Go, Python, and TypeScript.

 - Leverage cutting-edge AI models and third-party tools, or build your own from scratch, to level up our security game.

 - Own our vulnerability management and pentesting programs end to end, finding the best ways to automate vulnerability detection and mitigation.

 - Join the on-call rotation as a first responder for security events, and ensure we mitigate with lasting fixes so the same issue never wakes anyone up twice.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

General Experience

 - 5+ years of experience in engineering, with a track record of owning security-critical systems in production.

 - Hands on experience working on projects related to security and/or compliance. Experience with HITRUST is a plus.

 - You communicate extremely well. You favor communication that is clear, concise, and proactive.

 - Prior experience working on developer tools or platform engineering experience is a plus.

Technical Expertise

 - You have strong engineering fundamentals and coding ability, with comfort working across the full stack on a large distributed system.

 - You're a thoughtful developer in at least one mainstream language, are comfortable picking up new languages or working in unfamiliar codebases.

 - You have hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure security (AWS strongly preferred).

 - You have experience leading or heavily participating in incident response.

Organizational Strength

 - You're organized enough to run the technical portion of a compliance recertification as a project - coordinating with other engineers to collect and submit evidence by hard deadlines - without that becoming your whole job.

 - You don't let ambiguity or bumps in the road stop you. You can identify what's blocking you, and collaborate with other team members, sometimes cross-functionally, to get unblocked.

YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You appreciate working in a highly autonomous, trusted role, where the day to day priorities may shift.

 - You care about and what to be involved in what your teammates are building. You don’t want to be hyper-focused on your own isolated backlog.

 - You're a deeply curious problem solver, and you're not tied to a specific language or technology.

 - You’re an an engineer with some exposure to security and compliance, and are excited to focus on security and compliance more deeply. Alternatively, you’re in DevSecOps with meaningful security and compliance experience, have contributed production code before, and want to get more hands on with larger security-focused engineering projects.

 - You’re willing to help navigate understanding and communicating how written policies translate to security controls, and security controls translate to technical implementation.

YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF

 - You have no prior experience writing production-ready code or have no prior exposure to security and compliance. Being less experienced in one area is fine as long as you’re interested in both, however you must have prior exposure to both.

 - You are interested in exclusively buying security tools to solve problems, or interested in exclusively building security tooling to solve problems.

 - You’re not interested in working on a complex, always on system. We run a system that is business critical to hundreds of other companies. This requires a strong eye for automation, and sometimes - ideally very occasionally - overnight response.

jobs.title: Senior Commercial Broker, Brokerage Intelligence
jobs.description:
SENIOR COMMERCIAL BROKER, BROKERAGE INTELLIGENCE

Role in one line: Turn expert commercial brokerage judgment into the systems, training, and product recommendations that define how Harper brokers insurance.

The hardest brokerage decisions rarely begin as clean rules. They live in the judgment of people who have seen a difficult risk, a thin submission, an unusual coverage structure, and a market exception before. Your job is to make that judgment teachable, testable, and reusable across Harper.

This role does not sell or originate insurance, own a book, carry a sales quota, close customers, or make final account-level placement decisions.

You will work deeply with product, engineering, operations, and insurance teams to build the brokerage infrastructure behind the work: the workflows people follow, the standards AI systems are evaluated against, the training that changes behavior, and the feedback loops that make the whole operation improve.

Harper is building an AI-native brokerage, and that only works if expert judgment becomes something people and systems can learn from. New York and San Francisco are the on-site homes for this senior brokerage and product work.

WHY NOW

Harper serves many industries, coverage lines, and market paths. The company already generates enormous amounts of brokerage judgment through real accounts, market responses, exceptions, and outcomes. The opportunity is to turn that judgment into infrastructure instead of letting it disappear inside individual conversations.

The Senior Commercial Broker sits where commercial insurance practice meets product and strategy. You study how brokerage work is actually done, decide what excellent judgment looks like, encode it into workflows and decision standards, train AI systems and people against those standards, and use what fails in practice to improve Harper's products and operating model.

The mission is larger than documenting today's process. You will help define what the brokerage process should become when expert people and capable AI systems work together.

HOW YOU WORK WITH THE TEAM

You partner closely with product and engineering to turn brokerage judgment into useful tools and reliable AI evaluations. You bring the insurance standard and the evidence. Product leaders make roadmap and release decisions.

You also work with placement teams, licensed brokers, underwriters, and account owners who execute individual accounts. You define and evaluate how strong market selection, submission, negotiation, recommendation, and binding should work. They keep the final decision on each account.

You create the brokerage content, cases, and decision standards. Harper's learning and enablement teams help deliver them across the company.

WHAT YOU OWN

 - Encode brokerage judgment. Turn complex commercial decisions into clear workflows, decision standards, playbooks, examples, and escalation rules without flattening away the judgment that matters.

 - Define brokerage product requirements. Work with product and engineering to identify the brokerage problems worth solving, define what the product must understand, and recommend capabilities grounded in expert evidence.

 - Train and evaluate AI systems. Build realistic cases, expected outcomes, grading standards, and failure examples. Review AI behavior against source evidence and expert judgment, then turn failures into permanent evaluations and product improvements.

 - Design and evaluate brokerage workflows. Encode how information, decisions, exceptions, and handoffs should move through account processes. Test whether the workflow produces sound judgment without taking over its individual accounts.

 - Own the brokerage learning standard. Create the content, cases, worked examples, decision standards, and effectiveness measures that make expert brokerage judgment teachable. Collaborate with the learning and enablement owners on delivery.

 - Run the expert feedback loop. Stay close to frontline work, difficult cases, market responses, and user behavior. Separate one-off exceptions from recurring patterns and route each to the right product, process, or training change.

 - Set evidence standards. Make sure recommendations and decisions remain traceable to the real application, document, communication, quote, or market response that supports them.

 - Raise the quality bar. Identify where a workflow produces inconsistent judgment, where an AI system sounds right but is wrong, and where a person cannot tell what to do next. Redesign the system until the standard is clear and usable.

WHAT YOU WILL MAKE POSSIBLE

 - Priority brokerage workflows become clear enough to use, audit, and improve without flattening away expert judgment.

 - AI evaluations distinguish grounded commercial reasoning from an answer that merely sounds convincing.

 - Material failures become durable evaluation cases, product corrections, workflow changes, or explicit accepted limits.

 - Training built from live cases changes how people and systems handle the work.

 - Frontline evidence reaches product and engineering as a specific problem with a testable success condition.

WHO THRIVES HERE

 - You have substantial commercial brokerage, wholesale brokerage, or placement experience across complex small and middle-market accounts.

 - You have built submission strategies, negotiated difficult terms, and seen enough real outcomes to know where written process ends and expert judgment begins.

 - You understand general liability, property, workers' compensation, commercial auto, umbrella, and specialty coverage well enough to recognize the material facts, tradeoffs, and exception paths.

 - You are excited to use your brokerage expertise to build products, systems, and standards rather than personally produce accounts.

 - You can turn tacit judgment into precise instructions, worked examples, and reviewable evaluations without pretending every decision is deterministic.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Lead
jobs.description:
REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

THE ROLE

Two dashboards disagree about the same funnel. A stage changed without the owner changing. The forecast moved and nobody can trace why. Those are not reporting annoyances. They are failures in the operating system you own.

Here is the honest state of it: Harper has been piecing RevOps together as it grew — a routing rule here, a dashboard there, a forecast someone built because the company needed one that week. It got us to ~100x growth. It will not get us through the next stage. We need someone who has actually run revenue operations before, who knows what a canonical funnel definition looks like and why a CRM automation needs a failure state, and who will take permanent ownership of the definitions, system behavior, routing, forecast, and instrumentation underneath Harper's revenue. When another team proves a temporary fix, you decide how it enters the permanent system, and you keep it reconciled.

Why now: Harper is scaling across three offices. Atlanta adds frontline volume, New York adds a second headquarters, and this San Francisco seat keeps one inspectable revenue system underneath all of it. This role does not own frontline sales management, customer conversations, placement strategy, or marketing creative. It owns the system those teams run on.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the funnel definitions. Maintain the canonical meaning, entry rule, exit rule, source, and accountable owner for every revenue state, so there is one answer to what a stage means.

 - Own CRM behavior and routing. Define and maintain fields, validations, automations, permissions, and state transitions, and keep assignment logic, exceptions, ownership changes, and escalation paths inspectable and tested. Every routing change carries a test case, an approval owner, an effective date, and a rollback path.

 - Own the forecast. Publish the method, inputs, assumptions, and version, and carry the variance back to actual booked revenue every cycle.

 - Own revenue instrumentation. Make demand, contact, intake, quote, close, bind, and booked revenue reconcile to their source records for the same population and window.

 - Run funnel analysis and turn it into action. Find where volume, conversion, speed, or handoffs break, and convert the finding into a specific operating change with a named owner.

 - Automate repeat work with controls. Use enrichment, generated notes, task creation, quality checks, and reporting only when the source, resulting state, failure state, and human correction path stay visible.

 - Measure the change. Prove whether a workflow, campaign, routing decision, or sales motion moved conversion, speed, or revenue — and say so plainly when it didn't.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have owned revenue operations, sales operations, or growth operations at a fast-growing company. This is the real background we've been missing, not a nice-to-have.

 - You understand CRM architecture, lifecycle stages, routing, attribution, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene from the inside.

 - You can write SQL, or work directly enough with the data to test a claim yourself before you repeat it.

 - You move from analysis to operating change and then measure whether the change worked.

 - You can partner with sales leaders and frontline operators — working inside the sales, intake, placement, and service workflows before changing them — without turning every problem into a process meeting.

 - You treat AI as leverage — you've operated generated notes, enrichment, routing, or reporting automations with visible source data, failure states, and correction paths — and you have opinions about where it helps and where it quietly corrupts the record.

 - You care more about booked revenue and conversion than dashboard activity.

THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY

This job is on-site in San Francisco, Monday through Friday, long days, in the building with sales, intake, and placement, with travel to Atlanta and New York as the offices scale. You are inheriting a system that was assembled under pressure by people whose real jobs were something else. The first months are archaeology: finding every definition that drifted, every automation nobody owns, every report that doesn't reconcile, and fixing them while revenue keeps moving through the pipe. There is no pause button and no clean handoff.

If you want to administer a CRM without owning the revenue outcome, if you produce reports but don't make operating recommendations, if you want to own sales management, account placement, or marketing creative, or if you treat field completeness as proof that the underlying process works, this seat will frustrate you. It does not come with a remote or hybrid default. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.

COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS

 - Salary: 170,000–240,000 base, plus performance bonus and equity.

 - Free gym membership

jobs.title: Customer Operations Specialist, Payments
jobs.description:
CUSTOMER OPERATIONS SPECIALIST, PAYMENTS

Role in one line: Resolve the customer problems that cross payments, disputes, cancellations, audits, and insurance operations before they become repeat calls or unresolved risk.

A payment does not reconcile. A customer raises a dispute. A cancellation notice conflicts with the account record. An audit creates a question nobody can answer from one screen. You establish the real state, speak with the customer, and carry the issue to a documented resolution.

Harper's systems can surface records and prepare routine service work. This role handles the customer problems that still require judgment, persistence, and direct communication across payments and insurance operations.

WHY NOW

Harper serves a growing base of small businesses across many carriers, payment paths, and policy workflows. Routine requests belong with Customer Service. This specialist owns the harder cases that cross systems or require reconciliation across finance, insurance, and service records.

You own payments and disputes, plus the related cancellations, audits, insurance questions, phone work, and complex service problems that often arrive with them. The job is broad because the customer's problem rarely respects one system boundary.

WHAT YOU OWN

 - Resolve payment questions. Trace the payment question through the available records and identify the current state, amount, owner, and next action.

 - Work disputes end to end. Establish the issue, gather the source records, explain the current state, coordinate the required review, and record the final outcome.

 - Handle cancellation complexity. Read the full event chain, including notices, effective cancellations, reinstatements, and rescissions, before telling a customer what is true.

 - Support audits. Help customers understand the audit request, identify the records needed, and route licensed or specialized questions to the correct owner.

 - Answer general insurance questions within authority. Explain process and recorded facts clearly. Escalate coverage advice and licensed decisions rather than guessing.

 - Talk to people. Use the phone when a live conversation will resolve confusion faster than another automated message.

 - Reconcile across systems. Compare the customer record, payment record, policy record, communications, and external confirmation before closing a case.

 - Own the next action. Keep one named owner, one current state, and one promised update point until the issue is complete.

 - Find the repeated cause. Flag patterns that should become a permanent product, process, training, or finance fix.

WHAT RESOLVED MEANS

 - Cases preserve the customer's question, the amount or policy involved, the records checked, the owner, and the next action.

 - Payment conclusions name the evidence and the account or transaction they belong to.

 - Disputes end with a recorded resolution, customer notification, and any required financial or policy correction.

 - Cancellation answers reflect the latest event in the chain, not the loudest notice.

 - Repeat contacts decline because the underlying issue was resolved and explained clearly.

WHO THRIVES HERE

 - You have worked in payments, disputes, cancellations, audits, insurance service, or another high-volume problem-solving environment.

 - You can read several systems without losing the customer's question.

 - You are calm and direct with people who are frustrated or confused.

 - You document facts carefully and distinguish a missing record from a missing real-world action.

 - You know when to keep investigating and when to escalate.

 - You are comfortable with phone work throughout the day.

 - You are based in Atlanta or San Francisco, or ready to relocate to one of those offices.

WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

 - You want a back-office role with no customer conversations.

 - You close cases when you transfer them.

 - You infer payment, cancellation, or coverage from one status field.

 - You avoid difficult conversations or detailed reconciliation.

 - You need a remote or hybrid default.

BENEFITS

Harper offers health, dental, and vision insurance. Office-specific benefits will be set by working location.

HOW TO APPLY

Send your resume and a short example of a customer problem that crossed several systems or teams. Explain how you established the real state, what you told the customer, and how you proved the issue was resolved.

jobs.title: Account Executive, Renewals
jobs.description:
ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE, RENEWALS

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

THE ROLE

Keep good Harper customers by starting early, explaining the renewal clearly, and carrying each policy to a confident decision.

A renewal is not a reminder email. The customer's business may have changed, the market may have moved, and a successor policy must be earned before the current term expires. You own that commercial conversation.

Harper's systems surface expiring policies, prior terms, changed exposures, and the next action. You verify the account, lead the customer conversation, and earn the next term.

WHY NOW

Harper's growing policy book creates a recurring sales responsibility separate from new business and service. Service handles post-bind requests. You own the commercial decision for the next term, including updated needs, remarketing when required, and the final renewal close.

WHAT YOU OWN

 - Start early. Work the renewal book from a clear expiration-based clock rather than waiting for a carrier reminder or customer escalation.
 
 Re-understand the business. Confirm material changes in operations, payroll, revenue, locations, vehicles, contracts, and coverage needs.
 
 Build the renewal plan. Decide with placement and insurance experts whether to renew in place, remarket, change structure, or add coverage.
 
 Lead the customer conversation. Explain the options, changes, price, conditions, and deadline in plain language.
 
 Close the next term. Ask for the business, collect the required decision and completion items, and keep ownership through bind.
 
 Protect the account. Catch service issues, poor prior experience, or unresolved obligations that could undermine the renewal.
 
 Record the outcome. Capture why the customer renewed, changed, waited, or left.
 
 Identify expansion. Surface genuine new coverage needs without turning routine service changes into sales.
 
 
 
 

THE RENEWAL OUTCOMES YOU OWN

 

 - Assigned policies have a verified expiration date, renewal plan, and next customer action early enough to act.
 
 Recommendations make the current term, successor option, material changes, unresolved conditions, and deadline clear.
 
 Bound renewals move forward with the accepted option and completion steps recorded.
 
 Lost renewals preserve the customer's stated reason, or an honest unknown when the reason is not available.
 
 Renewal conversion, retention, total booked revenue, and time to decision improve without hiding lapsed or replaced terms.

WHO THRIVES HERE

 

 - You have closed renewals, account expansions, or recurring commercial relationships.

 - You can manage a large book with different clocks and levels of complexity.

 - You build trust quickly and can deliver a difficult price or coverage conversation directly.

 - You know when an account needs re-marketing rather than another follow-up.

 - You use account history and source documents instead of relying on one status.

 - You can earn and maintain the required commercial insurance licenses.

 - You are based in Atlanta or San Francisco, or ready to relocate.

WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

 - You treat renewals as customer service reminders.

 - You wait for the customer or carrier to create urgency.

 - You avoid direct closing conversations.

 - You infer renewal success from a cancellation or stage field.

 - You need a remote or hybrid default.
 
 

COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS

 - Salary: $150,000–$200,000 OTE. Top performers earn more.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco, New York, or Atlanta. Based here or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, very early morning start, in-office 5 days a week.

 - Licensing: Commercial insurance producer license required within ~30 days of start; Harper pays for training and licensing.

BENEFITS

Harper offers health, dental, and vision insurance. Office-specific benefits are set by working location. 

TO APPLY

Send your resume and a short renewal case. Explain the account, what changed, how you built the recommendation, the customer conversation, and the retention or revenue result.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Backend Engineer (Infra & Integrations) 

Data is the lifeblood of operating an excellent supply chain. Without clean data, everything crashes: forecasts drift, orders land wrong, and trust evaporates. The Spherecast Platform is the real-time operating system for global consumer-goods supply chains, and Agnes, our AI Supply Chain Manager, runs on top of it. The platform and Agnes are only as good as the data flowing in and the actions flowing back out. That's where you come in.

You'll own the integration layer end to end: the connective tissue between Spherecast and the (legacy) ERPs like NetSuite, the FTP drops and S3 buckets, the data warehouses like Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery, and the custom sheets where supply chains actually live today, plus the write paths that push Agnes's approved decisions back into those systems of record.

External data infrastructure and systems are quirky. We want you to go deep into the nature of each external API, understand its strengths and weaknesses, and build with them rather than against them. When a connector breaks at 2am on the customer's side, your monitoring tells us before they notice.

What you'll do

 - Build, extend, maintain, and monitor the integration architecture across diverse data sources: legacy ERPs (like NetSuite), FTP, S3, data warehouses (like Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery), and custom sheets.

 - Orchestrate and schedule their execution so syncs run reliably without a human watching.

 - Build a scalable, near-realtime, robust, and fault-tolerant system that handles millions of records per customer.

 - Bring the integration layer to the next level: make it more flexible and more seamless to connect new, before-unseen sources, so the next customer's stack is a configuration, not a rebuild.

 - Write round-trip integration tests ensuring the full read-update-write lifecycle never causes data loss.

 - Validate, cross-match, and detect likely errors in data early, before they cause business harm.

What we're looking for

You are a great fit if you have:

 - Hands-on experience with our backend stack: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic, with a track record of shipping production data pipelines and integrations.

 - Deep experience integrating third-party systems: REST, SOAP, and query-language APIs (think NetSuite SuiteQL), OAuth and credential management, rate limits, pagination, and the undocumented quirks every ERP hides. You've built connectors that survived contact with real customer data.

 - A strong instinct for pipeline design: fetch, validate, normalize, upsert, built idempotent and re-runnable, with clean schema boundaries between the remote system's world and ours.

 - Proficiency in SQL, writing high-performance queries and bulk upserts despite billions of data points for even a single customer.

 - Respect for the write path: pushing AI-approved actions into a customer's ERP demands safety rails, dry runs, failure capture, and auditability.

 - A habit of building for operability: structured logging, sync-run tracking, and alerting (we use PagerDuty) so failures are caught, triaged, and attributed, including telling an external stakeholder when the error is on their side.

 - Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode are your best friends. You know how to parallelize instances to make sure we're shipping 24/7, even while you sleep, and you know the ins and outs of each of them at any time.

 - Excited to work directly with CPG operators and their IT teams, owning integrations end to end, from scoping a customer's ERP setup to shipping and operating the sync that runs their business.

 - Motivated by the chance to join an exceptionally ambitious, high-ownership team that moves quickly, holds a high bar, and is determined to build a company that makes history.

 - Bonus: NetSuite experience, background task orchestration (Hatchet, Temporal), unstructured data ingestion and AWS.

About Spherecast

Spherecast is building the AI-native Operating System for Consumer Goods Supply Chains.

The Spherecast Platform brings demand, inventory, materials, capacity, costs, and business rules into one real-time operating context. It gives teams a single place to plan, evaluate tradeoffs, and execute the decisions that move physical goods.

Agnes, our AI Supply Chain Manager, runs on top of this foundation. It evaluates thousands of feasible options in seconds to decide what to produce, where to make it, and how to move it through factories, warehouses, and channels. Teams set the objectives and guardrails; Agnes turns them into approved actions in the ERP.

Our ambition is to make the physical flow of goods as programmable as code. When we succeed, every consumer product you touch will run on the Spherecast stack: planned in Spherecast OS, executed through Spherecast Rails, and optimized by the shared Spherecast Network.

Oracle made business data programmable. Spherecast makes the physical economy programmable.

Join us in the trenches in New York City to build the AI-native Operation System for Consumer Goods Supply Chains.

Be part of building the next trillion-dollar company.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter (3 month FTC, Temp to Perm)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is the platform for running reliable AI agents and workflows. Developers use it to build, deploy, and scale production systems with built-in tools for orchestration, scheduling, monitoring, and debugging.

Our Cloud product is a managed service where we deploy our users' code and auto-scale from zero to millions of executions. Today, we serve thousands of teams building AI apps and agents, handling hundreds of millions of executions per month.

ABOUT THE POSITION

We're looking for a Recruiter to work closely with our founders & Chief of Staff to fill open roles - primarily technical (engineering) hiring, with some generalist roles in the mix too. This is a 3-month fixed-term contract with the possibility of moving to a permanent role, depending on how the first few months go and where our hiring needs land.

We need a strong individual contributor who can take on the hands-on parts of hiring - sourcing, screening, interviewing, and managing agency relationships, giving time back to our leadership team and unlocking them for other priority projects without any drop in the quality of hire. We'd also love to see agency fees come down as you build out more of our own pipeline directly.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Executing hiring. Running sourcing, screening, and interviewing for our priority roles - you make hiring happen, they set the direction.

Technical hiring, primarily. Most of your time will go on engineering roles - backend, infra, and similar - but you'll also pick up generalist roles as they come up.

Headhunting and proactive sourcing. Building pipelines directly rather than waiting on inbound, including reaching out to passive candidates and using your network.

Screening and interviewing. Running first-round screens and structured interviews, and generating shortlists of genuinely qualified candidates - not a raw pile of applicants to sift through.

Managing agency relationships. Owning day-to-day contact with any recruitment agencies we use, and looking for ways to reduce our reliance on (and spend with) them over time.

Giving time back to the team. Taking on recruiting coordination and admin as much as possible to unlock the team.

Candidate experience. Making sure every candidate, hired or not, has a fast, clear, well-communicated process.

Running our applicant tracking system. Keeping our Ashby pipeline accurate and up to date so the team always knows where things stand.

REQUIREMENTS

Proven recruiting experience, technical-leaning. You've run full-cycle hiring for engineering roles at a startup or scale-up, and are comfortable picking up generalist roles too.

Fluency with engineering roles and stacks. You can hold a credible conversation about backend, infrastructure, or security roles well enough to screen and sell candidates on the role.

Strong sourcing and headhunting skills. You're comfortable building pipelines directly rather than waiting on inbound.

Experience managing agency relationships. You know how to get good work out of external recruiters and where it makes sense to bring hiring in-house instead.

Great written and verbal communication. Candidates and hiring managers alike get clarity and a fast response.

You'll be an amazing fit if you have:

 - Experience recruiting for developer tools, open source, or infrastructure companies.

 - Experience with Ashby or a similar modern ATS.

 - A track record of reducing agency spend by building direct pipelines.

 - Previous in-house (not just agency-side) recruiting experience.

 - An interest in staying on longer-term - this role has a genuine path to permanent.

ABOUT THE TEAM

 - We are a small team with a flat hierarchy.

 - We encourage continuous learning and personal development.

 - Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help.

 - We care about our customers and the open-source community.

 - Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge.

CONTRACT TERMS

3-month fixed-term contract, full time, with a genuine possibility of converting to a permanent role based on performance and ongoing hiring needs.

BENEFITS

Generous, transparent compensation - we hire the best talent and pay to reflect that.

Async working - need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!

Home office - we help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

Sick leave and time off - even on a fixed-term contract, we make sure you can take the time you need.

OUR VALUES

We are proud to be open source - we believe in the open source community and building a great free-to-use product.

We ship uncomfortably fast - as a startup, moving fast is key. We are pragmatic about what we build, when we build it.

Working autonomously - we don't tell you what to do. We decide as a team what will have the biggest impact for our customers and prioritise from that.

jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.description:
SENIOR FULL-STACK ENGINEER (VISA SPONSORSHIP)

Build the Spherecast Platform, the real-time operating system for global consumer-goods supply chains. Agnes, our AI Supply Chain Manager, runs on top of it to evaluate options, decide what to produce, where to make it, and how to move it through factories, warehouses, and channels.

You’ll own features end to end, from data models and APIs to the planning interfaces customers use every day. You’ll design the architecture that turns messy operational data into actions in real time, so physical goods flow reliably to the right place at the right time.

You’ll be part of the core team to make the physical flow of goods programmable.

If you're a builder who thrives at the intersection of large-scale data architectures, systems engineering, and interfaces that make messy real-world data feel simple, this is your opportunity to shape how global brands run their supply chains.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You are a great fit if you have:

 - Hands-on experience with our stack on both sides of the wire. Python and FastAPI on the backend. Vue 3 (or deep React experience and the willingness to switch), TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. A track record of shipping real products.

 - A track record of building full-stack apps end-to-end: designing the data architecture, building the API, and shipping the UI that puts it in users' hands.

 - Experience building data-dense product UIs such as interactive charts, editable tables, and
 drag-and-drop planning tools, and keeping them fast with server-state patterns like TanStack Query.

 - Proficiency in SQL, writing high-performance queries despite millions of data points for even a single customer.

 - A habit of testing what you ship: pytest on the backend, Playwright and Vitest on the frontend. Your features work, and stay working.

 - System design skills, one of your biggest assets. You know how to design architectures that not only scale in the short term, but can also grow with the company with minimal human supervision.

 - Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode are your best friends. You know how to parallelize instances to make sure we're shipping 24/7, even while you sleep, and you know the ins and outs of each of them at any time.

 - When it comes to engineering with your toolkit, you don't care whether it's a pickaxe or a shovel. You know which one to use at any time.

 - Excited to work directly with CPG operators and own product outcomes end to end, from understanding the workflow to shipping and operating the systems that improve it.

 - Motivated by the chance to join an exceptionally ambitious, high-ownership team that moves quickly, holds a high bar, and is determined to build a company that makes history.

 - Bonus: Experience building a company before, unstructured data ingestion systems, DevOps, and AWS.

ABOUT SPHERECAST

Spherecast is building the AI-native Operating System for Consumer Goods Supply Chains.

The Spherecast Platform brings demand, inventory, materials, capacity, costs, and business rules into one real-time operating context. It gives teams a single place to plan, evaluate tradeoffs, and execute the decisions that move physical goods.

Agnes, our AI Supply Chain Manager, runs on top of this foundation. It evaluates thousands of feasible options in seconds to decide what to produce, where to make it, and how to move it through factories, warehouses, and channels. Teams set the objectives and guardrails; Agnes turns them into approved actions in the ERP.

Our ambition is to make the physical flow of goods as programmable as code. When we succeed, every consumer product you touch will run on the Spherecast stack: planned in Spherecast OS, executed through Spherecast Rails, and optimized by the shared Spherecast Network.

Oracle made business data programmable. Spherecast makes the physical economy programmable.

Join us in the trenches in New York City to build the AI-native Operating System for Consumer Goods Supply Chains.

Be part of building the next trillion-dollar company.

jobs.title: Founding Designer
jobs.description:
ABOUT VERA HEALTH

Vera is the fastest-growing clinical app for healthcare professionals in the world. We’re a team of just over ten.

We’re already operating at a scale most teams never reach, with a team most people would think is too small to pull it off. Everyone here takes on significant responsibility, moves fast, and holds their work to an exceptionally high standard.

We’re building the founding team. The people who join now will define how this company operates for the next decade and shape the future of healthcare.

THE ROLE

The product is the company. Every screen and interaction should help a clinician understand what they’re looking at, find what they need, and know what to do next.

You’ll own how Vera looks, feels, and works. 

We’re looking for someone with exceptional taste. You have a creative point of view and can turn it into beautiful interfaces. You also understand software: how information should be organized, how interactions should behave, and how to make a complicated task feel simple.

Just as much, we care about your drive. You notice things other people miss, take initiative, and keep pushing until the work is right. You’re excited by the responsibility of being the founding designer and ready to put in the effort it takes.

You’ll work directly with the founders and engineers, move from ideas to prototypes quickly, and see your work reach users within days (sometimes hours). You’ll help decide what we build and stay involved through implementation, because the details matter in the product people actually use.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own design across Vera’s product and brand, creating a visual identity that feels distinctive and consistent.

 - Turn complex clinical workflows into intuitive experiences, from the overall journey to the smallest interaction.

 - Talk to clinicians, watch how they use Vera, and identify where the product can serve them better.

 - Explore ideas through prototypes, make clear design decisions, and bring them to life with exceptional visual craft.

 - Work closely with engineers to get the shipped experience right.

 - Build and evolve a practical design system that helps a small team move quickly.

 - Work directly with the founders on product direction and push the experience forward every week.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Exceptional taste. You have a strong eye for typography, layout, color, and interaction. Your work shows care, creativity, and a point of view.

Product intuition. You can spot a confusing flow, question an unnecessary step, and find a simpler way. You think about the entire experience and can explain the decisions behind it.

Drive and ownership. You find problems worth solving and take them on. You’re resourceful, persistent, and comfortable making progress without a fully defined brief.

Speed with high standards. You explore quickly, seek feedback early, and know where refinement will make the biggest difference. You can ship, learn, and improve without losing your attention to detail.

Command of your tools. You’re fluent in Figma and comfortable using whatever helps you prototype, communicate, and refine your ideas. Coding is a plus, but isn’t required.

There’s no minimum experience requirement. You might have spent a few years at a startup or be coming out of school with exceptional internships and personal projects. Show us strong work, clear thinking, and the ability to follow through.

HOW WE WORK

Ship, then improve. We put thoughtful work in front of users quickly and use real feedback to make it better.

Own it completely. You take responsibility for the outcome, work through constraints with the team, and stay involved until the experience works as intended.

Keep raising the standard. We give direct feedback, challenge each other’s ideas, and expect everyone to care deeply about the quality of what we ship.

Always look out for the user. Every decision comes back to the clinician on the other end. Their time, attention, and trust matter.

We work hard and move quickly. This is a demanding role with substantial responsibility, close collaboration, and the opportunity to shape a product used in consequential moments.

WHY VERA

 - Traction: 100%+ month-over-month growth, built by a team of five.

 - Meaningful work: Help clinicians find and understand the information they need to make better decisions.

 - Creative ownership: Set the design direction for the product and brand, with direct access to the founders and the people using your work.

 - Timing: We’ve just raised our Series A. We grew from 10k to over 650k users since the beginning of the year, and we're just getting started.

DETAILS

 - Location: In person in San Francisco. For exceptional candidates, relocation support (O-1A / H-1B sponsorship) available.

 - Compensation: $140k-$220k + meaningful equity.

 - Employment: Full-time.

APPLY

Complete the application form, and use the "Additional information" to include a link to your your portfolio - include one or two projects you’re particularly proud of and tell us what you personally owned. Internship work and personal projects are welcome.

jobs.title: Product Implementation Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Humaans is building the next generation of infrastructure for the workplace; software designed for companies that are scaling fast, operating globally, and pushing into new boundaries.

What started as a system of record has evolved into a broader platform for operating people globally. With Athena, our agentic AI layer, Humaans moves beyond data management into intelligent orchestration, connecting workflows across HR, IT, Finance, and Operations so organisations can act faster and with greater confidence, redefining how work gets done.

We work with ambitious teams across Europe and the US, from AI-native companies like Lovable, Poolside, Fyxer AI, and Tandem Health, to established, high-growth organisations scaling internationally and through acquisition, including Quantexa, Sellpy, Manychat, Gigs, Croud, and Threecolts. If you have massive ambition and want to work on a hard problem, with a small team that moves fast, at a moment when the category is genuinely up for grabs - this is it.

THE ROLE

A great implementation sets the tone for everything that follows: product adoption, customer confidence and the quality of the long-term relationship.

As a Product Implementation Specialist, you’ll own the customer journey from signed contract to successful launch across both our core HRIS and Athena platforms. You’ll help customers migrate complex data, configure Humaans around their organisation and deploy AI agents that deliver value from day one.

You’ll work closely with customers and teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product and Engineering. Alongside delivering excellent implementations, you’ll improve how the work itself gets done, using AI to increase accuracy, reduce manual effort and shorten time to value for every customer that follows.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own implementation projects from initial scoping through to launch, establishing clear requirements, timelines and responsibilities across the HRIS and Athena platforms.

 - Lead complex data migrations for global organisations, using AI-assisted tooling to accelerate data preparation, identify anomalies and validate accuracy at scale.

 - Configure Humaans around each customer’s organisational structure, workflows and policies, ensuring the platform reflects how they operate.

 - Act as a trusted adviser, guiding customers through implementation best practices and helping them achieve their operational transformation goals.

 - Manage stakeholders across HR, IT, Finance and Operations, maintaining alignment, resolving blockers and keeping multiple projects on track.

 - Guide customers through integrations, APIs and webhooks so they can take advantage of the platform’s technical capabilities.

 - Establish a seamless handover to Customer Success, ensuring the team has the context and foundations required to build a successful long-term relationship.

 - Improve our implementation approach by introducing AI-enabled workflows, refining playbooks and sharing recurring patterns, friction points and product feedback with Product and Engineering.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A strong record of delivering projects on time and within scope while managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders.

 - Exceptional attention to detail, particularly when handling data migration, validation and product configuration.

 - Practical experience using AI to materially improve implementation work, with clear examples of what changed and the impact it delivered.

 - Confidence working with integrations, APIs and webhooks, with the ability to explain technical requirements clearly to customers.

 - Strong working knowledge of Google Sheets or Excel and the ability to learn new systems and tools quickly.

 - Clear, credible communication and the judgement to manage expectations, resolve difficult situations and build trust with senior stakeholders.

 - Comfort operating in an environment where processes are still developing and you are expected to improve them through hands-on experience.

YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You prefer to inherit a fully established implementation process 

 - You are uncomfortable taking personal responsibility for project timelines, data accuracy and the quality of a customer’s launch.

 - You rely on customers or internal teams to drive progress when projects become complex or unclear.

 - You prefer to avoid technical conversations involving data, integrations, APIs or webhooks.

 - You have not yet incorporated AI meaningfully into your work.

 - You are uncomfortable managing several projects and stakeholder groups at the same time.

This is an in-person role. Our team comes together in the office Monday through Thursday, while most of the team collaborates in person on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays.

PACKAGE & BENEFITS

Early stage startups can be messy – we know that. We're putting effort in providing you with the best employee experience and a quality driven environment in exchange for trusting us.

 - Market-leading compensation that reflects your value

 - Share Options with 5-year exercise window so you don’t feel pressure to exercise if you leave

jobs.description:
ABOUT AFTERQUERY

AfterQuery https://www.afterquery.com/ is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it. 

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.

WHY APPLY

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives.

Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers.

Technical Content Writer (Contract)

Location: Remote, US-based

Commitment: Approximately 10–15 hours per week to start, with potential to expand based on content needs. Weekly deliverables will be prioritized together across social media, blog posts, and other public-facing content.

Compensation: $60/hour

OVERVIEW

We’re looking for a contract Technical Content Writer to help shape AfterQuery’s voice across our public-facing written content. You’ll communicate our work as a research lab curating human data for AI through social media, founder content, blog articles, and other company communications.

You’ll work closely with our marketing team, founders, and researchers to turn ideas, technical developments, and company updates into clear, compelling writing. This role spans technical and non-technical content, with audiences ranging from AI researchers and top labs to experts and prospective hires.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Write and adapt content for AfterQuery’s brand and founder social media accounts, including X and LinkedIn, maintaining a distinct and consistent voice for each

 - Develop technical and non-technical blog posts covering research, industry perspectives, company updates, and stories from our team and expert community

 - Turn research papers, technical findings, and conversations with subject-matter experts into accurate, accessible content

 - Draft founder thought leadership, hiring posts, announcements, and other public-facing written materials

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience writing content for an AI, software, data infrastructure, or other technical organization

jobs.title: Senior Product Engineer (£80k-125k + Equity)
jobs.description:
👋 HEY! WE'RE CONVEO.AI 

Conveo is a Y Combinator-backed company in an active growth period. We started this year as a team of ~20 and are on track to reach ~120 people by year end. The people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how this company is built.

 

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We’re investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

The engineering team is small and deliberately so. There are no product managers, no designer handoffs, no tickets waiting for someone else to prioritise. Engineers own the full distance from customer problem to working software, and that proximity to the product is exactly what makes this role interesting. You'll report directly to one of our engineering leads, and work incredibly closely with our CTO, Maarten.

Dig deeper into our Engineering/Product ways of working 👉 here https://engineering.conveo.ai/engineering-at-conveo👈

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/49c7399e-a401-4987-ab34-2ca5e18d2f29/82d8d474-2034-4e8c-990c-c2e828853c75/NRP19251.jpg]

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING AND WHY

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high quality consumer / B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing, and product teams.

Traditional research is slow, expensive, and superficial. Running it well requires expertise most teams don't have. That gap affects how well companies understand their customers and how well they can serve them. We're closing it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

We need a Senior Product Engineer who works backwards from the experience. This is someone who starts with the user's problem, not a spec, and owns everything between that conversation and the code that ships. You shape what gets built, actively contributing to product direction, influencing what we build and how we build it, with real technical and strategic impact.

Own the full stack, from the interface to the infrastructure

Build the interface customers open every day and can't imagine working without. React is the core of what customers see and touch — you lead frontend architecture in React and TypeScript, set the quality bar for components, state management, and performance. And you don't stop there. From API design to cloud infrastructure (AWS), you ship complete, polished features end to end, including AI-powered ones built on LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and async pipelines.

Be the engineering voice in every customer conversation

When a customer has a need, an engineer hears it, interprets it, and solves it. You join customer calls (about once a week), form a clear point of view on what to build, translate feedback into scoped product decisions, and follow through.

Use AI throughout

You reach for agentic solutions first. You use AI to reason, build, review, and test at every stage and you help raise the bar for how the whole team works. Documentation overhead doesn't slow us down here — AI handles that layer, and you're someone who is happy to work that way. You stay current on what frontier models can do and bring that into what we ship.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 6+ years of experience building full-stack applications with TypeScript and Node.js.

 - Strong backend experience: designing APIs, working with PostgreSQL, and managing background jobs and async workflows.

 - Solid frontend skills with React. .

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS and/or GCP) — you're comfortable with services like S3, media pipelines, and deployment tooling.

 - Experience building AI-driven applications (e.g. prompt engineering, working with LLM APIs, and/or fine-tuning experience are a plus).

 - Can independently lead projects from concept to launch.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English with a keen eye for detail.

 - A collaborative mindset, able to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced team.

BONUS

 - Experience with React Router v7 or Remix.

 - Experience at a small, fast-moving SaaS company where you’ve been client-facing

 - Exposure to market research or qualitative research tooling.

 - You've shipped agentic AI systems to production and can speak to failure modes, evaluations, and tool design.

WHY JOIN US?

 - Ship alongside engineers who've built and scaled products used by millions.

 - Work directly with frontier AI models and push what they can actually do.

 - Join a YC-backed team that's growing fast and gives you room to grow with it.

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity. We want you to own a real piece of what we're building.

 - Offices in London, Antwerp, and New York. We work best together, so we ask for 3 days a week in the office.

 - Regular socials: rooftop drinks, team dinners, run clubs, and more.

 - Twice-yearly off-sites to places worth travelling to. Austria, Las Vegas, and Portugal. 

 - Private health coverage with Vitality (incl. dental, vision)

 - Enhanced employer pension contribution (5% employer, 3% employee contribution)

 - Refer someone great and earn up to £5,000.

#LI-ML1

The increasing amount of regulations and complexity is breaking these old systems, making it increasingly hard to sell safe compliant products to consumers. We are building the product that enables compliance experts to stay afloat.

We are a small team of generalists working on all parts of the stack. One day you might be working on improving the reliability of our AI systems, another you might be tweaking the UI of the product. Our team is one of high trust, collaboration and autonomy, therefore we’re looking for engineers who thrive when given responsibility from day one and are not afraid to figure out things on their own. LOCATION

DAY TO DAY AT COMPLIR

 - Build AI native software that integrates with the latest models to solve our customers' hardest problems. (we have plenty of tokens)

 - Build durable workflows to understand customers' unstructured data.

 - Improve the data structures that connects cross border regulatory data

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least 2-5 years of experience

 - Strong understanding of React and TypeScript, with experience of working across the full stack. You understand browsers, but also the ins and outs of databases

 - Product taste. You have opinions about UI/UX and enjoy iterating to get to the correct product shape

 - High agency. You take responsibility and are able to work without a PM giving you tickets

 - Experience working at a startup

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Small collaborative team. We work hard but have a lot of fun. We are a diverse set of people with different backgrounds

 - Employee friendly equity package

 - Competitive salary

 - Work at a venture backed startup. Read our latest 11m seed round led by GC here: https://www.complir.io/resources/news/complir-raises-11m-seed https://www.complir.io/resources/news/complir-raises-11m-seed

 - 0 -> 1 work. Have real influence on how the product is shaped and work on green field projects

jobs.title: Staff Backend Engineer, Platform
jobs.description:
Opportunity

 - ZeitMind is an autonomous data engineer for mid-market businesses. Agents and people work the same company data: ingest, pipeline, clean, analyse, build operational apps

 - we are growing fast and will be onboarding multiple enterprise customers a week. The backend isn't ready yet, your impact will decide the speed at which we can grow

 - load growth is compounding: more customers, multiple users per customer, many agent interactions per user and multiple agent artifacts (data pipelines, schedules, analyses) coming out of the interactions

 - you own the platform

What you'll do

 - scale a multi-tenant Postgres under unpredictable load: query and I/O optimisation, read/write separation, horizontal scaling

 - make agent-driven workloads survivable: one user can spin up 30 table syncs, some running hours, while others query large sources

 - manage the sandbox layer: Docker containers where agents run queries and reverse-engineer files, with compute and memory budgets

 - own connectivity into customer networks: SOCKS5 over WebSockets, authentication, routing

 - scope the architecture and build it

What we're looking for

 - staff or principal level, still hands-on, writing production code

 - built and scaled multi-tenant data platforms in a B2B startup or platform company before

 - deep Postgres or database knowledge: query plans, locking, I/O, caching, replication, sharding

 - understands startup pace and ownership without specs

 - pragmatic over ideal, wants to build foundations right without overengineering

 - strong TypeScript

 - English C1, German a plus

Nice to have

 - experience at a data platform or warehouse company (Snowflake, Databricks, Cloudflare or similar)

 - networking depth: proxies, VPN, routing

Location

 - preferred: Munich, on-site. We support relocation within Europe

 - already in London? We can make that work. We have people here and are opening a small office, and we'd expect regular Munich travel. In-person culture is important to us

Tech stack

 - TypeScript end to end. Bun, tRPC, Postgres, Supabase. React frontend (Mantine, TanStack Query). Docker, job/process management, VPN/routing, agentic frameworks

jobs.title: SAP Integration Architect
jobs.description:
About the role

We are looking for an SAP Integration Architect to own how Finto connects to SAP. Some of our customers run their finance operations on SAP, and no two landscapes look alike: R/3, ECC and S/4HANA, on-premise and cloud, Business One and Business ByDesign. You'll design how master data, invoices and postings move between those systems and our AI platform, and turn what starts as a bespoke integration into a product that goes live in weeks. This is a hands-on role, working directly with our CTO and the founding team: you'll set the architecture, write code, and sit across the table from customer IT. You're the first hire dedicated to SAP at Finto and you define what the practice becomes. We're headquartered in Munich, with roots in San Francisco through Y Combinator.

What you'll do

 - Own the end-to-end architecture from a customer's SAP system into Finto: master data, invoices, postings, write-back.

 - Choose the integration path per SAP flavour - OData, IDoc, BAPI/RFC, BTP/CPI, file-based - and make that choice repeatable instead of re-deciding it per customer.

 - Build the connector platform: templates, validation, monitoring, and the tooling that makes every new landscape faster than the last.

 - Translate FI and MM process knowledge into specifications and field mappings our engineers build against.

 - Ship production code with the engineering team - same repo, same reviews, Node.js and TypeScript.

 - Be the SAP authority in the room: with customer IT, with their integration partners, and in our own technical conversations with prospects.

 - Set the standard for how Finto goes live on SAP, and move more of it into the product with every rollout.

What we're looking for

 - 5+ years of hands-on SAP integration work in real customer landscapes across R/3, ECC and S/4HANA, ideally more than one generation of them.

 - Deep knowledge of the accounts payable process in SAP: FI, MM, the document flow around incoming invoices, tax determination, and why the field a customer means is rarely the field the label says.

 - Fluency across SAP's integration surface - OData, IDocs, BAPI/RFC, BTP/CPI - and a clear position on clean core.

 - Strong coding skills, ideally in TypeScript/Node.js. You architect and you build; specifications alone aren't the job.

 - A product instinct: you'd rather build a pattern once than map the same fields twice.

 - Confidence in front of enterprise IT teams, and the directness to tell them when an export won't work.

 - Fluent German and English.

 - Bonus points for ABAP, for time on the consulting side of SAP rollouts, or for anything you've built that made your own job smaller.

Work at Finto

 - An environment where we enable you to have an impact and where we focus on outcomes, not time-tracking.

 - Career-defining growth: Big ambitions mean rapid progression, expanding responsibilities, and access to our San Francisco & YC network.

 - Shape your future role: As an early team member, you define what SAP at Finto looks like, and grow it into a team.

 - Real enterprise SAP landscapes from week one, not a sandbox.

 - 25 vacation days + 2 fixed "company recharge days."

 - A vibrant in-office culture (5 days/week) in a modern office.

Interview Process

 1. Intro - 20 mins with our CEO

 2. Technical Get to Know - 30 mins with our CTO

 3. Challenge - 60 mins architecture & design challenge on a real SAP landscape

 4. Culture call with our CPO

 5. Meet the team

 6. Offer
