jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Analytics Features
jobs.description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join the team working on analytics features in RevenueCat.

RevenueCat is the monetization engine for 40% of new subscription apps shipped — and the number of apps shipped is growing exponentially. We are uniquely positioned not only to give individual developer impactful information into the performance of their own apps, but also deliver truly unique data and insight given our position in the market; we know what good looks like, and we can not only put numbers in context, but give specific recommendations on metrics to target, experiments to run and anomalies to investigate.

Our analytics features help app developers make better decisions that improve the monetization of their apps. As product manager on this team, you are responsible for working with your team to set the vision and roadmap, delivering on it, launching new functionality, and increasing the impact of the team.

This role requires:

 - being analytical to be able to define how to show data as well as debugging issues and edge cases

 - being customer obsessed to understand what information app developers need for their decisions and how we can provide this information to them

 - having an understanding of the app ecosystem, how the economics of app businesses work, and what success means for app developers

You will oversee all of the Analytics features at RevenueCat — our charts, benchmarking, dashboard, and predictive LTV. You'll partner directly with leadership, collaborate across engineering and data teams, and act as the primary driver for how our customers understand and grow their revenue.

ABOUT YOU

Skills & Experience

 - You are technical. Coding is not a core requirement for this role, being able to prototype with code is (using your preferred AI stack). You can deeply understand how RevenueCat works — what is simple and what is complex within our domain. Maybe you haven’t built and shipped a mobile app yourself (yet) but you have enough knowledge to work closely and independently with highly technical folks. You can discuss APIs, data models, and risk logic with engineering partners and enjoy diving into system details

 - You’re an excellent communicator. You can express complex ideas clearly and succinctly — written and verbal, synchronous and asynchronous, across timezones and mediums. You can get your point across.

Values and Abilities

 - You act like an owner. You roll up your sleeves, dive into the logs, and get something done yourself.

 - You thrive in ambiguity. You are comfortable making low-information, high-stakes decisions. You can quickly get to confidence, move on, and iterate.

 - You're a systems thinker. You can step back from a specific customer request and see the broader system. You build things that scale.

 - You're deep on the details. You care about what users experience, not just what the data says.

 - You know when it's good enough. You are obsessed with getting things right, but you know when you're at diminishing returns. You have a bias toward shipping. You love building — and are energized by discovery, experimentation, and rapid iteration.

 - You’re passionate about great data visualization. Chart sins grind your gears. Your visualizations deliver meaningful insights. You care what is says — and what it looks like — and you know those things are dependent on each other.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product strategy and roadmap for RevenueCat's Analytics products.

 - Be obsessed with your customers. You will triage and investigate complex data and analytics problems deeply, instead of fully delegating to engineering. Dig deep to understand what developers really want — distill signal from noise and good ideas from bad ones.

jobs.title: Operations Specialist
jobs.description:
About Claim Health

Claim Health is the AI Revenue Platform for Post-Acute Care.

With the US population aging and preference for care moving to the home, post-acute care (home health, skilled nursing, home care, hospice) is one of the fastest growing verticals within healthcare. Post-acute providers operate across fragmented systems, manual workflows, and reactive processes that create operational drag and financial uncertainty. Claim Health replaces this fragmentation with an intelligent, software-driven platform that unifies data, automates execution, and enables real-time decision-making across revenue-critical operations.

We're building an adaptive platform that brings clarity, predictability, and scale to environments where reliability matters.

About the Role

We're hiring an Operations Specialist to own the accuracy of what our platform decides. Our automation runs the revenue cycle end to end for the majority of cases — referral intake, eligibility and benefits verification, prior authorization, notices of election, denials and appeals, and billing. You own the cases it can't, and you make sure the cases it can are right.

This is a high-autonomy role spanning the full revenue cycle, not a single workflow. Thousands of referrals, authorizations, eligibility checks, and claims move through the platform every week, and a missed detail means a delayed start of care or unpaid work. You'll sit directly alongside the team building the automation — the edge cases you catch and the patterns you surface become the next version of the product.

This role is open to recent graduates. Healthcare experience is a plus, not a requirement.

What You'll Do

Own the Exception Queue

 - Work a live queue containing edge cases for intake, eligibility, authorization, notices, and claims — resolving each case against payer, state, and agency requirements when no automation covers them

 - Meet turnaround expectations on time-sensitive work where a few minutes delay means delayed care or a missed filing window

Audit Quality and Accuracy

 - Review automation outputs for accuracy, consistency, and compliance before they reach the agency or the payer

 - Catch errors upstream — a wrong payer, a missing face-to-face, a misread document, a coverage gap — rather than discovering them as denials

 - Tag every exception with a clear cause so recurring failures become visible instead of absorbed

Denials, Appeals, and Revenue Recovery

 - Investigate denied and underpaid claims, determine root cause, and work the appeal through to resolution

 - Trace denials back to their origin — an eligibility miss at intake, a missing authorization, a coding or documentation gap — and close the upstream hole

 - Track denial patterns by payer and agency and flag the ones worth automating against

Turn Edge Cases Into Automation

 - Configure rules, mappings, coverage logic, and thresholds in internal tooling so solved problems stay solved

 - Document findings and write escalations with enough detail that engineering can act on them

 - Track patterns across payers, states, and EMRs and bring them to the team as automation candidates

Cross-Functional Execution

 - Partner with product and engineering to refine the logic powering intake, eligibility, authorization, and billing workflows

 - Build fluency across payers, plan types, and EMRs as you work an increasingly wide range of cases

 - Serve as the feedback loop between what actually happens in the queue and what gets built next

What We're Looking For

 - 0–2 years of experience; recent graduates encouraged to apply

 - Comfort making a judgment call on an unfamiliar case with no playbook — and the instinct to write the playbook afterward

 - Exceptional attention to detail. Revenue cycle work is unforgiving of small errors

 - Clear, concise written communication; you'll document causes and write escalations daily

 - Fast at picking up new software. You'll learn several EMRs and a long list of payer portals

 - Ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments

 - High ownership mentality and bias toward action

Optional Nice to Haves

 - A healthcare-related degree — nursing, health administration, public health, health information management

 - A clinical background or license: LPN, LVN, RN, MA, or paramedic. If you've worked a floor and want out of shift work without leaving healthcare, this is a real path

 - Experience with healthcare operations, claims, billing, eligibility, denials and appeals, utilization management, or revenue cycle workflows

 - Familiarity with EMRs like HCHB, KanTime, WellSky, or Axxess

 - Comfort working with data and tools such as SQL, Excel/Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, or internal dashboards

 - A habit of automating your own work — scripts, spreadsheets, whatever you built to stop doing something twice

Why Join Claim Health

 - Real impact: Your work affects mission-critical operations and financial outcomes

 - Ownership: Meaningful equity and influence over the platform's direction

 - Hard problems: Complex systems, real constraints, no toy use cases

 - Speed: Small team, fast feedback loops, high leverage work. We have a bias towards moving as fast as possible.

 - Culture: Low ego, high standards, deep respect for craft

 - Fun: One of the most important things we screen for is can you laugh with us.

jobs.title: Founding Marketer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAINDROP

Raindrop http://raindrop.ai/ is the monitoring platform for AI agents. Engineering teams at Fortune 100s and the fastest-growing AI companies (Vercel, Speak, Clay) use it to catch silent failures in production. When an agent misbehaves, Raindrop alerts the team, links to the trace, and surfaces the root cause so they can fix it fast. With Raindrop 2.0 (Self-Healing Agents) https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/introducing-raindrop-2/, the loop closes itself: your coding agent fixes it, and the fix becomes an eval to prevent regressions.

WHY IT MATTERS

AI agents fail constantly in ways both hilarious and terrifying. Regular software throws exceptions. But AI agents fail silently, leaving engineers with almost no visibility into how their agents are actually performing.

The current status quo is sifting through millions of logs and trying to debug flaky evals that just aren't matching real world results. Evals are like unit tests, they confirm your model got specific test cases right. But in the real world agents call thousands of tools, run for hours, and encounter millions of unpredictable actions.

That’s where Raindrop comes in. It learns the unique shape of each AI agent’s issues. Starting from presets like Laziness, Forgetting, or Task Failure, to automatically tuning itself to each agent and discovering unknown unknowns.

With one click of a button, AI engineers start tracking issues or topics across 100% of their production data. They can see frequency over time, how many users are affected, relevant properties and more.

In order to process hundreds of millions of events, we gradually train small, custom models, private to each company, that learn to uniquely understand how their product is used.

As part of the early team, you’ll play a fundamental role in shaping the company - from making strategy and product decisions, to helping scale the team, to shaping the future of AI agents.

OUR INVESTORS

We've raised $50M total https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/series-a/, led by CRV, with backing from Lightspeed, Figma Ventures, Vercel Ventures, and the founders of Replit (Amjad Masad, Michele Catasta), Cognition (Walden Yan), Framer (Koen Bok, Jorn van Dijk), Speak (Andrew Hsu), and Notion (Akshay Kothari).

THE ROLE 

You’ll own PLG at Raindrop, working directly with the founders to set our growth strategy and execute it. This is an ambitious role with large scope and ownership.

This will include running launches end to end, defining lifecycle marketing, AEO + SEO, curating creative digital and physical campaigns with the goal of driving demand gen and conversion.

You’ll also build our content engine alongside our CTO, Ben https://x.com/benhylak, who has 50K+ followers on X. That includes launching a podcast, publishing writing regularly, and collaborating on design. This is a rare opportunity to learn quickly and bootstrap your own audience.

IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - Proven experience growing a product targeted towards developers and technical buyers

 - Experience building AI agents or dev tools (+ avid user)

 - Excellent writing skills

 - Growth mindset

 - Willing to do whatever it takes to solve a problem

 - Must be in person in San Francisco (or willing to move)

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Alignment
jobs.description:
ABOUT ABUNDANT

Abundant is an applied research lab focused on scaling reinforcement learning for safe and reliable agentic capabilities. We are an extremely talent-dense team of researchers, roboticists, founders, and operators whose work includes the Waymo Driver.

 

THE ROLE

Frontier labs test their models in environments like ours, which means we are the first to see novel model behavior. You will make sure that alignment is baked into everything the do: the code we deploy, the runbooks we write, and the papers we publish.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Run experiments on how our environments shape behavior: reward hacking, cheating the task, unsafe use of tools, deception over long runs. Then change how we build them.

 - Break our own graders. Find the ways to score well without doing the work, close them, and keep the attacks as tests everyone runs.

 - Build the tools that watch agents: monitors over trajectories, red team harnesses, and safety benchmarks that stay hard as models improve. On real runs, not toy ones.

 - Keep our environments sealed. Network isolation, escapes, credentials, and how much damage an agent can do when it turns on us. Last summer’s failures came from here.

 - Choose a research question about oversight, control, or long-horizon autonomy, answer it, and publish. This is part of the job, not something you do at night.

 - Decide what we will not build. Tell partners plainly what they get from us is and is not safe for.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You are an engineer first. You build your own test pipelines, learn strange codebases quickly, and find the bug in the log.

 - You know LLM safety in depth: attacks, red teaming, monitoring and control evaluations, reward hacking.

 - You can turn a vague worry about a model into an experiment, run it, and say what the result does and does not prove.

 - You read transcripts closely. You catch the small thing that makes the whole result wrong.

 - You have put research into production systems, especially post-training, distillation, or evaluation that something depends on.

 - You write clearly enough that your results change what other people do.

 - You can decide fast with incomplete evidence and defend the call with data.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Published work on control, dangerous capability evaluations, oversight, or interpretability.

 - RLHF or RLAIF experience, and a view on how training choices show up in behavior.

 - You built or ran a public benchmark or agent task suite.

 - You have run many agents at once: sandboxes, containers, logging.

 - You have advised on AI safety or governance policy.
 
 

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$250,000 - $450,000

Cash Bonus

Sizable performance bonus tied to project and company milestones

Equity

Generous early-stage grant

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

jobs.title: DevRel (SF Events)
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRIGGER.DEV

Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is an open source platform used by developers to build production-grade AI agents. It's an SDK and the infrastructure to run agents reliably at scale, so teams can focus on the product instead of the plumbing.

Our Cloud product is a managed service where we deploy our users' code and auto-scale from zero to millions of executions. With the rise of AI, being able to offload async tasks reliably is a key part of any developer's toolkit - we're building the infrastructure to make that a reality.

ABOUT THE POSITION

We're looking for someone based in San Francisco whose entire job is turning up to events, meeting developers, advocating for Trigger, and being brilliant. This role is deliberately narrow: it's 100% events, not product education, content strategy, or general marketing.

The work breaks down into three things: showing up to existing events (meetups, AI Tinkers, YC events, conferences) and being visibly excellent in the room; getting speaking slots at those events and delivering awesome talks; and, over time, organizing our own events or co-hosting them with other big tech names, like joint hackathons at the YC offices.

The goal is pure awareness. You might not even mention Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev by name at most events - the point is being visibly excellent and well-liked in the rooms where developers already are, so that a groundswell of Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev mentions builds naturally across the SF ecosystem over time.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

You'll do a variety of things including:

 - Turn up to events, meet developers, advocate for Trigger, be brilliant - attending SF developer events, meetups, AI Tinkers, YC events, and conferences, and building genuine relationships across the SF developer and founder ecosystem

 - Get speaking slots at existing events, deliver awesome talks - pitching yourself for talks and panels, and showing up polished and memorable when you get the slot

 - Organize our own events (or co-host them with other big tech names) - running Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev meetups or talks, and exploring joint events like hackathons co-hosted at spaces such as the YC offices

 - Optionally writing blog recaps or producing short YouTube clips of talks, where it's a natural byproduct of the work rather than the focus

 - Working largely independently - you'll be on your own in SF a lot, so being deeply self-motivated is essential

 - Reporting back on activity: number of events attended, video of any talks given, and a written recap of who you met

REQUIREMENTS

You really need to have:

 - Genuine stage presence and charisma - we'll want to see video evidence of you speaking, presenting, or performing (YouTube is the bar)

 - A developer background; you should be credible and comfortable in a room of engineers

 - High self-motivation - this role has little day-to-day oversight and a real risk of isolation, so you need to thrive working independently

 - Genuine belief in what Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is building, since you'll be representing us informally in every room you're in

You'll be an amazing fit if you:

 - Are an ex-YC founder, giving you access to YC-only events and community

 - Existing relationships or an existing audience within the SF/AI developer or founder scene

 - Been an early-stage founder yourself, or are very early in your career and highly self-directed

 - A track record of speaking at or organizing developer events

 - Have a social media presence

ABOUT THE TEAM

 - We are a small team with a flat hierarchy

 - We encourage continuous learning and personal development

 - Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help

 - We care about our customers and the open-source community

 - Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge

WORKING AT A COMMERCIAL OPEN SOURCE SOFTWARE COMPANY IS MORE THAN JUST YOUR DAY JOB

 - We have an active community on Discord and GitHub. Everyone on the team helps customers, reviews PRs, and creates issues

 - Great documentation matters more than ever, both for humans and for the AI tools that read it. Everyone here keeps docs up to date

 - We are a product-led growth company so everyone is expected to get involved in creating content like code examples, blog articles, videos and tweets
 

BENEFITS

 - Generous, transparent compensation and equity - We hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity as a way to ensure everyone is invested in the success of the company.

 - Async working - Need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!

 - Home office - We will help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

 - Generous vacation - We believe it's important to take time off. We encourage you to take your 25 days vacation excluding national holidays, plus sick leave and generous parental leave.

 - Training budget - An annual budget to contribute towards learning such as purchasing books, an Audible subscription or online courses.

 - Pension and 401k contributions - Enroll in our company pension scheme or we'll contribute directly to your private pension.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.description:
WHY CASCA?

Casca is building AGI for banking. We’re replacing decades-old legacy systems with AI-native technology that automates 90% of the manual work humans once had to do. 

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Our customers are FDIC-insured banks. Every one of them puts us through security review, control questionnaires, pen test results, and third-party risk assessment before we touch production. Then they hand us borrower tax returns, bank statements, and the data behind credit decisions on their own balance sheet.

So security isn't a compliance checkbox here. It's a precondition for the company existing. Every deal we win depends on it, and one bad breach ends the business.

The surface area is large and getting larger: a multi-tenant AI platform, a cloud estate under bank data-handling requirements, agents that read and act on customer data, and an engineering team shipping into all of it every day. Nobody can review their way across that. You build the guardrails, defaults, and tooling that scale past you.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Software. Detections, libraries, policy-as-code, automation, CI/CD checks — reviewed, tested, and deployed like any other service.

 - Design reviews and threat models on what actually matters: auth, tenant isolation, data handling, anything touching borrower PII.

 - The AI attack surface. Prompt injection, tool-use abuse, exfiltration paths through agents, and the evals that tell you whether your controls hold.

 - Incidents, end to end, including the write-up and the fixes that follow.

 - Bank security reviews and audits, turned into engineering work that improves the system rather than paperwork that describes it.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - Several years of experience in AppSec, with specifics you can walk us through: bugs you found, incidents you ran, systems you hardened, tooling you shipped.

 - You write production code. We work primarily in TypeScript/Node.js and Python.

 - You know where security boundaries break in multi-tenant systems, and why it's usually authorization.

 - You can explain risk to an engineer in engineering terms and get the fix shipped without escalating.

 - You can sit across from a bank's security team, take hard questions honestly, and leave them more confident than when you walked in.

 - Steady during incidents. Honest afterward.

 - You'd rather build leverage than become a bottleneck.

HELPFUL, NOT REQUIRED

 - Securing LLM or agentic products in production.

 - Standing up a security function at a fast-growing company.

 - Working inside or selling into regulated financial institutions: SOC 2, GLBA, FFIEC guidance, third-party risk, exam support.

WHAT YOU'LL GET: 

 - Impact & Ownership: A unique opportunity to shape the future of banking through AI, owning end-to-end product initiatives.

 - Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a talented and passionate team that values continuous improvement and knowledge sharing.

jobs.title: Research Scholar
jobs.description:
ABOUT AFTERQUERY

AfterQuery https://www.afterquery.com/ is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it. 

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.

WHY APPLY

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives.

Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers.

The AfterQuery Research Scholar program is a semester-long collaboration for students pursuing ambitious, publishable work in one of AfterQuery’s focus areas:

 - Data quality and data mix

 - Post-training research, including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning

 - Agent and foundation-model evaluation

 - Public benchmarks in coding and specialized domains such as medicine, finance, law, and STEM

Projects are shaped around each scholar’s interests, with the goal of producing a joint publication. Scholars receive weekly mentorship and hands-on support with engineering, datasets, human annotation, and compute resources. A cash award is provided if a jointly authored paper from the collaboration is accepted for publication.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define and execute a focused project with an AfterQuery research mentor, aligned with your interests and at least one core research area.

 - Formulate research questions, design rigorous experiments, and analyze the results.

 - Develop the datasets, methods, evaluations, or benchmark assets the project needs.

 - Document methods and results clearly and work with AfterQuery’s research and engineering teams to make the work reproducible.

 - Co-author a paper and work toward publication.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Full-time undergraduate/master/PhD student with an established publication record 

 - Ability to participate in an ongoing research collaboration throughout the academic semester.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Research publications at leading conferences or peer-reviewed journals.

 - Experience developing, publishing, or contributing to public benchmarks.

COMPANY BENEFITS (FOR ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES):

 - Health Insurance: Medical, Vision, Dental

 - 401(k) with Employer Match

 - Daily Meals: Daily UberEats Stipend

 - Monthly Wellness Stipend

We comply with applicable pay transparency requirements and provide compensation ranges based on the position, qualifications, experience, and other relevant factors. jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO 

Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure.

Role at a Glance

Gecko Robotics is seeking a Software Engineering Intern to join RoboSPLAT within Field Infra in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.

RoboSPLAT builds software and tools that help teams develop, deploy, debug, and operate Gecko’s robotic and ultrasonic testing (UT) collection systems. You will work primarily in C/C++ and Python on a defined project that improves system integration, diagnostics, testing, or development workflows.

What you will do

 - Develop C/C++ and Python software for a defined software project under the guidance of experienced engineers.

 - Build or improve tooling, diagnostics, tests, or workflows that reduce friction in developing, debugging, and deploying software on robot hardware.

 - Work across software and system boundaries by integrating services or hardware-facing interfaces, investigating system behavior, testing solutions, and documenting findings.

 - Use version control, code review, and structured debugging practices to produce maintainable code.

 - Collaborate with RoboSPLAT and partner teams, communicate status and tradeoffs clearly, and deliver a final demonstration and handoff.

Technologies We Use (If Applicable)

C/C++, Python, Git, Linux, networking, and ROS 2. Depending on the project, you may also work with the Yocto Project, NVIDIA Jetson Orin, cloud infrastructure, or Electron, React, and TypeScript.

About You

You are a hands-on engineering student who wants to understand how software behaves on real hardware. You work methodically, seek out missing knowledge, communicate clearly, and care about building tools and systems that others can use.

Required Skills

 - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related engineering discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.

 - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.

 - Foundational programming experience in C/C++ and Python, including object-oriented programming.

 - Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.

 - Understanding of basic computer networking.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain findings and tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.

 - Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with ROS 2.

 - Familiarity with embedded Linux systems or platforms such as the Yocto Project or NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

 - Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP.

 - Experience building applications with Electron, React, or TypeScript.

 - Exposure to embedded communication protocols, microcontrollers, or real-time operating systems is a plus.

 - Ability to work with basic electronic systems, read simple schematics, and use common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and programmable power supplies.

WHO WE ARE

At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. 

Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact.

Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
WHY AUCTOR

Auctor is building the AI layer for professional services and software implementation. Think of us as the brain behind the best solution engineers, forward-deployed engineers, and onboarding teams—automating the documentation, the discovery, and the decision-making that powers $400B+ in services work. We're going after one of the biggest software categories of the decade.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

Auctor is looking for a Client Success Manager to join our founding Customer Success team. You will own a portfolio of implementation partners and systems integrators after the sale, driving adoption, demonstrating return on investment, and making renewals a natural result of the value we deliver rather than a negotiation.

You will become a trusted partner to customer leaders and power users, helping them identify where Auctor can have the greatest impact across their organization and turning those opportunities into measurable outcomes. That means understanding how customers work today, helping them redesign workflows around AI, driving adoption across teams, and ensuring the value of Auctor is visible to both day-to-day users and executive stakeholders.

This is a builder’s role. You will help shape our Customer Success approach, including playbooks, onboarding, quarterly business reviews, health scoring, adoption strategies, and ROI storytelling, while working closely with Product, Sales, and Engineering to bring customer feedback back into the company and help define how Customer Success operates as Auctor scales.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BUILD

 - Own the Full Post-Sale Lifecycle: Manage onboarding, adoption, health checks, QBRs, and renewals for a portfolio of implementation-partner and systems integrator accounts, from first login through renewal and expansion.

 - Prove and Present ROI: Build and present ROI narratives that connect Auctor usage (sessions, artifacts generated, active users) to real outcomes like faster delivery, fewer handoff errors, and margin improvement, tailored to what each customer's stakeholders actually care about.

 - Champion the Customer Internally: Turn support issues, feature gaps, and integration pain points into clear, prioritized product feedback, and close the loop with customers when it ships.

 - Navigate Technical and Compliance Conversations: Work alongside our technical team on security reviews, data handling questions, and integration scoping with customer stakeholders.

 - Manage Account Health Proactively: Track health signals, flag churn risk early, and drive the internal alignment needed to execute a plan before it becomes a renewal problem.

 - Represent the Voice of the Customer: Bring customer input into internal strategy conversations, including executive-level recaps and steering committee updates for our largest accounts.

 - Help Build the CS Function: Contribute to the playbooks, templates, and processes that the next CSM we hire will inherit.
 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 4+ Years in Customer-Facing, Post-Sale Roles: Customer Success, Account Management, or Implementation/Delivery Consulting, ideally in B2B SaaS or professional services.

 - Track Record Owning Renewals and Expansion: You can talk numbers, retention, and ROI, not just relationship warmth.

 - SI and Ecosystem Fluency: Comfort with how systems integrators and professional services organizations operate; you understand SOWs, scoping, and delivery models.

 - Technically Proficient: You don't need to code, but you're comfortable with technical stakeholders and unintimidated by integrations, data flows, and security or compliance questions.

 - Strong Written and Verbal Communication: You can write an executive-ready recap, run a QBR, and hold your own in a scoping conversation with a delivery team.

 - Builder Mindset: You're excited by the ambiguity of an early-stage startup and want to help build the CS playbook, not just inherit one.

 - NYC-Based: You thrive in a high-energy, in-person collaborative environment.

Drive implementations to go-live for complex projects

 Help Build the US Pre-Sales Function

 - Feed customer insight back to Product/Engineering in a way that shapes the roadmap without overpromising on it

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role at a B2B SaaS company, with genuine pre-sales ownership (discovery, champion-building, deal shaping) - not just implementation with some pre-sales overlap

 - Track record working complex deals with technical and non-technical stakeholders - consistent deal value of $100k-150k+

 - Strong communication skills: you can whiteboard architecture with engineers and translate value to executives

 - Hands-on with APIs - you can read documentation, ideally write sample code, and debug integration issues

 - Comfort with ambiguity and building things from scratch

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS

 - You've built and closed with at least one genuine technical champion in an enterprise account, not just a friendly technical contact

 - You've built real credibility with AEs and prospects in a domain (e.g. HRIS, ATS) you likely didn't know deeply on day one

 - You've built at least one reusable playbook, template, or asset (e.g. discovery framework, POC scoping doc, demo narrative) that other people on the team now use without you

 - You can point to your influence on ARR, deal velocity, or conversion

 - You're a trusted second read for AEs on deal strategy, and go far beyond just a technical resource they loop in when asked

HOW WE WORK

Ownership end-to-end. A customer isn't "handed off" when the contract is signed - you own the relationship from first technical call through successful go-live and beyond. Problems that surface in implementation are your problems to solve, not someone else's.

Written thinking. We use long-form documents to make decisions and share context. You'll write implementation plans, technical briefs, and customer-facing documentation that help the whole team move faster. If you prefer talking through everything in meetings, this isn't the right fit.

High-performance, high-support. We're a small team of people who are exceptional at what they do. Ex-founders, and operators who've built at scale before. We hold a high bar and give you the autonomy to meet it. We also celebrate wins together (roughly once a week for big releases, closings, or milestones).

Bias Towards Action, and high agency: We are building - if we need a resource, we create it. If a process needs improvement, we refine it. We take the initiative and ownership on everything we own, and don’t wait for permission.

In-person by default. We believe the best work happens together. This role is on-site in NYC 5 days per week.

NOT A FIT IF

 - You prefer fully remote work

 - You need extensive structure and hand-holding to be effective

 - Your instinct is to answer the question you were asked rather than find out why it's being asked in the first place

jobs.title: Customer Success Lead (San Francisco)
jobs.description:
ABOUT GIGA

Giga has recently raised a $61M Series A and is working with Fortune 500 customers to deploy the next generation of customer experience - real-time AI agents that can understand emotion, resolve issues instantly, and scale across the world's largest enterprises.

Industry leaders like DoorDash trust Giga with their most complex support and operations workflows across voice, chat, and email, in high-stakes regulated environments where accuracy and compliance matter. We're at an exciting inflection point.

While we've found real commercial success, our ambitions are larger: to become the go-to AI platform for all enterprise automation, powered by our voice superintelligence. The work affects millions of people every day, and our team has the autonomy to make true impact - with brilliant founders, a clear path forward, and the kind of momentum that defines generational companies.

If being part of that resonates with you, we'd love to hear from you!

 - Voice AI startup Giga raises $61M Series A https://fortune.com/2025/11/05/voice-ai-giga-raise-61-million-customer-service-series-a/

 - DoorDash and Giga Partnership https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7391576181009018883/

 

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Customer Success Lead to own consumption across a book of Giga's enterprise production customers. Every enterprise contract we sign carries a minimum usage commitment. Your job is to get each customer to that commitment and past it: more conversations on the agent, more intents live, more channels and business units on Giga. You carry a number for it. You'll own each customer's timeline for getting there, and you'll push on it from both sides: externally, when the customer's team is slow to expand scope or route volume, and internally, when a product bug or a missing capability is what's holding them back. You sit between our Forward Deployed Engineers, who build and tune the agents, and our Enterprise Sales Representatives, who close the deals. You're the quarterback in the middle.

This is the first hire in a function we intend to build. You report to the CEO, you'll work directly with the founders and the revenue leadership team, and you'll define how customer success works at Giga before anyone else joins it.

This is not an FDE role and it's not a renewals desk. You won't be digging through tickets to find the root cause; the FDEs do that. You will know that something needs fixing, what it's costing the customer, and when it has to be done, and you'll drive it there. You'll also be the one telling customers what we're shipping and where the next use case is. When that turns into a real deal, the Enterprise Sales Representative comes back in to run it with you. You own usage and the timeline, they own paper.

 

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

A few examples from our current roadmap:

 - Consumption plans for every account in the book: Build the per-account plan from go-live to the annual minimum and beyond: which intents and channels go live in which month, what volume each one carries, and what has to be true on the customer's side and ours for each date to hold. Track it weekly and act when a week goes flat.

 - Quarterbacking the timeline, both directions: Externally, keep the customer's team moving on scope expansion, volume routing, and the approvals that slow them down. Internally, when a product bug or a missing capability is blocking a customer's next step, get it prioritized with FDEs and Product, hold the date, and tell the customer the truth about it. You don't investigate the ticket. You make sure it gets fixed on time.

 - Escalations at the right altitude: When something breaks in production, you're the customer's single point of contact. You know what's broken and what it's costing them, you pull in the right FDE, you own the communication up to the customer's executive, and you stay on it until volume is back.

 - Evangelizing what's next: Pitch customers on what we're shipping and where the next use case is in their operation. Mine conversation data, Agent KPIs, and their queue metrics to find it, quantify the savings, and get their operating leader interested. When it turns into a real opportunity, bring the Enterprise Sales Representative back in and run it together.

 - Executive cadence: Run monthly value reviews and quarterly business reviews with the customer's VP or SVP of Customer Care, Operations, or CX, with our CEO and founders in the room when it matters. The output is a bigger volume plan with dates on it, not a satisfaction score.

 - Making consumption visible: Work with RevOps to get usage against commit, and the blockers behind it, in front of the whole revenue org in Salesforce every week.

As the first Customer Success hire at Giga, you'll be expected to build the playbook, not inherit one, and to show the CEO what the function should look like at 30 customers.

 

HOW YOU'LL BE MEASURED

You own a defined book of production customers and you're paid on two things: every customer in it reaching full value on their commitment, and the book growing past it.

 - Gross revenue retention. Every customer in your book consumes their full contracted commitment and renews at or above it. This is the floor, and it's most of the variable.

 - Net revenue retention. Usage above commit, new intents, new channels, new lines of business. You find it, quantify it with the customer, and hand a qualified opportunity to the Enterprise Sales Representative to close. They carry the quota credit, you get NRR credit when it lands.

 - Leading indicators we watch with you: time from production go-live to run-rate consumption, weekly usage against the ramp plan, and executive engagement on each account.

Compensation is $200,000 to $250,000 on-target earnings depending on experience, split 75% base and 25% variable, plus equity. Variable is paid quarterly, weighted 70% gross revenue retention and 30% net revenue retention across your book, with accelerator

jobs.title: Account Executive

jobs.title: QA Engineer
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Founding GTM
jobs.description:
ABOUT PROOF OF HUMAN

Proof of Human is building the global standard for human verification across the internet. As the line between human and machine behavior becomes harder to discern, establishing who or what is behind every interaction is becoming foundational to the integrity of a digital world. Founded by Princeton PhD scientists, Mayank Agrawal and Matt Hardy, Proof of Human is a research and technology company developing the science, products, and infrastructure required to meet that challenge at global scale. As a public benefit corporation, we treat this work as both a technical frontier and a public responsibility, advancing the field while shaping the standards and governance for how human verification systems are developed, deployed, and used.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Founding GTM to join us to build the next phase of how Proof of Human goes to market. You’ll work directly with the founders and staff across sales, growth, and market development: generating pipeline, leading customer conversations, advancing deals, and turning both your intuition, your research, and what you learn on the front lines into sharper positioning, stronger systems, and clearer strategic direction. This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who wants to create the playbook while running it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Market Development: Test new industries, buyer personas, use cases, messages, and acquisition channels to determine where Proof of Human has the strongest opportunity to win. Use what you learn to recommend where the company and product should focus.

 - Pipeline Generation: Build targeted pipelines across our existing market and select new verticals through thoughtful outbound, warm introductions, events, partnerships, and other distribution channels you identify, to create a steady flow of growth opportunities.

 - Customer Discovery: Lead early conversations with prospective customers to understand their problems, priorities, urgency, decision process, and willingness to commit. Clearly communicate Proof of Human’s value to both business and technical stakeholders.

 - Deal Execution: Own opportunities from initial outreach through discovery, demos, pilots, pricing conversations, close and commercial follow-up, working closely with the team to move qualified deals toward close while maintaining a consistent momentum throughout.

 - Sales Enablement: Create the materials that help deals move forward for you and the team, including tailored follow-ups, pitch decks, business cases, pilot proposals, objection handling, case studies, and vertical-specific narratives for the buyer and use case.

 - Growth Experimentation: Run lightweight, measurable experiments across audiences, messaging, distribution channels, and conversion points. Use the results to determine what should be scaled, changed, or stopped, and turn tests into repeatable programs
 .

YOU’LL BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - Nobody has to hand you a map. There’s no established process yet for much of what this role touches. You find a starting point, try something, learn from the result, and build the next version without losing momentum as conditions change.

 - You’re curious across disciplines. Whether you’re speaking with an academic, engineer, or business executive, or entering an unfamiliar market, you want to understand the substance and communicate in the language of the person across from you.

 - You move fast once you see what needs to happen. You don’t wait for the perfect moment or someone’s blessing. You take ownership, bring other people along, and keep pushing through ambiguity, friction, and setbacks until the work is finished.

 - You think in hypotheses. You turn open-ended questions into focused experiments, define what you need to learn, and pay attention to the evidence. When the answer changes, you adjust your approach without getting attached to the original idea.

jobs.title: AI Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT GREENBOARD

At Greenboard, we're building the future of financial compliance. Greenboard is the unified, AI-native compliance operating system for RIAs, fintechs, private funds, hedge funds, and more. It replaces the fragmented mix of legacy tools and automates more than previously possible. By centralizing data and workflows, Greenboard helps firms reduce regulatory risk, simplify their technology stack, modernize how they run compliance, and save money.

Our founding team includes engineers who have scaled products at Amazon, Google, and multiple unicorn startups. We're backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Base10, and other top-tier investors, and have raised over $20M to date. Brand-name financial institutions already rely on Greenboard, and we're growing fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be our first dedicated Automation engineer. Our customers are regulated financial institutions, which means a missed bug is not just a bad user experience. It can mean an incomplete books-and-records archive, a marketing review that never routed for approval, or an attestation that quietly failed to send. Quality is part of the product we sell.

You'll own how we test: the framework, the automated suites, and the release process, built from scratch and then embedded with the engineers who ship. You'll also help us solve something most automation engineers have never had to solve, which is how to test AI systems whose output is not deterministic.

There is no existing playbook here. If you like defining the standard rather than enforcing someone else's, this is the seat.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The foundation. Test framework, automated regression suites, and QA practices built from zero, with your call on tooling

 - The critical paths. Message archiving and supervision, marketing review routing, employee attestations, and audit trails, which are the flows that cannot break

 - Testing the AI. How we evaluate AI-driven detection and review, including golden datasets and quality bars for output that is not deterministic

 - Data integrity at scale. End-to-end validation from ingestion of tens of millions of messages a day through to what a compliance officer sees on screen

 - The release gate. Bug triage, release sign-off, and the definition of deployment-ready at Greenboard

WHO ARE YOU?

 - Love to move fast and build things

 - Looking for deep ownership over the quality of everything we ship

 - Obsess over the customers you're building for

 - An excellent communicator

 - Value collaboration

 - Located in NYC

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years testing software where being wrong has consequences beyond a bad review: fintech, healthtech, payments, or anywhere an audit followed a bug

 - Able to test a system you cannot fully see from the UI. Comfortable with REST APIs and querying the database directly, because verifying a feature here means checking what landed and what the retention policy did with it, not just what rendered

 - Write Playwright or Cypress suites that survive a redesign, with opinions about selectors, fixtures, and what belongs in an integration test versus an end-to-end one

 - Can read a feature spec and name the states nobody thought about: the employee who left mid-attestation, the message that arrives out of order, the marketing piece edited after approval

 - Have held a release before, explained why to someone who wanted it out, and been right

NICE TO HAVE

 - Tested a system where output is not deterministic and had to define correct as a threshold rather than an exact match

 - Worked in a Node JS and React codebase on AWS, or debugged a queue-based ingestion pipeline

 - Been through a SOC 2 audit and know what evidence a test suite can produce for one

 - Sat with a compliance officer, an advisor, or a back-office team and watched them work

 - Interest in the financial industry is a plus, but not necessary

BENEFITS

 - 401(k) with 5% company match

 - Medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - 15 days PTO + 11 company holidays + flexible sick time

 - 2 additional PTO days for each year of service (up to 10 additional days)

 - 10 remote days per year plus additional around the holidays

 - Bi-annual off-sites and team retreats

 - Front-row seat to building the operating backbone of modern finance

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Remote)

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own a subsystem end to end document processing, workflow automation, compliance rules, communications, or integrations; and lead the projects inside it from design doc through rollout.

 - Ship AI agent capability into production: extraction and validation pipelines, confidence handling, human review routing, and the feedback loop that raises accuracy document type by document type.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Research (Intern)
jobs.description:
IMPORTANT: in the application form, please specify what term you would like to begin your internship (winter/summer/fall)

ABOUT ABUNDANT

AI models rely on two fundamental ingredients: compute and data. Abundant is building the NVIDIA of training data. NVIDIA, the leader in compute, has a peak market cap of $5T and generated $130B in revenue last year as the need for scaling compute has exploded. We believe the need to scale data is just beginning, as we move beyond SFT and human supervision to RL and Learning from Experience.

 

Our founding team consists of former founders, ML engineers, roboticists and data leads from Waymo, Google, Mercor and AWS. Our team has previously worked with DeepMind to deploy deep learning models at 1B user scale, trained SOTA models for self-driving at Waymo, and scaled data pipelines of tens of thousands of human annotators at YouTube. Our pioneering work in human computation, synthetic data, simulation and RL give us the advantage in delivering results to our customers.

 

Why now? Training data is more important and more scarce than ever before. Scaling laws dictate that linear improvement in model performance demands an exponential increase in training data. But there is only one World Wide Web and most of it has already been trained on. The next advances will require major advances in simulation, synthetic data and learning from experience.

 

What happens if we succeed? Abundant will be the core enabler for not only AGI, but ASI and physical intelligence. Most of the challenges in model algorithms and compute are already solved. What’s missing? The data necessary to move from general knowledge to domain expertise; from chatbots to agents; and from text to multimodal and physical AI. Ask any AI researcher or roboticist: the core bottleneck to progress is the availability of data, hence “abundant data”.

 

Abundant works with a majority of the top AI labs, as well as frontier startups and F500 enterprises.

 

THE ROLE

As a Member of Technical Staff, you will work directly with Abundant's founding team to architect the next generation of model reasoning and intelligence. You will lead at the absolute frontier where research and execution collide, co-designing strategies alongside top-tier researchers from AI labs to push SOTA boundaries. This is a role for a extremely strong engineers who are already contributing frontier research.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Drive Foundational Research & Execution: Architect and execute a core research agenda to discover simple, generalizable ideas that advance model reasoning and intelligence at scale. This includes owning the full research-to-production lifecycle and ensuring rapid deployment of your work in live systems.

 - Model Alignment & Data Strategy: Partner with the world's most advanced AI research teams to design, engineer, and iterate on high-impact datasets and large-scale benchmarking efforts that shape how frontier models behave, specifically focusing on critical alignment, safety, and defining optimal reward signals.

 - Autonomous Problem Selection: Autonomously identify, scope, and manage long-running research projects, choosing the most impactful problems that are critical to scaling data for AGI/ASI.

 - System Infrastructure: Collaborate closely with engineering teams on data pipelines, internal tooling, and high-performance deep learning algorithm implementations.

WHO YOU ARE

 - Exceptional Research Depth & Strategic Vision: Research expertise in a related field (e.g., CS, ML, NLP) ideally with that work published at a major conference (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). You must possess the velocity to master complex fields and a proven track record in the productization of research, encompassing high-stakes evaluation, large-scale benchmarking, and product feature development.
 
 - Proven experience shipping research directly to production and live systems, specifically focusing on advanced post-training, distillation, and high-stakes evaluation methodologies.
 
 - Large-scale agent systems: orchestration frameworks, tool APIs, distributed execution, observability, and logging infrastructure.

 - Strategic & Ethical Leadership: You possess a thoughtful, strategic perspective on the societal and safety impacts of deploying general-purpose AI systems. Experience advising on or shaping governmental policy related to AI safety and governance (e.g., House of Lords or Online Safety Bill initiatives) is required.
 
 

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$10,000/month

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

jobs.title: Founding Content Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
About Phonely: 

At some point in the future, every business will answer their phone with voice AI. We are building the platform that makes it possible.

Phonely builds conversational voice AI agents for high volume phone workflows. Our customers use us to qualify leads, book appointments, route calls, and resolve real customer conversations in production. We just raised a Series A from top-tier investors, we are one of the fastest growing companies in San Francisco, and we are still early.

About the Role:

Audiences get built on stories. Distribution matters, but only after someone has something worth saying.

This role is for someone who can find those stories, shape them, and make people care. You will own how Phonely shows up in public.

Our buyers are not a generic tech audience. They run phone lines for a living: car dealerships, home services companies, insurance agencies, lenders. They do not wake up looking for AI content. Your job is to make them stop, watch, and care about what happens on their phones.

Nobody has built this at Phonely before. There is no playbook, so you will write it. This is on-site in San Francisco, five days a week, working directly with the founders.

What You’ll Do:

• Own the public voice: what we sound like, what we talk about, and what people remember us for.

• Publish constantly: start at 5 to 10 pieces a week and ramp. The best company in our category publishes 10 times a week. We want to pass them.

• Build the system behind the output: your taste sets direction, AI tools and repeatable workflows carry the lift. Forty good pieces a month beats eight perfect ones.

• Mine the tape for stories: find the moments that show what is actually changing on real phone lines, then get them out fast.

• Run the whole chain: concept, shoot, direct, edit, publish, reply.

• Put the right people on camera: sometimes you, sometimes an engineer, a rep, a founder, or a customer.

• Figure out the channels: start with LinkedIn, YouTube, and Meta, then go wherever our buyers actually spend time.

• Turn shoot days into paid creative: cut the best moments into assets the growth team can put spend behind.

• Learn from the people closest to the work: the engineers building the models, the reps selling it, the customers running their businesses on it.

• Represent Phonely outside the office: launches, customer sites, industry events, podcasts, anywhere the story should be told.

What You’ll Bring:

• A body of work nobody assigned you. A hundred pieces or more on your own account, no client, no brief.

• AI-native production habits. You already use tools to multiply your output and have opinions about which ones actually help.

• Comfort on camera without a script. One take, phone camera, no autocue.

• A sharp read on your own work. You can explain why one piece landed and another did not.

• Range across the production chain: shooting, producing, editing, and publishing with whatever tools you taught yourself.

Bonus Points:

• You are an athlete, or you have a background worth telling a story about.

• You have made paid creative for a startup.

• You have worked at an early-stage company.

Where you went to school, and whether you have held this title before, are not the point. We will read what you made.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6 to 12 months:

• Cadence: a daily rhythm that holds, with a production system that makes the next piece easier than the last.

• Audience: real growth on Phonely’s channels from a standing start.

• Measurement: total impressions, impressions viewed, marketing qualified leads, and conversion from content engagement into qualified sales conversations.

• Voice: a Phonely voice on camera the rest of the team can learn from and repeat.

Why Join Phonely:

We are a team of ex-athletes, founders, and builders with low egos and high standards. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. On-site in San Francisco, meals covered, quarterly offsites to interesting places (Rocky Mountains, Costa Rica, Indonesia), and meaningful equity in a company that is growing fast. You will work directly with the founders and have real ownership over the brand.

The brand you build will be Phonely’s, but the work will be yours, and we will say so publicly.

Interview Process:

1. 15 minute intro call to hear your story and what you have built.

2. Send your best performing piece plus a 60 second video shot on your phone, one take, no script: a true story about a phone call that changed something.

3. Portfolio review. We go through your feed together and talk through two pieces, one that landed and one that did not.

4. Paid test week at your day rate. Two days with us, twenty pieces published by Friday, at least five on subjects you chose. Then show us the system you built to make twenty possible.

5. Final conversation with Will.

Details:

• Location: San Francisco, CA (on-site, 5 days a week)

• Type: Full time

• Compensation: $80K to $150K, offers equity

ABOUT FIRSTWORK

Labour markets are broken. Millions of people are ready to work and can't start. Screening, right-to-work checks, contracts, onboarding and scheduling still run across disconnected systems, with hundreds of manual decisions in between. Firstwork builds AI agents that run frontline workforce operations end to end. We activate hundreds of thousands of workers a month globally for some of the world's largest employers and staffing firms, working forward-deployed inside the customer's operation. Backed by Y Combinator and Gradient (Google’s AI fund), with offices in New York, and London and Dubai opening this year.

WHY THIS ROLE

Frontline labour markets are badly measured. Governments publish unemployment and vacancy statistics. Nobody publishes a credible number for how long it takes to get a qualified person from application to first shift, what that delay costs, or how much of it is regulatory rather than operational.

We see activation at scale, across sectors and jurisdictions, so we can measure what nobody else can. Publishing it sets the terms of the debate, gives policymakers something real to work with, and gives our commercial teams something better than a pitch deck. The standard we are aiming at is work a member of government or tier one investor forwards along to their colleagues.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Set the research agenda

 - Write and publish flagship reports and white papers

 - Own editorial standards across everything Firstwork publishes

 - Build data stories with our data and engineering teams

 - Lead policy engagement on European labour and employment regulation

 - Produce the CEO's long-form writing and speaking material

 - Build partnerships with academics, institutions and industry bodies

 - Manage a Content Producer who turns the research into video, graphics, podcasts and report design

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Seven or more years in research, journalism, think tanks, policy, or a strategy function producing original published work

 - A portfolio with at least one piece that changed how someone thought about a subject

 - Quantitative comfort. You can interrogate a dataset and recognise when it won't support the claim you want to make

 - Real interest in labour markets, migration, regulation or the economics of work

 - The spine to hold a line on accuracy when there is commercial pressure not to

 - Editorial judgement. You can commission, edit and improve other people's work

 - Use of AI across the research process, on the understanding that it raises the verification bar rather than lowering it

This is a rare opportunity for a serious writer and content creator to help shape the future of work at a high-growth, well-funded company with strong opinions about what the world should look like in the age of AI. If the idea of running a research desk on a dataset nobody else has access to excites you, send us your best work.

We're bootstrapped and profitable which means we answer to our customers and play by our rules. We're proud of our 130-person, 100% remote team, focused on building Close so that no small, scaling business fails because it can't figure out sales.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our GTM org has a lot of questions. Most of the questions we care about can’t be answered by spinning up a cute dashboard. Is branded search creating new customers or capturing demand that already existed? Did the homepage redesign improve conversion, or did our traffic mix change? If we’ve got some wild ideas for our next bet, where should the money go?

These kinds of big-picture questions require someone who can interrogate the metric, trace it through the warehouse, understand the business context, and turn it into action. This person will be our first Full Stack Data Analyst dedicated to GTM. You’ll work alongside GTM leadership to make consequential decisions while still staying hands-on in the nitty gritty of all the data.

The best part: the way we answer these questions is changing. Effective SQL is just a few tokens away, dashboards can be Claude-ed in minutes, and teammates increasingly expect to find their own answers. You’ll build the semantic layers, context, and guardrails that make self-service possible, even trustworthy, then determine where an analyst’s expertise is indispensable.

YOU ARE

 - An experienced analyst. You have roughly 8 years of hands-on, highly technical analytics experience. Most importantly: you’re backed by the pattern recognition that comes with having seen all sorts of hairy problems. You’re at the point in your career where you can take an ambiguous business question, dive head-first into the data, turn your findings into a decision, and bring everyone else along with you.

 - A bridge between the technical and the business. You can build a model in dbt, work directly in Snowflake, and translate it into something actionable. You’ll partner closely with our Lead Analytics Engineer but you need to be willing and able to dive in and self-serve.

 - Fluent in the quirks of GTM data. Attribution, channel definitions, UTMs, bots and broken tracking are known quantities. You don’t need to have been a dedicated GTM Analyst, but you should certainly know your way around this part of the business.

 - Pushing the boundary of what AI means for analytics. AI is writing your first-draft SQL, analysis, and reporting and you’ve shifted that energy to bringing analysis into the future: building the semantic layers, context, and guardrails that let the team self-serve trustworthy answers.

 - A trusted cross-functional leader. Teammates across functions and levels listen to you. You immerse yourself in the context of their needs and bridge gaps in understanding.

 - Fiercely independent and accountable. You welcome a vague ask with aplomb. You’ll scope the problem, find the dependencies, bring in the right people, and drive the work through the analysis, recommendation…all the way to a fix.

 - More concerned with impact than output. A polished dashboard is useful only when it changes what we do. You prioritize the questions that can materially improve acquisition, conversion, retention, and revenue.

YOU WILL

 - Make our GTM data trustworthy. You’ll define metrics, model the funnel from first touch through paid conversion, and reconcile discrepancies across Snowflake, Segment, Amplitude, GA4, and our ad platforms.

 - Explain what we’re seeing. Why are trials up while paid conversion isn’t? Why are Snowflake and Amplitude disagreeing? Which channel is driving volume but producing low-quality customers? You’ll dig into the data until we understand what changed and why.

 - Help decide what to do next. Are we on track to hit our goals? What would another investment in paid media produce? You’ll forecast, model the tradeoffs, and empower leadership to make the best possible decision.

 - Own the outcome. Whether you uncover something small like broken campaign tracking or you’re focused on moving a major business metric, you’ll bring in the right people and shepherd the team to the data-driven outcome.

 - Define the next era of Data at Close. You’ll help us move from a queue of reactive requests to a system where an agent spots changes, assembles the context, and gets the right insight to the right person at the right time.

BENEFITS

Strive for greatness - Constantly challenge yourself and others

ABOUT APTIBLE

Large language models are transforming software engineering — developers can now go from idea to code faster than ever. But that speed cuts both ways: AI makes attackers more capable, zero-days weaponize faster, and AI-assisted "vibe coding" is shipping more code with less security review. Deployment, observability, cost, security, reliability — all of that has to scale too, and LLMs don't yet solve the problem.

That's where Aptible comes in. Since 2014, our cloud delivery platform has been automating security, compliance and reliability for engineering teams whose apps handle the most sensitive data, in the most highly regulated industries. The future of Aptible is to be the safe place to run both traditional and AI-native applications: isolated from lateral movement, defended against known and emerging vulnerabilities, and instrumented so that if something does go wrong, the blast radius is contained and the forensics are already in place.

The need for a platform like Aptible has never been greater. If you're passionate about cloud infrastructure and ensuring DevOps evolves to meet the pressure of AI-assisted development — and you're excited to join a small and highly talented team — we’d love to hear from you.

NEW! Aptible is part of Opti9 Technologies, a cloud solutions provider specializing in managed cloud, security, disaster recovery, and compliance. Joining forces with Opti9 gives Aptible the resources to invest more aggressively in the platform — expanding what we can deliver to the engineering teams who depend on it.

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

We see great value in bringing together a team with different perspectives, educational backgrounds, and life experiences, and we prioritize diversity within our team. We encourage people from underrepresented backgrounds to apply.

-----

 

ABOUT THIS ROLE

We’re looking for a dynamic Product Manager who can set the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition that expands our positioning as the secure PaaS for the AI-native era, for both traditional and generative/agentic applications. In this role, you will partner closely with our engineering team, product designer, and marketing team to:

 1. Build something our target customers want (create value), and

 2. Build something that helps us strategically grow the business (capture value)

This PM is responsible for Acquisition (measured by new customers), and will work alongside the PM for Retention (measured by NDR).

WHAT YOU’LL DO

There are two types of outcomes this role will be accountable for:

 1. (Quantitative) Business outcomes/Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
 
 - Product signups and new product-led customer conversions
 
 - Count of customers using features delivered against the Acquisition roadmap, across LLM Gateway and PaaS
 
 - New ARR ($) from features delivered against the Acquisition roadmap

 - Engineering: De-risk Feasibility (can we build it?)
 
 - Design: De-risk Usability (can users figure out how to use it?)
 
 - Define a clear roadmap of features (or product “bets”)
 
 Delivery: Helping the team get the product built and in the hands of customers
 
 - Define product requirements for features based on the outcome of discovery
 
 - Empower engineering and design to build the product, unblocking implementation as needed in a timely manner
 
 - Empower Marketing and CS to put our product in front of users by providing foundational resources such as (but not limited to):
 
 - Pricing
 
 - ICP
 
 - Documentation
 
 Analytics: Measuring and analyzing how our customers use our product
 
 - Define data sources and success metrics, working with BizOps to set up dashboards and monitoring
 
 - Analyze adoption, engagement and usage patterns

YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

Overall Professional Experience

 - Functional Experience: You have 10+ years of experience as a Product Manager.

 - Technical Acumen: You have 3+ years of experience in the PaaS / Developer Tools space, either as a Product Manager or other relevant role (e.g. Software Engineer). You can speak the language of our customers without having to go through our Engineering Team as translators.

 - Driver Mindset: You’re motivated to steer direction for a small, highly collaborative team. You don't let bumps in the road stop you: you identify what's blocking you, take ownership, and drive to get unblocked.

 - Going 0 → 1: This isn’t an environment where interviewees are lined up to talk to you. You’re:

You use that instinct to position our product strategically, thinking about go-to-market and how the value we create actually gets captured.
