jobs.description:
ABOUT BOLNA

Bolna is Voice AI infrastructure built for India - and now for the world. We help businesses deploy intelligent voice agents that can call, converse, and convert in any language, at scale. From collections to customer support to sales, our agents handle millions of conversations so humans don’t have to.

We’re a YC F25 company, backed by General Catalyst, with 1,050+ paying customers and growing fast.

THIS ROLE

As an Enterprise Lead, you will own the success of Bolna’s largest and most strategic enterprise deployments.

You will lead a team of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), ensuring enterprise customers move from business problem → deployment → measurable outcomes. You’ll work closely with CXOs and senior stakeholders on the customer side while partnering with Bolna’s Product, Engineering, and Business teams internally.

This is a high-ownership role. You will be expected to bring structure to complex enterprise problems, drive execution through your team, and ensure that deployments are not just launched - but successful.

You’ll operate at the intersection of enterprise delivery, customer success, technology, and business.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead and manage a team of FDEs, setting clear priorities, driving execution, and maintaining a high bar for customer delivery.

 - Own the end-to-end success of strategic enterprise deployments - from scoping and solution design to launch, adoption, and expansion.

 - Work directly with enterprise stakeholders and CXOs to understand business objectives, define success metrics, and communicate progress.

 - Translate complex business requirements into clear execution plans across FDE, Product, and Engineering teams.

 - Review deployment strategies, solution architecture, agent performance, and customer outcomes to ensure quality and scalability.

 - Identify risks and bottlenecks early and drive cross-functional teams toward resolution.

 - Build repeatable enterprise deployment playbooks, processes, and best practices.

 - Analyze customer and deployment data to identify patterns, improve outcomes, and make informed decisions.

 - Present deployment plans, business cases, performance reviews, and recommendations to senior stakeholders.

 - Partner with Sales and Business teams on enterprise opportunities, solutioning, pilots, and expansion conversations.

 - Act as the senior escalation point for critical enterprise accounts.

 - Develop the FDE team through regular feedback, coaching, and high-quality problem-solving standards.

 - Bring customer insights back to Product and Engineering to influence product priorities and platform improvements.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

MUST-HAVE

 - 5+ years of experience in management consulting, B2B enterprise deployments, enterprise SaaS, or a fast-growing startup.

 - Strong preference for candidates with prior corporate/enterprise experience and exposure to complex stakeholder environments.

 - Experience leading teams and driving execution through others.

 - Strong ability to structure ambiguous problems and turn them into clear, executable plans.

 - Excellent communication and presentation skills - comfortable presenting to CXOs and senior enterprise stakeholders.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving ability; you can work with data to understand what is happening and why.

 - Strong project and stakeholder management skills.

 - Ability to operate across business, technology, and customer-facing teams without needing a predefined playbook.

 - High ownership and bias towards execution - you take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly.

GOOD TO HAVE

 - Experience in B2B SaaS, AI, Voice AI, Conversational AI, or technology deployments.

 - Experience managing or mentoring FDEs, consultants, solution engineers, implementation teams, or customer success teams.

 - Experience working with large enterprise customers and complex deployment environments.

 - Exposure to enterprise sales, solution consulting, or pre-sales.

 - Experience building processes or playbooks from scratch.

 - Consulting experience from a top-tier consulting firm is a plus.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In this role, success means:

 - Enterprise deployments launch on time and with high quality.

 - Customers achieve measurable business outcomes from their Bolna deployments.

 - FDEs operate with increasing ownership, speed, and technical/business depth.

 - Enterprise escalations are resolved quickly and systematically.

 - Deployment processes become increasingly repeatable and scalable.

 - Customer insights translate into meaningful improvements across Product and Engineering.

 - Strategic enterprise accounts expand because of the outcomes delivered.

WHY BOLNA

 - Work directly with some of India’s largest enterprises and solve high-impact business problems.

 - Lead a team operating at the intersection of AI, technology, and enterprise business.

 - High ownership and visibility - your work directly impacts customer outcomes and company growth.

 - Work closely with founders and senior leadership on strategic enterprise initiatives.

 - Build the playbook for deploying Voice AI at enterprise scale.

 - Competitive compensation + meaningful ESOPs.

 - Delhi office with a highly collaborative, in-person working environment.

jobs.title: Key Account Manager
jobs.description:
CAN YOU HELP US FIX THE WORLD'S MOST BROKEN SUPPLY CHAIN?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo, turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. In July 2026 we closed our Series B, led by Burda Principal Investments with participation from eBay and FJ Labs, alongside existing backers a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, plus angels who helped build Depop, Shopify and Postmates.

Today, we connect suppliers across India, Pakistan and Dubai with roughly 50,000 retailers and resellers in 100+ countries. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters and move fast doing it. Sound good? Keep reading.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Key Account Manager to grow Fleek's vendor and seller base in India. You'll sit in our Supply team, reporting to our Supply Lead and own a portfolio of India's most important vendor accounts end to end: finding them, signing them, onboarding them and scaling them.

India is one of Fleek's most important supply markets and this role is the engine of its growth. You'll build a portfolio of key accounts, put milllions of dollars of healthy inventory on the platform every month and drive India toward its goals in monthly marketplace GMV.

This is a hunting role as much as a farming one. The best vendors in India aren't waiting in an inbox: they're in godowns, wholesale markets and aggregator networks and you'll go find them.

WHY THIS ROLE STANDS OUT

Most account management jobs hand you a book of existing clients and a renewal target. This one hands you a market. India's used-clothing trade is enormous and almost entirely offline, and every vendor you bring onto Fleek is inventory that 50,000 buyers in 100+ countries can suddenly see and order.

You'll own real commercial outcomes early: negotiating pricing, commission and payout terms, deciding which accounts to scale and writing the playbooks that the whole India supply org will run on as it grows. Your numbers will be visible to the whole company.

And you'll do it AI-native. FleekSort and our internal tools automate the grunt work of cataloguing and account management, so your time goes into relationships and growth, not spreadsheets.

WHAT MAKES YOU A FLEEK KEY ACCOUNT MANAGER?

 - Hunter: You proactively source and close new accounts rather than waiting for inbound and you get a kick out of the chase.

 - Relationship Builder: You're equally credible with a small boutique seller and a large aggregator and you build trust that lasts beyond the first deal.

 - Commercial Negotiator: Pricing, commission and payout terms don't scare you. You find the structure that works for the vendor and for Fleek.

 - AI-Native: You reach for AI tools to automate and scale your workflows by default and you're excited to work somewhere that runs that way.

 - Bias for Action: You're comfortable in a fast-moving, ambiguous startup environment and would rather ship an imperfect first version than wait for a perfect plan.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Hunt and close key accounts: Build a portfolio of vendor accounts, each averaging $35K+ in monthly GMV, by proactively sourcing aggregators, godowns and quality sellers across India.

 - Own onboarding and activation: Take new vendors from first conversation to live, healthy catalog on the platform, fast.

 - Grow catalog depth and quality: Drive healthy inventory onto the platform every month, growing over 20% month on month, with listing quality and freshness to match.

 - Drive GMV: Grow India's contribution in healthy monthly marketplace GMV, growing 30% month on month.

 - Improve retention and performance: Manage account health hand in hand with vendors, bringing cancellation rates down.

 - Deepen share of wallet: Strengthen relationships across your portfolio so Fleek captures a growing share of each vendor's inventory.

 - Build the playbooks: Turn what works into repeatable onboarding and scaling playbooks for the India vendor base.

 - Automate your workflows: Use AI tools to scale account management, reporting and vendor communication, so you can run a bigger book than a traditional KAM ever could.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3 to 5 years in key account management, vendor or seller management, or B2B growth. Ideally in a marketplace, e-commerce or D2C business.

 - A proven track record of growing a supply-side or seller base. You've onboarded, activated and scaled sellers and can talk through the numbers.

 - Commercial negotiation experience. You've negotiated pricing, commission or payout terms directly with vendors or sellers.

 - A working understanding of catalog and inventory operations. Listing quality, SKU management and product categorisation aren't foreign concepts.

 - An AI-first mindset. You already use AI tools to work faster and want to get better at it.

 - Structured communication. You can report account health clearly and escalate issues to Ops, Supply and Product

jobs.title: Strategic GTM, Principal
jobs.description:
STRATEGIC GTM, PRINCIPAL

New York City · On-site

THE VOICE AI WORKFORCE FOR HEALTHCARE

Healthcare runs on phone calls and loses $450B a year to the administration around them. Patients wait on hold, staff spend hours calling insurers, and revenue leaks at every handoff.

At Prosper, we're building the AI workforce that runs healthcare operations end to end. Our voice AI agents answer patient calls, schedule appointments directly in the EHR, verify insurance benefits, automate billing, and get payors on the phone when humans would otherwise wait on hold. We've grown revenue 5x in the last year, partnered with 100+ healthcare organizations covering more than 150,000 providers, and raised $35M, including a $30M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a Strategic Account Principal to own a segment of the largest provider organizations in the country: national MSOs, PE-backed platform groups, and multi-region specialty organizations.

Think of it as running a business rather than working a patch. You'll own the segment the way a GM would. You decide how it's defined, which organizations belong in it, what the thesis is for winning each one, and what Prosper has to build, say, and do to get there. Then you go make it happen: a named account list you built yourself, run from first touch to signature, with marketing, product, solutions, and the founders working against the plan you set.

Prosper is at an inflection point. Revenue is up 5x on a lean sales team. It's early enough that the strategy is yours to write, and consequential enough that writing it well changes the trajectory of the company.

If you've spent years building strategy for other people's businesses, this is the version where you own the thesis, run the execution, and see the number move. This is the best opportunity for someone who wants a path to be a founder or learn the entrepreneurial joruney

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own a segment of the market

 - Build the strategy from a blank page: market map, account segmentation, prioritization logic, and a defensible point of view on where Prosper wins and why

 - Construct the named account list, a finite and deliberately chosen set of organizations, along with the entry hypothesis for each one

 - Set the commercial architecture for the segment: pricing posture, pilot design, and land-and-expand paths from a single site or specialty to the full organization

 - Bring the rest of GTM with you. Marketing, outbound, solutions, and product should be executing against your plan, not adjacent to it. You'll define the campaigns, content, and product priorities the segment needs and drive them cross-functionally

Run the outcome of the deals

 - Own long-cycle, multi-stakeholder deals end to end: account planning, prospecting, discovery, pilot, negotiation, and close

 - Build durable relationships with the people who decide. The best strategic sellers are trusted before they're needed. You'll invest in multi-year relationships with CFOs, COOs, CIOs, and VPs of Revenue Cycle, arriving with a point of view on their business rather than a pitch

 - Multi-thread across revenue cycle, finance, IT, security, compliance, clinical operations, and procurement, and hold every thread yourself

 - Author the ROI case. Every strategic deal at Prosper is won on a quantified business case: cost-to-collect, denial rate, days in A/R, FTE hours redeployed, cash recovered. You'll build these models from the customer's own data and defend them in front of a CFO

 - Navigate the enterprise gauntlet of RFPs, security reviews, HIPAA and BAA diligence, legal negotiation, and phased multi-site rollouts without losing momentum

Build the playbook

 - Codify what works into an outreach strategy, business-case templates, and qualification criteria the next five hires on this team will run

 - Feed the top of the market back into roadmap, and turn roadmap into commercial advantage

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MBB or top-tier strategy consulting experience (McKinsey, Bain, BCG) is strongly preferred, specificially, 6-10 years of experience. You've demonstrated you can take an unstructured market, break it into a defensible framework, and turn that into a prioritized plan to execute, and iterate on

 - Relationship-building as a core competency. You build trust with senior operators over years, and people who've worked with you once seek you out again. You can win a room of C-suite executives and excel at building trust and product knowledge

 - Entrepreneurial eagerness. You're eager to build, comfortable getting in the mud, and just as comfortable stepping back to decide what actually deserves your time. If you want to find the ceiling of what you're capable of, or build a billion dollar company of your own one day, this is where you learn how
 
 

BONUS POINTS

 - Healthcare or PE/provider-services practice experience in consulting

 - Experience selling AI, automation, or voice technology into regulated industries

 - Fluency with EHR and practice management ecosystems (Epic, athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks) and clearinghouse/RCM stacks

 - An existing network across provider group leadership or PE-backed provider platforms

 - Early-stage or hypergrowth startup background

WHY PROSPER

 - A trillion-dollar problem, real customers, and revenue growing 5x

 - A segment you own outright: the strategy, the accounts, and the number

 - Direct access to founders, product, and engineering. Deals get unblocked in hours

 - Competitive base, commission, and meaningful equity

jobs.description:

At Inscribe, we're on a mission to catch fraud with confidence. In 2017, we set out to build the first document fraud detection product. Today, we process millions of applications each year and work with many of the leading fintechs and banks across the U.S. We believe the game of cat-and-mouse in fraud requires a fundamentally new approach. With care for our customers, attention to detail, and grounded execution, we’re reimagining how fraud is detected and prevented.

Inscribe is trusted by leading banks and fintechs, including Coinbase, Plaid, Bluevine, and Ramp. Inscribe is backed by Threshold Ventures, Uncork Capital, Y Combinator, Crosslink Capital, and Foundry, and is headquartered in San Francisco, CA.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Inscribe is seeking our first dedicated Partnerships Lead to build and scale a partner-sourced revenue channel. You will be a core member of our GTM team, working across Sales, Product, Product Marketing, and Legal to source, close, and grow partnerships across our four models: referral, white-label, reseller, and integration. You'll own the partner relationship end to end, from first conversation through signature through ongoing enablement and support. This is a high impact role with the mandate to build partnerships into a repeatable, quota-carrying revenue motion. The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo, turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. In July 2026 we closed our Series B, led by Burda Principal Investments with participation from eBay and FJ Labs, alongside existing backers a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, plus angels who helped build Depop, Shopify and Postmates.

Today, we connect suppliers across India, Pakistan and Dubai with roughly 50,000 retailers and resellers in 100+ countries. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

You'll be the person who brings it online, backed by a marketplace with 50,000 buyers in 100+ countries pulling demand through everything you source.

This isn't a caretaker GM role.  - P&L Owner: You think in revenue, margin and unit economics by default, and you're comfortable being held to a hard commercial number.

 - AI-Native: You personally build or run repeatable automations, and you push your team to work the same way. AI is how you operate, not a slide in your deck.

 - Ground-Level Operator: You're as comfortable on a warehouse floor in Panipat as in a board review and you know the metrics that make warehousing, QC and logistics tick.

 - Shape-Shifter: In a single day you can be a salesperson winning a supplier, an operator fixing a fulfilment issue and a customer-experience owner obsessing over a buyer complaint, and be equally credible in all three.
 
 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the India P&L: Scale India's supply engine into a $30M+ business by 2028, sized against the roughly 9,000 containers of used clothing landing in India each year.

 - Deepen supply: Grow the inventory value our existing Panipat and Kandla suppliers contribute over time, measured through Net Dollar Retention of supplier inventory acquisition.

 - Broaden supply: Build toward 1,000+ quality suppliers by strengthening Panipat and Kandla and standing up sourcing in other high-potential Indian markets.

 - Turn suppliers into a social engine: Get Indian suppliers ready for video handpicks and chat-based selling, backed by ongoing seller education and tracked through Seller NPS.

 - Protect the buyer experience: Build a base of vetted, quality sellers and deliver a great experience for Fleek's global buyers, measured through fulfilment rate and cancellation rate.

 - Launch the liquidation bet: Stand up and scale factory leftover stock, sourced with brand licensing to resell, as a distinct new business line.

 - Build the India org: Grow the team beyond today's baseline (QC and operations staff, a Senior Supply Manager and a supply KAM) into the structure needed to run all of the above.

 - Run an AI-native operation: Automate the repeatable parts of supply, QC and seller management, and hold the whole India team to the same standard.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 7 to 10+ years of relevant experience, based in Delhi NCR. This is an on-the-ground leadership role, not a remote one.

 - A proven market-launch track record. You've built and scaled t

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Evals & Post-Training)
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO

Ambral Labs helps enterprises own the intelligence behind their most important workflows.

Every company has years of historical evidence showing how work gets done: the context people had, the decisions they made, the actions they took, and the outcomes that followed. Today, most of that history is inert. It isn’t structured in a way that companies can use to evaluate models and improve agent behavior.

Ambral turns this history into replayable environments and eval sets grounded in real workflows and observed outcomes. We use those environments to improve model performance through reinforcement learning and other post-training techniques, alongside context engineering, harness design, and agent engineering.

The result is better, more cost-efficient AI for each enterprise’s specific work, powered by open-weight models that the company owns and controls. This allows each company to retain ownership of its core intelligence instead of outsourcing it to a model provider.

We graduated from YC S2025, raised millions in funding, and are already deployed within multi-billion dollar enterprises. Now we're growing the founding team

 

What you’ll do

At the center of Ambral Labs is a replayable environment engine for the enterpirse.

The system reconstructs a company’s world as it existed at a particular moment in the past then exposes that state through the same tools an agent would use in production. This lets us place new policies and agent configurations inside real historical environments, observe how they reason and act, and grade their performance against real outcomes.

You'll work across research, infrastructure, and production systems including:

 - Building an environment factory that converts recorded enterprise data and task definitions into runnable environments

 - Designing graders that turn ambiguous business objectives into verifiable rewards

 - Developing methods for mining useful tasks, trajectories, and evaluation cases from historical workflows

 - Creating eval sets that are representative, reproducible, and resistant to overfitting

 - Finding the right combinations of models, tools, context, and policies to maximize performance while reducing inference cost

 - Training and evaluating agents that operate over long horizons, incomplete information, and large tool spaces

 - Building replay and observability systems that make agent behavior explainable and measurable

 - Scaling from individual environments to thousands of concurrent training and evaluation runs

These problems are wide open. You’ll have significant ownership over both the research direction and the production systems that make it real.

You’ll work directly with the CTO, deploy into real enterprise workflows, and see your research tested against consequential problems and observable outcomes.

 

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 1-7 years of experience building production software or machine-learning systems (we're hiring at multiple levels for this role).

 - Bonus points for working on reinforcement-learning environments, LLM post-training, evaluation infrastructure, agent harnesses, or closely related systems

 - You understand how environment design, reward design, context, tooling, and policy behavior interact

 - You’re comfortable turning fuzzy business objectives into tasks and signals that can be evaluated reliably

 - You can diagnose whether a model’s limitations come from the model itself, its context, its tools, its harness, or its training

 - You can move between research questions and production implementation without treating them as separate jobs

 - You write strong software and can build systems that process large, messy datasets at scale

 - You care about reproducibility, observability, and understanding why a model behaves the way it does

 - You’re looking to do the best work of your life and build something you’ll be proud of for decades

We care much more about what you’ve built and how you think than credentials or conventional career paths.

BENEFITS

 - Significant equity and ownership

 - Equinox membership

 - Free meals, coffee, and snacks

 - Health insurance

 - Unlimited PTO

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - CRM (USA Only, 100% Remote)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Since 2013, we’ve been building a CRM that gets out of your way and helps your team sell more, faster. Now we’re building AI into every part of it, so Close does the busywork and your team does the selling. No manual data entry, no 10-click workflows. Just communication-first, AI-powered sales software designed to help you succeed and scale.

We're bootstrapped and profitable which means we answer to our customers and play by our rules. We're proud of our 130-person, 100% remote team, focused on building Close so that no small, scaling business fails because it can't figure out sales.

 

OUR STACK

Our backend tech stack consists primarily of Python Flask web apps with our TaskTiger https://github.com/closeio/tasktiger scheduler handling many of the backend asynchronous task processing chores. Our data stores include MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and Redis. The underlying infrastructure runs on AWS using a combination of managed services like EKS, MSK, RDS and ElastiCache and non-managed services running on EC2 instances. We have CI/CD pipelines that build Docker images, run automated tests and deploy to Kubernetes clusters. We also use these images in our local development environment allowing coding locally against all of our services. We have a well-documented public API https://developer.close.com/ that is consumed by our front-end JavaScript app as well as numerous integrations. Our infrastructure is heavily automated using Terraform, Ansible and other AWS tools. 

We love open sourcing our code and ideas on our GitHub https://github.com/closeio and on The Making of Close https://making.close.com/, our behind-the-scenes Product & Engineering blog. Check out our open source projects like SocketShark https://github.com/closeio/socketshark, TaskTiger https://github.com/closeio/tasktiger, LimitLion https://github.com/closeio/limitlion and ciso8601 https://github.com/closeio/ciso8601.

AI is both how we build and what we ship, and that's reshaped what engineering looks like. This is a transformation we’re embracing and find deeply exciting. 

ABOUT THE ROLE

The CRM team owns everything that Close’s customers touch all day, every day: leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, activities, custom objects, and search. Each time a call is logged, an email is threaded, a meeting is summarized, it lands on the record this team owns, and every agent we ship starts there.

Today, this team is making big moves towards the next iteration of Close's core data model, our largest engineering effort currently underway. We're reopening assumptions made a decade ago and asking what a modern CRM's data model should look like — one that makes Close flexible for our small, scaling business customers. This is a long series of migrations and rearchitecture projects. If you like greenfield and you like hairy, this is both: help design the next version of Close, and untangle the current one.

One thing to know: we do move people between teams as the work shifts. Most engineers here end up on more than one team over their time at Close — this team is where you'd start, but over time you'll likely have the opportunity to work on many different projects.

YOU ARE

 - A seasoned engineer. Python is our backbone, but perhaps you've worked across Go, Rust, or TypeScript. You pick the right tool for the workload rather than retreating to what you know.

 - Architecturally minded. This is the thing we care about most. You've designed systems others built on, planned a migration that couldn't take the product down, and know how to sequence a rearchitecture into pieces that ship independently.

 - Drawn to data model and retrieval problems. Schemas, relationships, normalization, query design, type systems. The plumbing decides whether a CRM feels fast and we pride ourselves on being fast.

 - Experienced in search — this is a serious bonus. Elasticsearch especially, and anything adjacent: Lucene internals, query planning, relevance, indexing at scale, building or operating a search engine.

 - AI-native in production. You've shipped meaningful LLM-backed or agentic features to real users, and you have a POV on where AI earns its place in a CRM workflow and where a structured system wins.

 - Working with AI in your day-to-day. You use AI tools in your own workflow to ship faster, write tighter code, and reason about unfamiliar parts of the codebase. We fund best-in-class developer tools and treat experimentation as part of the work.

 - Battle-tested. You've debugged incidents where latency budgets didn't hold, owned a system everyone else relied on, or carried a pager for something with real customer impact.

 - A builder first. You'd rather get a sloppy v1 in front of fifty customers than spend three weeks on abstractions. You ship.

YOU WILL

 - Rearchitect the core CRM data model. Rework how leads, contacts, opportunities, and custom objects relate to each other so each of our customers can represent their business the way it operates.

 - Make Close usable by agents. The Agents team builds the MCP foundation; we build the tools and endpoints on top of it that expose the CRM's data and actions. The hard part is search: any MCP-compatible harness should be able to traverse, filter, and reason over a customer's CRM without learning our private query language first.

 - Ship AI-native CRM features. This team built agentic enrichment: instead of paying a third-party data provider, an agent goes and researches whatever field you need, in bulk or automatically inside a workflow. There's a lot more of this ahead, including AI-powered data cleaning and richer AI search.

 - Keep the hot paths fast. Finding a lead, updating a deal, scanning a pipeline, running a bulk action. Salespeople do these hundreds of times a week and no amount of clever architecture matters if they're slow.

Tech you'll touch: Python, Flask, FastAPI, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Redis, TaskTiger, MCP — plus whichever LLM ships nex

This role is open at the Senior and Staff levels. You don't need to pick one when you apply: we'll calibrate together during the process.

YOU ARE

 - A seasoned Python engineer. Python is our backbone and it matters in this role more than on other teams at Close. Architectural patterns don't port cleanly between languages, and you'll be setting the patterns. Go, Rust, or TypeScript alongside it is welcome.

 - Drawn to meta-problems. This team doesn't ship features to customers; it changes how features get built.

 - AI-native in production. You've shipped meaningful LLM-backed or agentic work to real users. For a team building AI tooling that other engineers depend on, this is foundational to the role.

 - Working with AI in your day-to-day. You use coding agents in your own workflow and have a real POV on where they help and where they get in the way. On this team, your POV becomes the product. We fund best-in-class developer tools and treat experimentation as part of the work.

 - Fluent in observability and production practice. Telemetry, metrics, tracing, alerting, Sentry ownership, what production-ready actually means. You've been the person who made a system legible when it broke.

 - Opinionated about API design. You've shipped internet-facing APIs and you think about who's on the other end — apps, agents, humans reading docs — and what each needs.

 - Battle-tested. You've debugged incidents where latency budgets didn't hold, owned a system everyone else relied on, or carried a pager for something with real customer impact.

 - A builder first. You'd rather get a rough v1 in front of five engineers than spend three weeks on abstractions.

 - Energized by internal customers. Your users are a Slack DM away. You'll talk to them directly instead of through a PM, and you'll use most of what you build yourself.

YOU WILL

 - Expand DevDawg and Spice. Cloud development environments for our full stack, paired with automated review and root-cause tooling that can approve real pull requests. Making that safe enough to cover more of our review surface is one of the team's biggest projects.

 - Build the paved roads for our API layer. REST blueprints, GraphQL schema

jobs.title: Head of Research
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO

Ambral Labs helps enterprises own the intelligence behind their most important workflows.

Every company has years of historical evidence showing how work gets done: the context people had, the decisions they made, the actions they took, and the outcomes that followed. Today, most of that history is inert. It isn’t structured in a way that companies can use to evaluate models and improve agent behavior.

Ambral turns this history into replayable environments and eval sets grounded in real workflows and observed outcomes. We use those environments to improve model performance through reinforcement learning and other post-training techniques, alongside context engineering, harness design, and agent engineering.

The result is better, more cost-efficient AI for each enterprise’s specific work, powered by open-weight models that the company can own and control rather than permanently renting from a model provider.

We're YC S2025 , have raised millions in funding, and are already deployed inside multi-billion dollar enterprises. Now we're growing the founding team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

We’re building a replayable environment engine over real enterprise history.

The system reconstructs a company’s context as it existed at any past time, then exposes that state through the same tools an agent would use in production. This lets us place new policies and agent configurations inside real historical environments, observe how they reason and act, and grade their performance against real outcomes.

As Head of Research, you'll own the research agenda required to make that possible. You'll identify the highest-leverage technical questions, design the experiments needed to answer them, and remain deeply hands-on in building the systems that turn those answers into production.

Some of the problems you'll work on:

 - Building an environment factory that converts recorded enterprise data and task definitions into runnable environments

 - Designing graders that turn ambiguous business objectives into verifiable rewards

 - Developing methods for mining useful tasks, trajectories, and evaluation cases from historical workflows

 - Creating eval sets that are representative, reproducible, and resistant to overfitting

 - Finding the right combinations of models, tools, context, and policies to maximize performance while reducing inference cost

 - Advancing post-training methods for agents that operate over long horizons, incomplete information, and large tool spaces

 - Building replay and observability systems that make agent behavior explainable and measurable

 - Scaling from individual environments to thousands of concurrent training and evaluation runs

These problems are wide open. You’ll have significant ownership over both the research direction and the production systems that make it real.

You’ll work directly with the CTO, deploy into real enterprise workflows, and see your research tested against consequential problems and observable outcomes. 

You'll also help establish the research culture at Ambral Labs: how we run experiments, evaluate progress, choose technical bets, and recruit and develop an exceptional research team. 

WHO YOU ARE

You'll likely thrive here if:

 - You have a PhD in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or an equivalent track record of significant research experience

 - You have deep experience in reinforcement learning, LLM post-training, evals, agent environments, or closely related areas

 - You've taken ambitious, open-ended research problems from hypothesis through experimentation into working systems 

 - You’re comfortable turning fuzzy business objectives into tasks and signals that can be evaluated reliably

 - You can move between research questions and production implementation without treating them as separate jobs

 - You’re looking to do the best work of your life and build something you’ll be proud of for decades

We’re especially interested in candidates who have worked at a leading foundation model lab, top AI research organization, or high-performing AI startup.

BENEFITS

 - Significant equity and ownership

 - Equinox membership

 - Free meals, coffee, and snacks

 - Health insurance

 - Unlimited PTO

jobs.title: Scriptwriter
jobs.description:
LA MISSION DE FINARY

Notre mission : rendre le pouvoir aux investisseurs. Le bon conseil financier a toujours existé, mais il était réservé à ceux qui dépassaient un certain seuil de patrimoine. Nous changeons la donne en construisant la plateforme d'investissement tout-en-un, propulsée par l'IA : suivre ses actifs, gérer son budget, investir et se former, au même endroit. Une idée simple et ambitieuse nous guide : mettre un banquier privé dans la poche de chacun.

Mounir https://www.linkedin.com/in/mounirlaggoune a lancé Finary en 2021, et plus d'un million de personnes nous confient aujourd'hui leur vie financière. Nous lançons des produits de pointe avec une touche de plaisir, et nous sommes exigeants sur l'expérience, la performance et la simplicité.

 

POURQUOI MAINTENANT ?

Une nouvelle génération d'investisseurs émerge : ambitieuse, impliquée, débarrassée des tabous autour de l'argent. Nous croyons en un monde où investir permet à chacun de vivre la vie dont il a toujours rêvé. Pour accélérer, nous avons levé 40M€ auprès de Hedosophia, Y Combinator et Speedinvest, aux côtés de fondateurs et d'opérateurs comme Steve Anavi et Alexandre Prot (Qonto), Matthieu Rouif (Photoroom), Eric Demuth (Bitpanda), Axel Weber (ancien président d'UBS) et Harsh Sinha (CTO de Wise).

En juillet 2026, l'AMF nous a accordé l'agrément MiCA, qui s'ajoute à notre agrément d'Entreprise d'Investissement : nous sommes l'une des très rares plateformes françaises à détenir les deux, avec actions, ETF et crypto réunis sur une seule plateforme régulée, au moment même où l'Europe se consolide autour des acteurs agréés. Il n'y a jamais eu de meilleur moment pour nous rejoindre.

 

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

Nous sommes 70 builders qui aimons profondément ce que nous faisons : de vraies responsabilités dès le premier jour, un package salaire et equity au meilleur niveau du marché, des bureaux en plein cœur de Paris avec du remote hybride, et des offsites trimestriels qu'on attend vraiment.

Nous recrutons des A-players aussi bienveillants qu'exigeants, des personnes dont les idées transforment notre produit autant que notre façon de travailler et de penser. Notre culture est directe et transparente : on se challenge ouvertement, puis on s'aligne et on exécute. Et sur l'IA, pas de demi-mesure : c'est la compétence la plus importante de la décennie et un vrai critère chez nous. Chacun a repensé sa manière de travailler autour d'elle. Si c'est déjà une seconde nature pour vous, vous trouverez ici des gens qui repoussent cette frontière chaque jour.

Découvrez nos valeurs ici https://app.notion.com/p/About-Finary-2f5919045b5d8060afd1d4e887ac550f?pvs=21.

---

LE POSTE

Finary construit la banque privée de la génération internet. Notre chaîne YouTube est la première chaîne de finances personnelles en France : 880 000 abonné·es et 5 à 10 millions de vues par mois, entièrement produite en interne par une équipe qui traite le contenu comme un produit, c’est-à-dire mesuré, itéré, conçu avec méthode.

Tu prends en charge tout ce qui s’écrit chez Finary Media, de bout en bout : recherche, script, packaging, vérification des faits, livraison. Les mots t’appartiennent, de la première idée au montage final.

Tes deux terrains de jeu principaux :

 - La chaîne YouTube Finary. Des vidéos longues qui mêlent storytelling, économie et investissement, regardées par des centaines de milliers de personnes. Ton point de repère : nos meilleures vidéos dépassent le million de vues.

 - Finary One. Le contenu de notre offre de gestion de patrimoine, destiné à des investisseur·ses averti·es disposant de plus d’un million d’euros de patrimoine. C’est l’écriture aux enjeux les plus élevés chez Finary : moins de vues, mais des conséquences bien plus importantes.

Tu écris aussi pour tous les formats qui gravitent autour : la préparation du podcast Finary Talk, et tout ce qui a besoin de mots. Si c’est écrit et que ça compte, c’est pour toi.

Deux éléments distinguent ce poste de tout autre métier de scénariste :

 - Tu passes devant la caméra. Tu présentes toi-même tes scripts. Ce n’est pas une option, cela fait partie du métier ici.

 - Tu travailles nativement avec l’IA. Notre système de production repose sur des workflows LLM, des skills sur mesure et de l’automatisation. Tu ne te contenteras pas d’utiliser ces outils, tu construiras les tiens. La personne idéale pour ce poste a déjà construit des choses : prompts, agents, bases de connaissances, petits scripts.

À QUOI RESSEMBLE LA RÉUSSITE

 - Une de tes vidéos dépasse le million de vues dans tes trois premiers mois

 - À partir du troisième mois, ton contenu Finary One génère 100 M€ d’encours prospects chaque mois

 - 90 % de tes scripts sont validés en un seul tour de relecture, et tes délais de production baissent

TU ES FAIT·E POUR CE POSTE SI TU AS

 - Une maîtrise experte de l’investissement et des finances personnelles : tu peux aller en profondeur, sans notes, sur le private equity, l’immobilier, les enveloppes fiscales et la structuration patrimoniale

 - Une expérience d’écriture éprouvée face à un vrai public (YouTube, presse, newsletter, blog), avec des résultats à montrer

 - Une rigueur factuelle sans faille : aucune erreur de données, de chiffres ou de concepts, jamais

 - La concision comme réflexe, à l’écrit comme à l’oral

 - Une autonomie totale : tu gères ton propre système, tu tiens tes délais, et personne n’a besoin de te relancer

 - Une pratique native de l’IA : tu construis avec les LLM et l’automatisation parce que c’est ta façon de penser

 - De l’aisance face caméra, ou l’envie d’y arriver vite

LES PLUS

 - Tu as écrit pour des chaînes YouTube performantes, ou tu as la tienne

 - Un parcours en finance, en gestion d’actifs ou dans la fintech

 - Tu as mené seul·e un petit projet de code, une skill Claude ou un pipeline d’automatisation

Entretiens

Les entretiens avec les candidat·es francophones se déroulent en français. En tant qu’entreprise internationale, nous

jobs.description:
ABOUT ARTIE

Artie is a fully-managed real-time data streaming platform that replicates production databases into data warehouses and lakes - in real time, with zero maintenance. We make high-volume data replication simple, reliable, and scalable for engineering teams.

Our platform powers mission-critical use cases including fraud and risk monitoring, inventory visibility, customer-facing analytics, and AI/ML workloads.

We’re trusted by teams like Substack, Alloy, and ClickUp, and raised a Series A from top-tier investors including Standard Capital, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Pathlight, and the founders of Dropbox and Mode.

Artie is built for engineers who care about performance, reliability, and operational simplicity - and we’re growing fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Solutions Engineer to help scale Artie's pre-sales and post-sales enterprise motion.

This is not a demo-delivery role. You'll go deep with customers on their data architectures, run tight proof-of-value engagements, and be the technical backbone of every enterprise deal. You'll work directly with founders, shape how we position Artie technically, and set the bar for how we win.

If your background is engineering that never got to touch the business, this is the role where it finally does. If it's been RevOps where you were quietly the most technical person in the org and nobody ever let you build properly, same.

We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. A company moving this fast catches its own mistakes sooner with the whole team in one room, thinking out loud at a whiteboard.

This will probably be one of the harder jobs you've had. It should also be one of the more interesting ones, because the revenue problems you'll be solving here will be the catalyst for our continued hyper growth.

Excited? Good, we are too!

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales, built across Hyperbound Practice (AI roleplay), Hyperbound Perform (real call scoring and coaching), and Kota, our AI agent that acts on what we find. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.

Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23), we're around 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

You'll build the systems the go-to-market org runs on: lead routing and enrichment, pipeline and forecasting tooling, scoring and deal-desk workflows, and the data layer that ties it all into one source of truth. Where a no-code tool is genuinely the right call, use it; the bar is that you can build the real thing when that's what the job needs.

There's a part of this job most GTM engineers never get. You'll dogfood Hyperbound on Hyperbound: our own reps run on Practice, Perform, and Kota, so the internal systems you build plug straight into the product we sell, and what you learn building them feeds back into the roadmap. You'll work closely with the founders and GTM leadership, act as part engineer and part systems designer for the revenue org, and have real say in what we build, not just how.

We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and hunters. We've hired from our competition, brought on former founders, and pulled in early customers who loved the product enough to come build it.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Post-Training & Applied Research
jobs.description:
AT SF TENSOR, WE'RE BUILDING THE FUTURE OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTE

We firmly believe that the future of AI depends on the unglamorous: rethinking and rebuilding the stack, all the way down. From the hardware underneath it to the compiler targeting it and the cloud running it. Right now those three things fight each other and that friction shows up as a tax on every researcher trying to build something ambitious. We're here to axe that tax and make compute faster, cheaper and more available. When we succeed, compute will be portable enough that "which cloud, which chip" stop being something you worry about.

To achieve this, we are building our Kernel Optimizer, which takes code and finds its fastest possible form for whatever vendor and cluster topology you point it at, automatically, as well as the Model Foundry which manages the runs, makes research easier and moves workloads across clouds and chips as prices and availability ship, instead of leaving you locked into whatever vendor you signed with first.

We're backed by Susa Ventures, Y Combinator, along with some great funds and angels including Max Mullen and Paul Graham, as well as founders and executives at Neuralink, Notion and AMD. We're looking for researchers, engineers and organizations who agree with the basic premise: you don't get the next leap in AI without a leap in compute first.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We build the fastest GPU compiler in the world. Most compilers have to preserve correctness at every transform, constraining how far they can search, while we prove correctness at the end instead, allowing us to search a far wider space, with agents, with RL, with anything that works and still guarantee the result. It's why we hold #1 on NVIDIA's own kernel benchmark across hundreds of production kernels.

Speed at the kernel layer is only worth what we do with it though and our enterprise offering promises we'll turn a customer's dataset into a specialist model in days. To do that we run SFT, RL, DPO, design evals and distillation down to smaller and edge-deployable models. We're hiring a Member of Technical Staff to own the modeling side of that end to end.

The infrastructure you'll be working on top of is unusually strong, which is the only reason we're able to train models so fast. Every experiment goes through Model Foundry, which let's you run experiments on the best hardware, look at overviews or dive deep into any detail all in a versioned and reproducible manner, making it trivial to reuse and modify recipes. Underneath that is the most powerful engine you could ask for, which has been used to post-train multi-100B language parameter models on TPU, post-train robotics models on Trainium and pre-train AlphaFold v3 on AMD.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - You'll own the post-training pipeline end-to-end: data curation, SFT, preference optimization, RL, evals, distillation and finally deployment

 - You'll design reward functions and RL looks along customer domain experts, who know the task inside-out but not our training stack

 - You'll build an eval harness trustworthy enough to make a ship/no-ship call within a short window, especially where the target is subjective taste rather than a scored benchmark

 - You'll structure and generate datasets, including synthetic data pipelines, from whatever the customer actually has

 - You'll distill specialist models down into smaller models

 - You'll drive the time-to-model, which means finding what's actually on the critical path and removing it, run after run

 - You'll embed with customers as a forward-deployed researcher, then hand the pipeline over cleanly when their team is ready to take over

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Someone who's shipped post-trained models into production and can talk honestly about the tradeoffs

 - Someone with hands-on depth across SFT and RL (DPO, GRPO, PPO or similar)

 - Someone who can judge evaluation honestly: what to measure, what a result means and when a number is lying to you

 - Someone who's comfortable owning data: curation, filtering, labeling workflows and synthetic generation

 - Someone proficient in PyTorch or JAX

 - Someone willing to sit with customers' domain experts to turn their intuition into a reward function

NICE TO HAVE

 - You'll extend our sandboxing stack to new vendors and accelerators

 - You'll build and maintain GPU virtualization below the runtime, including gVisor work at the driver and ioctl level

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARINI

Arini is building the single platform to run all healthcare operations.

Healthcare has spent the last decade consolidating under large enterprises, but operations are still fragmented, manual, and expensive. A large group runs dozens of disconnected systems for scheduling, billing, insurance, accounts payable, and reporting, with people moving data between them by phone, fax, and spreadsheet.

Outpatient healthcare is a $650 billion market, and almost every dollar of it still runs on manual work. Consolidators bought thousands of clinics on the promise that scale would expand margins and lift their EBITDA multiple. Scale alone has not delivered it. Automation is now the only way to hit the numbers they promised investors, and Arini is how they get there.

We partner with some of the largest healthcare enterprises in the country, covering thousands of clinics and billions of dollars in annual revenue. We ship the systems that run their operations end to end, and the best of that work becomes the platform that scales across enterprises.

When operations run themselves, patients feel it: calls answered on the first ring, appointments booked in seconds, insurance sorted before they walk in, and clinicians who spend their day on care instead of paperwork. That is what we are building, for every clinic in the country.

We are backed by Y Combinator (W24) and on track to grow more than tenfold in 2026.

THE TEAM

Everyone at Arini ships code, including operators, growth, and customer leads. Our founders, Rami and Abdul, have worked together for over a decade. Rami studied computer science at MIT, Abdul at Harvard.

Everyone carries more than one job, and nobody has time for work that does not matter. If AI can do it, a person should not be doing it. We move extremely fast, take extreme ownership.

THE ROLE

You will build the platform that runs operations for the largest healthcare enterprises in the country. Our forward deployed engineers find the problems inside each customer. You build the systems that solve them once and run them everywhere: the integrations into practice management, billing, and payment systems, the agents that do the work, the data layer that makes an operation legible, and the infrastructure that keeps all of it running across thousands of clinics.

You own modules end to end: design, build, deploy, operate. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build the modules that run operations: scheduling, patient communication, insurance, accounts payable, reporting, and more.

 - Build integrations into enterprise healthcare systems: practice management, billing, payments, and vendors with no APIs.

 - Build and operate AI agents in production, with the evaluation, guardrails, and observability that let them take on work that matters.

 - Design the data models and pipelines that let an operation spanning thousands of locations be queried, monitored, and acted on.

 - Own reliability. You are on call for what you build, you find the root cause when it breaks.

FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Day 30: work alongside the engineer who owns a product line, and ship into it.

 - Day 60: write the plan for how you will own and build out a vertical of your own (e.g., insurance verification, outbound campaigns, etc.).

 - Day 90: own a product line end to end.

WHO YOU ARE

 - A strong generalist. You move between backend services, data, and the interfaces operators use. We work mostly in Python and TypeScript, on AWS and Cloudflare.

 - You have shipped and operated systems in production, and you have opinions about what went wrong and why.

 - You build with AI every day and expect the same from the people around you. If a model can do it, you do not do it by hand.

BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary with meaningful equity

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Lunch and dinner in the office

 - Unlimited PTO

jobs.description:
We’re building the next generation of employee benefits infrastructure.

At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.

Happl is backed by leading investors such as YCombinator, 6Degrees Capital, Haatch, Portage, and more, known for backing leading companies such as Deel, Rippling, Airbnb, Coinbase, Dropbox, and most recently was awarded a place in the UK’s top 100 startups for 2026.

About the role

As Financial Controller at Happl, you’ll own the financial engine of the business — everything from the cash in the bank to the numbers our board and investors use to make decisions runs through you. You’ll run the monthly close, the full revenue cycle, the compliance calendar across two jurisdictions, and our treasury position, and you’ll decide how all of it gets built, systemised, and automated.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role with a direct line to leadership. You won’t be managing a process someone else designed — you’ll be deciding what good looks like across revenue, cash, compliance, and reporting, then making it happen. We’re FCA-regulated and YCombinator-backed, having raised $11m to date, and we give global employers a single place to design, deliver, and manage benefits across 160+ countries and 70+ languages — which means the finance function behind the product has to be just as sharp as the product itself.  - Owning the cash position and treasury strategy — cash flow forecasting, working capital, FX management, and structuring how we hold company funds to earn a sensible return without taking risk we shouldn’t

 - Managing our outsourced bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners — holding them to deadlines and quality, and pulling work in-house where doing so makes us faster

 - Owning the finance tech stack and having a strong opinion on it, actively replacing manual work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across reconciliations, invoice processing, variance analysis, and reporting drafts

 - Leveraging AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to speed up your own work and build the systems that let finance scale without adding headcount

 - Acting as the financial conscience of the business, with a direct line to the founders and a real say in how we grow

What we’re looking for

 - Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA), or qualified by experience with a track record that stands up to scrutiny

 - Genuine ownership of a monthly close cycle and management reporting pack, start to finish

 - Strong technical grounding in revenue recognition, accruals accounting, and balance sheet control

 - Comfortable with tax and compliance across VAT, corporation tax, and payroll, ideally spanning both the UK and US

 - AI-native in your approach — you already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and can talk specifically about what you’ve automated and what it saved you

 - Exceptional attention to detail, alongside the judgement to know when precision matters and when speed does

 - A clear communicator — you can explain a number to a non-finance audience without patronising them or losing them

 - Ideally, SaaS or subscription business experience, particularly ARR reporting and deferred revenue, and familiarity with modern billing infrastructure like Xero or Stripe

jobs.title: GTM Engineer – Revenue Systems
jobs.description:
ABOUT WARP

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.

About the Role

We're looking for our first GTM Engineer to build the operational layer our entire revenue motion runs on. You'll own how our GTM stack is designed, connected, and scaled, from Salesforce architecture to the automation and AI layers on top of it. This is a high-impact IC role where you'll pioneer the GTM Engineering function at Warp, working directly with tenured GTM leaders who give you the context to build well and the independence to decide how.

GTM Engineering is an emerging discipline that blends software operations principles, Salesforce development, and systems design. We're looking for someone excited to build this function from the ground up and treat our GTM stack as a product that needs to be engineered, maintained, and improved over time.

What You'll Own

 - Revenue systems: Build the operational layer the whole revenue motion runs on, from Salesforce architecture to the automation and AI layers on top of it

 - Salesforce build: Design and build objects, flows, validation rules, reports, and dashboards that support GTM teams across the company

 - Cross-functional building: Serve as the primary Salesforce builder for Sales, Tech Partnerships, CX, Finance, and more, translating process needs into technical solutions

 - Workflow redesign: Partner with GTM leaders and frontline teams to understand how the revenue motion works today and where it breaks, then redesign and automate those workflows with better systems design and AI (ergo, cedar, sumble, gumloop, clay, claude)

 - Agentic systems: Build agents that run parts of the revenue motion, not just automate steps in it

 - Commissions and incentives: Build the systems that run commissions and incentive calculation, so payouts are accurate and questions resolve without manual digging

 - Data quality: Build the validation, governance, and structure that the rest of the GTM stack can rely on

 - Systems integration: Connect Salesforce to adjacent systems through APIs, webhooks, and automation layers, and own the GTM tooling that runs on top of it, adding and integrating new systems as the stack evolves

 - Reporting infrastructure: Build the reporting and forecasting infrastructure GTM leaders use to plan, so pipeline and revenue data is clean and trustworthy by design

 - Documentation and enablement: Document and enable what you build so the rest of the org can trust and extend it, not route through you

 - Build for scale: Design for where we're going, not one-off fixes, as we bring our org from 30 sellers to 100+

What We're Looking For

 - 2-5 years in Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, or Sales Ops at a B2B SaaS company

 - Hands-on Salesforce experience: building within it, not just configuring it (Flow, custom objects, validation rules, reports, dashboards)

 - Familiarity with GTM tech stack (Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Apollo, Chili Piper, Sales Navigator)

 - Track record of building processes and systems from scratch in a fast-growth environment

 - Strong attention to detail: data quality issues are painful for customers and for us

 - Comfortable working autonomously and making decisions with limited oversight

 - Proficiency in Google Sheets/Excel. Can juggle multiple workstreams, keep projects moving, and translate messy data into clear insights

Nice to Have

 - Hands-on ability with APIs, webhooks, and cross-system workflow design

 - Experience building in Clay, or with AI automation tooling (ergo, cedar, sumble, gumloop, claude)

 - Ability to build and problem solve with Python, JavaScript, SQL, SOQL, or TypeScript

 - Experience with business intelligence tools and SQL

 - Experience building and maintaining pipeline/forecast reporting for GTM leaders

 - Salesforce Administrator or Developer certification

BENEFITS AT WARP: 

 - 100% Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents.

 - 401(k) Matching: Start investing in your future from day one.

 - Flexible PTO: We offer uncapped flexible PTO, meaning you’re trusted to take the time you need to recharge while balancing your responsibilities and team commitments.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre-tax commuter benefits for your daily trip to our NYC office.

 - Catered Lunch Daily: Great food, every day, on us. No meal prep, no decision fatigue.

 - Quarterly Offsites: Beautiful locations to connect as a team. Past locations include Spain, Catskills, and San Francisco.

Warp is based in New York City, and most of our team works together in-office 5x per week. Please refer to the top of this page for this position's hiring location and working model.

jobs.title: Senior Account Executive Defense - Israel
jobs.description:
We’re looking for an Account Executive based in Israel to join our sales team and play a key role in growing Jiga’s defense and aerospace business.

THE OPPORTUNITY IN ISRAEL

Manufacturing capacity is at the centre of the conversation in defense. Demand is surging across defense systems, drones, aerospace, and space, while critical programs still lose valuable time waiting for custom parts.

The capacity exists across Israel and the global supply base. What’s missing is the coordination layer that finds and qualifies the right capacity, removes friction, and moves work across it with the speed, traceability, and accountability these programs require.

Jiga is building that layer. We route demand to the right manufacturers, operate as supplier of record with full traceability, and become a production arm for custom mechanical parts.

ABOUT JIGA

Jiga is the professional manufacturing platform that helps the world's best companies make their products. Companies source the mission-critical parts that help them launch satellites, build robotics, and strengthen national security.

We're a fast-growing Series A, Y Combinator backed company transforming how hardware companies build their supply chains. We have strong and proven product market fit, growing exponentially YoY. Teams at companies like NASA, Collins, Archer and Leidos use our platform to get high-quality custom parts faster.

THE ROLE

You’ll own a portfolio of Israeli defense and aerospace accounts—from defense primes and Tier 2/3 contractors to defense-tech companies. You’ll sell Jiga as a strategic manufacturing solution, including production contracts, capacity agreements, and supplier-of-record relationships, working with the people who own supply chain, procurement, operations, and program delivery.

You’ll build your named-account list, generate your own pipeline, run deals end to end, and work directly with Jiga’s leadership on deal structure and where we invest. Some opportunities will be urgent and high-stakes; others will require a longer enterprise motion. You’ll know how to navigate both while building trust and durable customer relationships.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a book of strategic Israeli defense and aerospace accounts end to end, from the first conversation to a signed contract and account expansion.

 - Sell Jiga as a solution to programs through production contracts, capacity agreements, and supplier-of-record relationships.

 - Navigate the Israeli defense ecosystem. Understand who holds budget and influence at primes, Tier 2/3 contractors, and defense-tech companies, how sourcing decisions are made, and how to get in the room.

 - Travel to defense industry events and customer sites to build relationships with supply chain, procurement, operations, and program leaders.

 - Understand each customer’s manufacturing and program-delivery challenges, demonstrate how Jiga solves them, and structure the right commercial solution.

 - Shape deal structure with leadership and help decide where Jiga should invest resources and capabilities.

 - Guide customers through their first orders and ensure a smooth onboarding experience.

 - Bring market insight back into the company and collaborate with marketing, supply chain, and product to improve our offering and customer experience.

YOU’RE A FIT IF YOU

 - Bring a strong, active network in Israel’s defense and aerospace ecosystem. You already know decision-makers across supply chain, procurement, operations, and program leadership—and can name the accounts you would open first.

 - Have 10+ years selling into or operating inside aerospace and defense manufacturing, including experience with primes, Tier 2/3 contractors, or defense-tech companies.

 - Have a demonstrated track record of closing complex, high-value production contracts or enterprise deals, and can explain exactly how you moved them from first conversation to signature.

 - Speak shop floor and quality requirements fluently: CNC machining, injection moulding, DFM, tolerances, materials, AS9100, first articles, traceability, source approval, and export-control requirements.

 - Generate your own pipeline. You’re comfortable building an account book without relying on inbound leads or heavy marketing support.

 - Are a go-getter with a “hunter” mentality - you’re comfortable doing outbound.

 - Are deeply service-oriented - you care about the customer's success as much as the sale.

 - Are a great communicator who knows how to build trust and follow through.

 - Can manage yourself, your time, and your pipeline with minimal supervision.

 - Are excited about being part of a fast-moving startup.

 - Communicate professionally in both Hebrew and English.

 - Are based in Israel and able to travel regularly to customer sites and industry events.

 - Relevant security clearance or experience in program-sensitive environments is a plus.

 - Are tech-savvy and comfortable working in remote environments (Slack, Notion, Loom, etc.)

THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF

 - Most of your experience is in short, transactional sales cycles and you haven’t owned complex enterprise deals.

 - Your background is limited to government capture or program-office relationships without closing commercial supply-chain or production agreements.

 - You need a mature company brand or inbound pipeline to create opportunities.

 - You’re looking primarily for a management title or a team to lead. This is a hands-on selling role.
 
 

OUR CULTURE

We’re a remote-first company. We don’t count hours; we measure performance. We trust our team to deliver, encourage hard questions, and avoid micromanagement and unproductive meetings.

We play online games together and bring the entire company together once a year for a week-long offsite in a beautiful location.

WHY JOIN US

 - Real impact - Your work directly affects whether defense companies meet their deadlines and contracts

 - Ownership - Build pipeline and close deals with full autonomy

 -

jobs.title: Research Scientist
jobs.description:
About idler

idler is a frontier data research lab. We build the evals and environments that the world's leading frontier labs use to measure and train their models.

After raising a $9m seed round led by Paradigm, we spent the last year developing coding evals for top coding models you know and love. At the same time, we've expanded into other domains besides coding: RSI & Auto-Research, Law, Enterprise Business, Cybersecurity, and others. Now, we are facing more lab demand for our data than we can serve, and are rapidly scaling the team to grow the business.

Our approach to creating training data scales using technology, and all of our data products are built on a unified self-reinforcing platform that learns through experience.

You would be joining a close-knit team that has reached product market fit, and your work would directly help to multiply our revenue.

You can see some of our work here: https://idler.ai/collections

About the role

As a Research Scientist at idler, you'll own measuring and improving how models learn from our tasks. The job is to maximize learning signal we produce per unit time. You'll draw on your own experience and collaborate with researchers at the frontier to validate our data quality, identify where improvements are needed, and create new datasets. To succeed, you'll need to have extensive experience doing this work in production at a frontier lab.

Examples of what you’ll do

 - Work with our customers — researchers at frontier labs — to design novel post-training recipes and data quality measurement techniques

 - Design and run our in-house post-training stack to measure model lift on our tasks

 - Develop new data products based on datasets and experts available to us

 - Identify opportunities to take advantage of self-reinforcing exponential feedback loops

 - Create agents to analyze thousands of environments and millions of trajectories

 - Help curate and specify task distributions for new corpora

 - Work with procurement to ensure external data we acquire is suitable for refinement

 - Create scaleable systems for ingesting & evaluating data we are considering buying

 - Develop new techniques for mining data for signal

What we’re looking for

 - 1+ years of experience doing RL in production at a frontier lab

 - Track record of post-training an LLM end to end

 - Desire to drive the research roadmap and implementation on a fast-moving team

 - Deep curiosity about how machines learn from data and how to extract the maximum learning signal from our tasks

Tech stack

Typescript, React, NodeJS, Postgres, Redis, Vercel, Cursor/Claude Code/Codex, Tinker, Modal, AWS, Daytona, GRPO

Details

 - In-person in San Francisco

 - Competitive salary + meaningful equity

 - Free meals in office

 - Healthcare, 401(k), 15 days of PTO per year

 - Relocation assistance

 - Small, ambitious team

This is an in-person role in San Francisco. We're a tight-knit founding team and we play to win. Join us if you like to win too.

jobs.title: Forward-Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ALEX & THE ROLE

Alex is an AI recruiter. Alex screens and interviews candidates over voice — on the web and over the phone — and it works inside the systems companies already recruit with: their applicant tracking system, their requisitions, their hiring process. Enterprises and staffing firms use it to run interviews at a volume they otherwise couldn't.

Forward-Deployed Engineers are the technical owners of every Alex deployment. When a customer signs, FDEs are the people who make Alex work inside their systems and their process — and keep it working. It is the most end-to-end engineering role at the company: you design the solution, build it, integrate it, ship it to production, and own it afterwards.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build how a customer uses Alex. Turn a hiring process described in a meeting into workflows that actually run — triggers, filters, interview guides, and the actions we take back in their ATS. When a customer needs something their setup doesn't do yet, you drive it: design, build, test, roll out, verify.

 - Own the integration surface. We integrate with roughly two dozen applicant tracking systems, some directly and some through a unified API partner. You'll build new integrations, maintain existing ones, and go deep on the ones you own — along with the other systems a customer's workflow reaches into, like assessment providers and identity verification.

 - Run the technical side of onboarding. Connection, permissions and scopes, job import, field mapping, workflow build, test interviews, go-live — sequenced so nothing is discovered in front of a candidate.

 - Own the deployments in production. The team owns the support queue — for customers and candidates both — and diagnoses to root cause rather than working around it. You'll also build the monitoring that catches problems before a customer has to call.

 - Be the technical voice of the customer. You are the person who sees, across many accounts, where the product runs out. Turning that into an evidenced case our product engineering team can act on is part of the job.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Real engineering ability. This role reads code, writes code, and ships changes. It is not a technical-adjacent role.

 - Comfort working inside someone else's system with incomplete documentation. Much of this job is finding out what a third-party API actually does, as opposed to what its docs claim.

 - Debugging instinct — the reflex to go get the evidence rather than reason from the symptom.

 - Direct customer contact without a buffer. You'll run your own working sessions and say hard things clearly.

 - Strong writing. A large fraction of the output of this role is a clear written explanation.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Forward-deployed, implementation, solutions, or integrations engineering experience — especially anywhere with a long tail of third-party systems.

 - You've built against a messy enterprise API and lived with the result.

 - Fluency with observability tooling — logs, traces, dashboards, alerting you had to live with.

Why join

 - High ownership and growth opportunities

 - Collaborate with a tight-knit team of talented builders

 - Launch products that directly impact people’s careers

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - FSA, DCFSA, HSA options

 - Flexible paid time off (PTO)

 - 401(k) plan

 - Fully paid parental leave program

If you've gotten this far and this role resonates with you, we want you to apply. Your first conversation will be with Alex, our AI recruiter.

Alex is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Our mission is to make healthcare safer by automating hospital quality reporting and helping staff identify and prevent the root causes of avoidable harm.
