jobs.title: Founding Account Executive
jobs.description:
WHAT DO WE DO?

Our mission is to radically accelerate the pace of software development by empowering every engineer to ship at the speed their agents write code. We’re building the last piece of the puzzle to enable this - the part that makes it actually safe to ship.

AI is enabling engineers to write code faster than ever before. But software review and testing hasn’t caught up. Engineering leaders are drowning in long software review cycles and more bugs than ever. The bottleneck isn’t writing code anymore, it’s everything that comes after it.

We spent 3 years building patented foundational technology to solve this. Our CTO, Quentin, spent over a decade at Palantir, where he led the 0 to 1 of core products that insiders credit as the primary value drivers behind Gotham and Foundry. We now work with the world's top engineering orgs - Notion, ElevenLabs, Mercor, Dropbox, Discord, LaunchDarkly, Wiz, CoreWeave, Wealthsimple, and more.

You’ll be joining us at a pivotal time. We’ve raised $20m from Chemistry, Menlo and Coatue, the same investors behind Twilio, Twitch, Intercom and PagerDuty and are backed by angels including the founders of Vercel, Datadog, Segment, Dropbox, the CTO of GitHub, CPO of Adobe, head of engineering at Cursor and many more.

This is an opportunity to join a company going through hypergrowth as we scale from millions of annual recurring revenue to $100m ARR.

If this excites you, come help us build it!

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

Join us as a Founding AE hire in London and own the full sales motion end-to-end, from first discovery to strategising pilot deployment to closing the deal.

Most AEs work a narrow slice of the stack, repeating the same sales scripts and motion deal after deal and handing off to a sales engineer the moment a conversation turns technical. Here, you’ll own the sales cycle from discovery to pilot, then stay on as deployment lead to make sure it actually succeeds. You’ll own technical conversations, building real technical authority with engineering leaders and understand exactly what their software development workflow looks like, why they buy and what they’d like to see different about the product.

This is an IC role, there is no team beneath you and no one to delegate work to.

Examples of what you will work on

 - Own end-to-end cycles: You’ll build and manage your own sales pipeline, win pilots and close deals, growing to lead a geography or sector or team as we scale

 - Lead enterprise sales: Navigate complex sales cycles with the world’s leading mid-market and enterprise tech businesses (up to $XXX BN market cap), initially securing low-six then mid-six figure deals

 - Strategise complex deployments: Work alongside our engineers on pilots to figure out how to make them successful, run training sessions and build strong relationships at the user level

 - Help steer our roadmap: You’ll become the best person in the company at explaining and pitching the product and can take specific customer feedback back to our product teams

 - Events: You’ll network with CTOs & engineering leaders, attend our dinners and conferences across the US, and become well-known in this space
 
 

YOU WILL LOVE THIS ROLE IF

 - ⭐ You learn fast and want to dive deep into the product - you have strong analytical thinking and can work from first principles; ambiguity / lack of experience in a technical domain doesn’t faze you / you are excited to learn!

 - ⭐ You are highly agentic - you have a bias to action, move fast, take ownership without being asked (e.g. if you need sales collateral you build it yourself!)

 - ⭐ You’re a hunter - chasing down revenue feels energizing, not exhausting or stressful, you create your own pipeline if there isn’t one!

 - ⭐ You want to work with engineers - you will spend most of your time externally and internally with developers, and this excites you!

THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF

 - You expect to work regular working hours and to travel infrequently; our teams, customers, investors span SF, London, NY

 - You need a team of BDRs, RevOps and Marketing to support you across the sales motion

 - You expect to lean entirely on engineers for technical demos and discovery calls

 - You expect never to have to build your own pipeline

REQUIREMENTS

 - STEM degree

 - 3-7 years of work experience outperforming in a B2B SaaS sales, strategic deployment or adjacent role

 - Experience with outbound-led sales

 - Bonus if you have experience selling a deeply technical product to senior engineering leaders or have been an early GTM hire (< #20) at a fast growing startup

 - If you were previously or are currently a software engineer with strong commercial acumen looking to pivot into tech sales, we’d strongly encourage you to apply!

YOU MAY LOOK LIKE THIS

 - Ex-STEM: You were always on the STEM track but realised being around people is what drives you! You are currently an AE but want to go back to doing something that is a bit more technical.

 - Builder: You are an AE but were previously a founder, have been part of an incubator (YC, EF, Antler) or want to be a future founder. You spike at commercial work but want to build knowledge outside of that to be a more well rounded leader in the future.

 - Early-stage operator: You have been or want to be an early founding hire to help shape what sales looks like and work to build up the processes, materials and strategy that will help us win!

 - AI lover: You work in b2b sales but feel like AI is developing so quickly you’re being left behind and want to build out a more technical skillset

PERKS ♥️

 - Competitive comp + significant equity

 - 🍲 Unlimited food & drinks in office - including daily lunch as a team, and your own Amazon business account to buy whatever snacks you want for the office.

 - 💻 A setup you’ll love - everyone has a standing desk, brand new Macbook, your choice of ergonomic peripherals, and a £2k WFH budget to make home just as good

 - 🏄‍♀️ £300 monthly welln

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Healthcare is in crisis and the people behind the results deserve better. With more and more data coming from wearables, lab tests, and patient–doctor interactions, we’re entering an era where data is abundant.

Junction is building the infrastructure layer for diagnostic healthcare, making patient data accessible, actionable, and automated across labs and devices. Our mission is simple but ambitious: use health data to unlock unprecedented insight into human health and disease.

If you're passionate about how technology can supercharge healthcare, you’ll fit right in.

Backed by Creandum, Point Nine, 20VC, YC, and leading angels, we’re working to solve one of the biggest challenges of our time: making healthcare personalized, proactive, and affordable. We’re already connecting millions and scaling fast.

SHORT ON TIME? 

 - You: You’ve led experienced engineers, stayed close to the code, and care about the product and the customers using it.

 - Ownership / Focus: You’ll lead a small and growing engineering team, you’ll own its engineering direction, technical delivery, team health and hiring.

 - How we manage: We don’t believe in purely pastoral engineering managers. You’ll manage and develop people, but you’ll also ship, unblock, review and make technical decisions alongside them.

 - Salary: £120-£150k + equity (based on experience and location)

 - Location: Fully remote (GMT). We have one company offsite each year, with possible travel to London every couple of months for team meet-ups.

WHY WE NEED YOU

Our engineering team is growing, and we need another Engineering Manager to grow with it. You’ll report to Mark, our Head of Engineering, and work alongside Rui, our other Engineering Manager. You’ll initially take ownership of a small engineering team, working closely with product and other teams to decide what to build and get it shipped.

At Junction, engineering management is a technical job. We want our managers close enough to the work to know what’s going on, give good feedback and get involved when needed. But we don’t want you to become the person everyone waits for when something gets difficult.

Six months in, your team should trust you, people outside the team should know where things stand, and the team should be delivering what it says it will.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY

 - Own the engineering direction, delivery and health of a small team of senior product engineers.

 - Work with product on what the team commits to, then make sure it gets delivered.

 - Stay close to the code: review PRs, give technical feedback, pair on problems and ship when it makes sense.

 - Unblock the team when decisions are unclear or things go wrong.

 - Give engineers regular feedback, run useful 1:1s and performance reviews, and actively help them grow in their careers.

 - Notice what’s slowing the team down and fix it, surface problems early and keep the rest of the company clear on what’s happening.

 - Own hiring for your team and play an active role in helping Junction grow.

REQUIREMENTS

 - You’ve led and directly managed experienced software engineers.

 - You’ve stayed technically involved while managing

 - You’ve owned a team’s delivery, not just its people management.

 - You can give useful technical feedback and make sound calls on engineering trade-offs.

 - You’ve worked with product and other teams to turn customer problems into shipped software.

 - You’ve helped engineers develop through direct feedback, coaching and meaningful opportunities to take on more.

 - You’ve hired engineers and helped raise the technical or operating standards of a team.

You don’t need to tick every box to fit in here. If the problems we’re solving genuinely interest you and you know you can contribute, we’d love to talk.

 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - You’ve worked at an early-stage or scaling company where managers are expected to manage people and build product.

WHAT THIS ROLE ISN’T

 - If you want to stay out of the code and spend most of your time in 1:1s, planning and status meetings, it won’t be a good fit.

 - You’ll have to make tough calls on technical and non-technical topics and own the outcomes

 - It isn’t a tech lead role with a few 1:1s either. Developing people, giving difficult feedback, hiring and building a healthy team are core parts of the job.

How you'll be compensated

 - Your salary is dependent on your location and experience level

 - Equity (extended exercise post 2 years of employment) 

 - Company and team offsites

 - Monthly learning budget of $150 for personal development and productivity

 - $100 monthly wellness budget

 - Flexible, remote-first working, including $1K for home office equipment

 - Coworking budget

 - 36 days paid time off (including bank holidays)

 - Premium healthcare coverage 

 - 4% monthly contribution to pension/401k

 - Yearly blood test on us

 - Enhanced parental, foster, and adoption leave
 
 

Important details before applying:

 - We only hire folks physically based in GMT and EST timezones 

 - We do not sponsor visas right now given our stage

jobs.title: Implementation Engineer
jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Offstream is looking for a talented implementation engineer to join our growing team. You will own the success of our customer implementations. This means taking a project from signed deal to a fully configured deployment on the Offstream platform. This role sits at the intersection of compliance, software implementation, and project management, and will have a direct impact on how quickly and reliably our customers can operate.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own the end-to-end success of MRV implementations, from kickoff through go-live, managing timelines, dependencies, and stakeholders along the way

 - Project-manage through change: re-scope and re-plan when requirements, registry guidance, or stakeholder priorities shift, while keeping timelines, owners, and risks clear

 - Translate project design documents into complete MRV plan requirements - identifying gaps, making judgment calls where the guidance is ambiguous, and writing MRV plans for registry submission

 - Communicate directly with registries and compliance bodies to resolve open questions and get plans approved

 - Configure the Offstream app to match each project's specific monitoring, reporting, and verification needs

 - Make judgment calls on app updates and configuration changes as project requirements evolve or compliance guidance is released

 - Work closely with engineering to flag where the platform needs new functionality versus where a project can be solved with configuration

 - Build systems that improve upon themselves so that each new project goes faster and smoother than the last
 
 
 
 
 WHAT YOU WILL BRING
 
 (If you don't meet all of these requirements, you should still apply. We want to find high-slope individuals, so if you can quickly grow into this profile we'd love to hear from you)

 - 3+ years in an implementation, project management, or MRV/technical advisory role, ideally in carbon markets, energy, or another data-heavy regulated industry

 - Comfort making judgment calls under ambiguity and owning the outcome

 - Experience configuring or working closely with software platforms to meet customer-specific requirements

 - Strong project management instincts. You keep projects on track without needing to be told to and intrinsically enjoy managing many workstreams

 - Experience working on capital project development and/or on-the-ground operations (construction/startup/commissioning), with an ability to translate field realities into clear plans, schedules, and execution

 - Excitement about using AI tools to move faster, whether that's drafting MRV plans, digging through registry guidance, or configuring the app

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll be writing plans for registries and talking directly with customers

 - Passion for startups

 - Ease balancing multiple stakeholders along an ambiguous path to get to a final outcome

WHAT IT'S LIKE TO WORK AS AN IMPLEMENTATION ENGINEER AT OFFSTREAM

 - We are an AI native team that rarely does anything the slow, manual way by default, but we still expect a high level of rigor and expect ownership over what you produce

 - We believe that applying steady effort over a long period of time will result in incredible progress

 - Relentless ownership means we take full responsibility for outcomes: anticipating problems, driving solutions end to end, and never waiting for someone else to make progress.

THE FIRST 3 MONTHS

 - Month 1 - you will shadow live implementations to learn our MRV plan process, registry relationships, and app configuration end to end

 - Month 2 - you will independently own an implementation from kickoff to go-live

 - Month 3 - you will be running multiple implementations in parallel and contributing improvements to our playbooks and internal processes

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive salary and equity ($100 - $160k) depending on qualifications and experience: $115k - $160k in SF, $100k - $145k in Denver

 - A full suite of benefits

 - Unlimited PTO with a minimum of 2 weeks off per year + all federal holidays and a company shut down for the week between Christmas and New Years

LOCATION

Denver, CO - we work in an office near union station 3 days per week

San Francisco, CA - we work in an office near the 4th and King Caltrain station 3 days per week

ABOUT THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Intro call: Learn about Offstream in more detail including the mission, goals, and what implementations look like today. You'll be asked about projects you've managed and how you think about ambiguity and tradeoffs

 - Take home SOP writing exercise: Write an SOP document to implement software with a hypothetical customer

 - Live implementation role-play: Live execute on your SOP with a member of Offstream's team

 - Technical systems and reasoning: Deal with messy data and show off your ability to handle ambiguity when faced with the reality of complex, real-world systems

 - Team interview: Meet the team to talk about your background, experience, and motivations for joining an early-stage startup

Kernel is crazy fast, open source browser infrastructure for AI agents. We handle autoscaling, observability, and the messy details of web interaction, so developers can focus on what their agents do instead of how they do it.

jobs.title: Developer Experience Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAINDROP

Raindrop http://raindrop.ai/ is the monitoring platform for AI agents. Engineering teams at Fortune 100s and the fastest-growing AI companies (Vercel, Speak, Clay) use it to catch silent failures in production. When an agent misbehaves, Raindrop alerts the team, links to the trace, and surfaces the root cause so they can fix it fast. With Raindrop 2.0 (Self-Healing Agents) https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/introducing-raindrop-2/, the loop closes itself: your coding agent fixes it, and the fix becomes an eval to prevent regressions.

WHY IT MATTERS

AI agents fail constantly in ways both hilarious and terrifying. Regular software throws exceptions. But AI agents fail silently, leaving engineers with almost no visibility into how their agents are actually performing.

The current status quo is sifting through millions of logs and trying to debug flaky evals that just aren't matching real world results. Evals are like unit tests, they confirm your model got specific test cases right. But in the real world agents call thousands of tools, run for hours, and encounter millions of unpredictable actions.

That’s where Raindrop comes in. It learns the unique shape of each AI agent’s issues. Starting from presets like Laziness, Forgetting, or Task Failure, to automatically tuning itself to each agent and discovering unknown unknowns.

With one click of a button, AI engineers start tracking issues or topics across 100% of their production data. They can see frequency over time, how many users are affected, relevant properties and more.

In order to process hundreds of millions of events, we gradually train small, custom models, private to each company, that learn to uniquely understand how their product is used.

As part of the early team, you’ll play a fundamental role in shaping the company - from making strategy and product decisions, to helping scale the team, to shaping the future of AI agents.

OUR INVESTORS

We've raised $50M total https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/series-a/, led by CRV, with backing from Lightspeed, Figma Ventures, Vercel Ventures, and the founders of Replit (Amjad Masad, Michele Catasta), Cognition (Walden Yan), Framer (Koen Bok, Jorn van Dijk), Speak (Andrew Hsu), and Notion (Akshay Kothari).

YOUR FOCUS

 - Ensure customers have a world-class developer experience integrating and using Raindrop

 - Maintain, improve and add SDKs

 - Help customers debug integration

 - Write clear documentation, tutorials, and guides

 - Quick iteration without compromising on quality

 - Deeply understand the customer

IDEAL CANDIATE

 - Knows how to balance short-term and long-term speed

 - Strong programming, problem solving, and debugging skills

 - Passion for working with developers and building developer communities

 - Excellent technical writing skills

 - Interest in AI products + tools (ideally experience building these or an avid user)

jobs.title: Product Engineer, Backend
jobs.description:
About David AI

David AI is the first audio data research company. We bring an R&D approach to data–developing datasets with the same rigor AI labs bring to models. Our mission is to bring AI into the real world, and we believe audio is the gateway. Speech is versatile, accessible, and human—it fits naturally into everyday life. As audio AI advances and new use cases emerge, high-quality training data is the bottleneck. This is where David AI comes in.

David AI was founded in 2024 by a team of former Scale AI engineers and operators. In less than a year, we've brought on most FAANG companies and AI labs as customers. We recently raised a $50M Series B from Meritech, NVIDIA, Jack Altman (Alt Capital), Amplify Partners, First Round Capital and other Tier 1 investors.

Our team is sharp, humble, ambitious, and tight-knit. We're looking for the best research, engineering, product, and operations minds to join us on our mission to push the frontier of audio AI.

About our Engineering team

At David AI, our engineers build the pipelines, platforms, and models that transform raw audio into high-signal data for leading AI labs and enterprises. We're a tight-knit team of product engineers, infrastructure specialists, and machine learning experts focused on building the world's first audio data research company.

We move fast, own our work end-to-end, and ship to production daily. Our team designs real-time pipelines handling terabytes of speech data and deploys cutting-edge generative audio models.

About this role

As a Backend Engineer at David AI, you'll build the systems and infrastructure that power how our users process and make sense of the audio data they'll use to train their models, working closely with researchers to consistently iterate on how to best collect our data.

In this role, you will

 - Design and build scalable backend systems and core data processing pipelines that derive actionable insights from terabytes of audio data every day.

 - Architect and maintain the APIs and services that power features thousands of users interact with daily.

 - Build, deploy, and evaluate LLM and DSP based solutions to increase our customers' understanding of nuanced features across our datasets.

 - Iterate rapidly on our research hypotheses by working closely with researchers and our Operations team to deploy backend infrastructure that supports new data collection.

 - Stay up-to-date with cutting edge technologies and frameworks to apply to our current product offering across backend engineering, data engineering, machine learning, and signal processing.

Your background looks like

 - 2+ years of backend engineering experience.

 - Strong backend fundamentals with experience designing scalable systems, APIs, and data pipelines that handle significant scale and volume.

 - A proven track record of delivering engineering solutions that contributed value to customers.

 - Experience working in a high-pace environment where constant progress was enabled by detail-oriented execution.

 - Emphasis on building robust, reliable infrastructure that supports highly polished, production-grade products.

 - AI/ML or audio experience is not required but you should be excited to learn.

Bonus points if you have

 - Educational or professional experience with digital signal processing and a deep understanding of speech.

 - Experience building and deploying ML models in a production environment.

 - Led (managed or tech-led) engineering teams in high-growth environments.

Some technologies we work with

 - Node.js, tRPC, PostgreSQL, AWS, Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev, WebRTC, FFmpeg, TypeScript.

Benefits

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.

 - FSA & HSA access.

 - 401k access.

 - Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.

 - Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.

In this role, you will

 - Iterate rapidly on our research hypotheses by working closely with researchers and our Operations team to deploy interfaces to collect new data.

Your background looks like

 - Emphasis on building intuitive products and experiences that resonate with users, with a track record of shipping highly polished, production-grade interfaces.

Bonus points if you have

 - Educational or professional experience with digital signal processing and a deep understanding of speech.

 - Experience building interfaces for ML-powered or data-heavy products in a production environment.

 - Led (managed or tech-led) engineering teams in high-growth environments.

Some technologies we work with

jobs.title: Agent Experience Engineer
jobs.description:
AgentMail is building the identity layer for AI agents, starting with email. Our most important user is an agent: it discovers us through model answers and docs, then signs up and integrates on its own. We're looking for an Agent Experience Engineer to own how AI models and agents discover and use AgentMail. That means AEO, evals, benchmarks, agent traces, docs, and llms.txt.

AgentMail has raised $6M from investors including General Catalyst, Y Combinator, Paul Graham (founder of YC), Karim Atiyeh (founder of Ramp), Paul Copplestone (founder of Supabase), and Dharmesh Shah (founder of HubSpot).

You'll work on:

 - Answer-engine presence: when someone asks an LLM about email or identity for agents, AgentMail is the recommendation. You measure share of voice on the prompts that matter and move it

 - Original research: evals and benchmarks on how well frontier models, open source models, and agent harnesses use AgentMail

 - Agent traces: running agents against our docs and site, reading their reasoning, and fixing what confuses them. A stray Reddit thread once convinced LLMs we have a feature that doesn't exist

 - The agent-facing surface: llms.txt, MCP descriptions, docs structure, and the error messages agents hit at 3am with no human watching

 - The AEO content engine: steering and verifying our automated page pipeline, briefing freelancers, and doing backlink outreach to the pages models already cite

 - The weekly AEO briefing's action queue, from freshness debt to competitor watch

You're a fit if:

 - You build with agents daily and have opinions about what makes a product easy or miserable for an agent to use

 - You work cross functionally by default

 - You express your opinion early, and you'll publish an honest writeup even when the result is inconvenient

 - You go deep on messy technical problems. You'd rather spend a day reading agent traces than guess

 - You understand retrieval: models pull chunks, not pages, and you write accordingly

Strong preference for published technical writing or benchmarks people actually cited. SEO or AEO experience helps, as do contributions to docs or MCP servers in the wild.

Compensation: $110K to $175K, plus 0.2% to 0.5% equity.

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Mercura (YC W25) helps the companies that build the real world move at software speed, automating the back-office work that runs the $12 trillion industry behind every hospital, school, and power plant. We started with one of their biggest bottlenecks - turning messy technical requests into accurate quotes. With a team of 16, we're now targeting $10M by the end of 2026 as well as our expansion into the US.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

You are the second designer here, and you own product surface end to end: you find the problem, decide if it's worth solving, design it, build it, ship it, and then check whether it worked.

That last part is the job. Most designers stop at handoff. You won't have one. You'll sit with a German construction supplier watching them fight a spreadsheet, decide which of their five complaints is the real one, and have something in front of them within days. Then you'll open PostHog to find out if it moved anything.

We ship fast and polished. If those feel like you, this is the right role for you.

WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON

 - Find the real problem. Run your own customer conversations — no PM filter. Distinguish what users ask for from what they need, and be willing to conclude something isn't worth building.

 - Ship it yourself. Design and write the production code. React/TypeScript. You own the result, not a layer of it.

 - Know if it worked. Instrument what you ship. Define the success metric before you build. Kill your own features when the data says so.

 - Set the quality floor. Empty states, loading states, error states, keyboard behaviour, the transition that makes a slow thing feel fast. Nobody is going to catch these for you.

 - Compress the loop. Prototype in whatever gets to a real answer fastest. Speed here means speed to validated user value, not speed to merged PR.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Evidence of discovery. You've changed your own mind about what to build because of something a user said or did. You can tell us about a time you were wrong.

 - Evidence of analytics. You've made a product decision from data you instrumented yourself. You know the difference between a metric that moved and a metric that mattered.

 - Taste. You notice when spacing is off, when a flow doesn't communicate, when an interaction feels sluggish — and you fix it without being asked. We'll look at what you've made.

 - Real code shipped to real users. React and TypeScript to production. Not prototypes, not a bootcamp project. Some Python helps; we can teach it.

 - AI as leverage, not as identity. We don't care which tools you use. We care that you've restructured how you work around them and can show us the difference it made.

 - German and English. Our users are almost entirely German-speaking. You'll be in those conversations from week one.

How we work

In the office, Munich, five days a week. We build in the same room — decisions happen at desks, not in tickets. Relocation support if you're not here yet.

High pace, steep learning curve. Most of the team is here well past six. That's not a policy or a number we track, it's what building something this size with sixteen people currently takes, and it's a phase, not a permanent state. If you're optimising for predictable hours right now, this is the wrong role, and that's a completely reasonable thing to be optimising for.

This is not the role if you want specs handed to you, you separate "my design work" from "my engineering work," you need a design system before you can start, or your best work needs a slide to explain it.

ABOUT THE FOUNDERS

We are Lukas, Stefan & Sean, the co-founders of Mercura. 

We share a deep commitment to excellence and the discipline to pursue what others might consider impossible. 

Two of us come from non-academic families, and we all know what it means to create our own paths and overcome barriers. This experience shapes our belief in equal opportunity and fuels our dedication to social mobility.

Lukas (left) is responsible for business development at Mercura. With his background as a Data Scientist at Allianz and at Google in Silicon Valley, he brings extensive expertise in data and AI. 
Lukas’ family has been active in the construction industry for over 100 years, giving him a deep understanding and passion for the sector's specific needs.

Sean (middle) is responsible for technical development at Mercura. As a top 0.01% physicist, Sean earned a Silver medal for Germany at the International Physics Olympiad (IPhO), began researching with the Max Planck Institute at the age of 16, and has since published at leading machine learning conferences. 

Stefan (right) leads product development at Mercura. Previously, he worked in management consulting at Bain & Company, where he helped manufacturers improve their operations. 
Stefan leverages his research experience at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Harvard Business School to develop innovative solutions for the industry.

jobs.title: Account Executive Nordics/UK - AI & Security
jobs.description:
ABOUT ESCAPE

Escape secures the code-to-cloud attack surface. Our platform maps every asset a company actually exposes to the internet including undocumented APIs and endpoints then tests them continuously. We run automated AI penetration testing and DAST at the pace that engineering teams ship code, not just once a year for auditors.

 

We’re 45+ people based in Paris, Amsterdam, Hawaii, Boston, New York, Series A funded, and rapidly growing.

 

WHY WE’RE HIRING

Escape has growing customer demand and inbound interest in the Nordics and UK with an already existing client base.

 

This is a first-in-region role with full ownership. You’ll be responsible for end-to-end sales, your own pipeline, building a territory plan, and shaping how we go to market in these regions. Successful approaches will directly influence our future playbook working in autonomy, direct impact, and shaping our approach.

 

THE ROLE

You’ll own the full sales cycle, from first contact to signature, selling to technical buyers CISOs, Heads of AppSec, Security Engineers, and platform leaders. These stakeholders have deep expertise, strong preferences, and often existing tools, and will challenge you on how things work.

 

While you’ll partner closely with Sales Engineers for POCs and technical validation and have direct access to founders and the product team you’ll need to confidently handle first conversations and independently build most of your pipeline.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Proven cybersecurity sales experience, you’ve sold real security products to real security teams.

 - Closed complex enterprise deals: six-figure ACVs with long cycles, buying committees, procurement, legal, you’ve managed deals through stalls and restarts.

 - Demonstrated ability to build pipeline from scratch via successful cold outbound.

 - Track record of meeting/exceeding quota ready to discuss your targets and results.

 - Fluent English plus either native/fluent Swedish or deep UK market expertise.

 - Eligible to work in Sweden or the UK (required). We don't do VISA sponsorship.

 

Bonus points for:

 - Experience with AppSec or developer tooling

 - Being the first AE in a new market

 - Knowledge of structured selling methods (e.g., MEDDIC)

 - Experience with partner-led sales

 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 3 Months:

 - Confidently demo the product solo and explain our differentiators

 - Deep knowledge of ICP, competitors, and security buying cycles in your region

 - Own and move existing opportunities in the pipeline

 - Write a territory plan: key accounts, segments, priorities

 - Launch consistent outbound and generate your first qualified opportunities

 

3–6 Months:

 - Independently run end-to-end deals

 - Deliver your first closed-won accounts in-region, including at least one sourced cold

 - Pipeline at 3x forward quota with reliable forecasting and CRM hygiene

 - Bring valuable market insights: why buying cycles start, recurring objections, who we’re losing to and why

 - Strong collaborative rhythm established with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product with your feedback driving change

 

6–12 Months:

 - Consistently hit quota with a scalable pipeline 

 - Recognized as the point owner for Nordics/UK; you set the direction, we support it

 - Documented playbook new AEs can ramp using your processes

 - See expansion, multi-year deals, reference customers, and case studies

 - Help hire and onboard additional AEs for the region

 

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive base salary with uncapped commission [OTE, currency, split provided during interviews]

 - [Equity Package]

 - Remote-first, with regular trips to Paris and company offsites

 - Local benefits via Deel EOR

 - Full autonomy and genuine ownership in a high-impact role, with direct access to founders who value your input

 

HIRING PROCESS

 - 30 min intro call with People & Talent

 - 30 min sales deep dive with our Head of Growth

 - 60 min sales simulation (“Sell Escape back to us”) with an AE and Sales Engineer

 - 45 min conversation with the founders

 - References check, then offer

 

Total process: 2–3 weeks. We’ll keep you informed throughout.

 

Escape is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.description:
About Elyos AI

We’re building the next generation of customer service with AI Agents. Our agents answer calls, reply to emails and WhatsApp messages, make bookings, take payments, and operate the CRM in the same way a human would.

We founded Elyos in June 2023 and took part in the Y Combinator S23 batch. Our founders spent four months in San Francisco living and breathing AI. Since then, we’ve been growing revenue ~30% month on month and shipping fast. It’s been wild so far - and we’re just getting started. We recently raised a $13m series A to turbocharge our growth.

The product has grown faster than any one of us can hold in our head - agent configuration, calls, email, campaigns, scheduling - and design has been shared out across whoever happened to be building the feature. It needs an owner. Someone to give it one language, and enough depth that it holds up when hundreds of customers use it in ways we didn't plan for.

There are two sides to it. How the agents behave, on the phone and in the inbox and over chat. And the product behind them, where a trade business sets up what its agents do and checks what they did.

You'd be our first designer, working directly with the two CEOs, the CTO and with engineers to build what you design.

The work, roughly in order:

 - How our customers work alongside their agents. Watching a call, correcting the agent, deciding what it can and can't do, trusting it a bit more next time. Nobody has good patterns for this yet.

 - One design language. Type, colour, icons, components, written down and held to.

 - Joining the product up. Onboarding, creating an agent, setting up on-call, reviewing what it books - separate islands today, and you'd be central to fixing it.

You'll spend real time with customers. They run vans, not product teams, and they'll tell you exactly what's wrong. Their current software was designed in the 2000s and has been cobbled together ever since. Nobody has seriously designed for this industry. There's nothing to inherit and nothing to copy, so the patterns would be yours to set. And they're the best users you could ask for: they've never had good software, so they know within a day whether something works.

We're looking for someone who's designed something genuinely complicated. Dense screens, real operational workflows, software people sit in all day. You prototype fast, you're fluent with AI tools, and you won't be the one shipping the React unless you want to be. You'll need opinions and the willingness to push them.

Brand and the marketing site sit elsewhere. This is the product.

PERKS & BENEFITS

 - 💸 Competitive salary & equity - we are building together, we win together

 - 💪 Wellhub Gold subscription - access 1000's of gyms and health related activities (inc. GymBox, 1Rebel, F45 etc)

 - 📚 AI-focused learning & development - stay ahead of the curve.

 - ✈️ Team socials & annual offsites - cool destinations included (last year we went to Greece!).

 - 🏥 Private healthcare - because your well-being matters.

Record requests today move through fax machines, phone trees, and manual follow-up, a process that can take weeks and routinely stalls the legal and clinical decisions that depend on it. We use AI in conjunction with human review to pull decision-ready records in a fraction of the time, with a level of accuracy legacy vendors can't match.

We just turned two, doubling order volume month over month, and on a clear path to category leadership. We're well-funded (post Series A) and building toward 100x our current scale.

Our mission is to fully automate record retrieval. Getting there takes sharp engineering and relentless execution, in equal measure.

About the Role

Sales is how Codes Health grows. We have doubled our sales team since January. As an Enterprise Account Executive, you'll own our largest, most complex accounts: law firms and healthcare systems where deals involve multiple stakeholders, longer cycles, and higher stakes. Our customers hand us mission-critical workflows that directly affect legal outcomes and patient care, so how we close, how we set expectations, and how we build long-term partnerships matters as much as whether we close at all.

You'll own the full sales cycle from initial contact to close and account expansion for enterprise-tier accounts, while helping shape our early-stage enterprise sales playbook with your own expertise and autonomy. You're helping define how we sell into large, sophisticated organizations, how we structure enterprise agreements, and what "great" looks like at the top of our market. You'll be selling a complex, high-trust product to demanding, multi-stakeholder buying committees, and shaping our enterprise go-to-market motion from the ground up in the process.

Culture is part of the job here. How we sell, how we treat prospects, how we connect with internal teams, and how we represent the company are all things we take as seriously as the number itself.

What You'll Do

 - Own the full sales cycle for enterprise accounts: prospecting, discovery, demo, negotiation, and close for a complex, high-trust product sold to multi-stakeholder buying committees.

 - Navigate long, complex enterprise sales cycles, including procurement, legal, and multiple internal stakeholders on the buyer side.

 - Contribute to and evolve our enterprise sales playbook: refine qualification criteria, messaging, pricing, and contract structures, and help onboard and ramp new AEs as we continue scaling the team.

 - Manage and grow relationships post-close, building strategic account plans and identifying expansion opportunities within the large accounts you land.

 - Expect lots of travel. When you're not traveling, expect to be in the office. Our teams are in-person five days a week at our office in Dumbo.

 - Represent Codes Health in person at conferences, on-site meetings, and industry events. This is a core part of how we build trust and scale distribution.

 - Work directly with the VP of Sales to shape enterprise go-to-market strategy and feed customer insight back into product and positioning.

 - Understand that we are selling an outcome, not a service.

Who You Are

 - A high-caliber B2B seller with a track record closing large, complex, multi-stakeholder deals, ideally with six- and seven-figure ACVs.

 - Experience selling into legal preferred.

 - Excellent at discovery. You ask sharp questions, listen closely, and diagnose what a prospect actually needs before you pitch anything.

 - In-person oriented. You believe trust is built faster face-to-face and want to be in the room with prospects and with your team, not just on Zoom.

 - Comfortable operating without a playbook. You build structure rather than wait for it.

 - NYC or remote.

Why Join Codes Health

You'll be a foundational part of building a category-defining company. You'll work directly with the VP of Sales to shape enterprise go-to-market strategy, help scale our fast-growing customer base, and define how Codes Health sells to the largest accounts in our market for years to come.

The work has real stakes: your deals directly affect how quickly law firms resolve cases and how efficiently healthcare providers deliver care. In return, you get real ownership, visibility across the company, a steep growth curve, and a chance to help steward Codes Health through hyper-growth while building a track record that compounds.

If you want a role where your judgment, your execution, and your relationships genuinely move the business, this is it.

Compensation & Benefits

 - Base salary: $90,000–$125,000, commensurate with experience.

 - OTE: $180,000–$250,000

 - Meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Health benefits and a setup built around doing your best work.

Actual base pay is based on experience, skills, and qualifications and may vary from the range listed above, consistent with New York pay transparency requirements.

jobs.title: Founding Developer Relations
jobs.description:
LiteLLM is the open-source AI gateway used by developers and enterprises to access, manage, and govern LLMs through a unified interface.

Teams use LiteLLM to route requests across model providers, control spend, monitor usage, implement security policies, and reliably operate AI applications in production.

We are looking for our first Developer Relations hire to help more developers discover LiteLLM, understand what they can build with it, and successfully deploy it in production.

WHY WE’RE HIRING

LiteLLM has a large and growing technical community. Developers discover the project through GitHub, documentation, search, technical content, and recommendations from other engineers.

But discovering LiteLLM is only the beginning.

Developers need to quickly understand how LiteLLM fits into their stack, see credible examples of it solving real problems, and get from their first request to a production deployment. They also need clear ways to share feedback, contribute to the project, and learn about new capabilities.

You will help us build that developer journey.

This is LiteLLM’s first dedicated Developer Relations role. You will establish how we educate developers, engage with the community, support product launches, and turn developer feedback into better documentation, examples, and product decisions.

WHAT THIS JOB ACTUALLY IS

This is a hands-on technical individual-contributor role.

You will spend much of your time building with LiteLLM and turning what you learn into resources that help other developers succeed. You should be equally comfortable opening a code editor, explaining an infrastructure concept, and talking with developers about where they are getting stuck.

In a typical month, you will:

 - Build and maintain runnable demos, sample applications, integrations, and reference architectures for real LiteLLM use cases.

 - Create technical guides, videos, workshops, launch demos, and deep dives that make complex capabilities understandable and immediately usable.

 - Engage directly with developers through GitHub, community channels, livestreams, meetups, conferences, and other technical forums.

 - Partner with Product and Engineering on launches so new capabilities ship with strong examples, documentation, and a clear technical story.

 - Identify recurring questions and points of friction, then turn them into better documentation, examples, product feedback, issues, or code contributions where appropriate.

 - Explore the wider AI developer ecosystem and build useful examples with the models, frameworks, tools, and platforms LiteLLM users care about.

 - Use developer feedback and adoption data to decide which educational resources, integrations, and community initiatives will have the greatest impact.

 - Represent LiteLLM publicly through technical talks, workshops, videos, podcasts, and conversations with the developer community.

This is not a traditional social-media or event-marketing role, and it is not a frontline support position.

You will help individual developers, but the goal is to turn what you learn into resources and improvements that help the entire community. You will not be measured by content volume or impressions alone. The best outcome might be a runnable example that unlocks an important use case, an explanation that becomes the canonical resource for a difficult topic, or a pattern of feedback that leads us to improve the product.

Because this is a founding role, you will also help define our Developer Relations priorities, operating cadence, and measures of success. You will shape the function while continuing to ship technical work yourself.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

TECHNICAL EDUCATION

 - Create high-quality tutorials, demos, sample applications, reference architectures, videos, and technical deep dives.

 - Develop educational resources around the problems developers are actively trying to solve.

 - Explain LiteLLM capabilities such as model routing, fallbacks, cost controls, observability, authentication, guardrails, MCP, and production deployment.

 - Keep examples and technical content accurate as LiteLLM and the wider AI ecosystem evolve.

 - Improve the path from reading about a capability to successfully implementing it.

DEVELOPER COMMUNITY

 - Build genuine relationships with developers using, evaluating, and contributing to LiteLLM.

 - Participate in GitHub discussions, community channels, technical forums, and open-source conversations.

 - Help developers get unstuck while identifying patterns that should become durable resources or product improvements.

 - Support contributors and power users and create opportunities for them to share what they have built.

 - Represent LiteLLM at relevant conferences, meetups, workshops, livestreams, podcasts, and community events.

PRODUCT FEEDBACK

 - Build a structured feedback loop between the developer community and LiteLLM’s Product and Engineering teams.

 - Identify recurring points of confusion, missing integrations, documentation gaps, and product friction.

 - Reproduce technical issues and distinguish between documentation, usability, and product problems.

 - Turn developer feedback into clear product recommendations, issues, examples, and documentation improvements.

 - Contribute technical fixes directly when they are within scope, while partnering with Engineering on larger product changes.

PRODUCT LAUNCHES

 - Own the developer-facing execution for major product and open-source launches.

 - Work with Product and Engineering to understand what is shipping, who it is for, and why it matters.

 - Produce the demos, sample code, tutorials, documentation, and technical explanations developers need to try new capabilities.

 - Ensure launches show working implementations rather than only announcing features.

 - Evaluate whether launches result in meaningful developer understanding and adoption.

DEVELOPER RELATIONS STRATEGY

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
LiteLLM is the world's most popular AI Gateway, trusted by companies like Adobe, Netflix, and NASA. We're building the next generation of infrastructure for AI applications—and now we're building our second product.

WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON

Skills: Python, LLM APIs, FastAPI

As the AI Engineer, you'll be responsible for ensuring LiteLLM unifies the format for calling LLM APIs in the broader OpenAI + Anthropic spec. This involves writing transformations to convert API requests from OpenAI/Anthropic spec to various LLM provider formats, building provider-agnostic unification functionality (e.g. session management across non-openai models for /v1/responses API, etc.). You'll work directly with the CEO and CTO on critical projects including:

 - System design for supporting provider level features at the gateway level (skills, compaction, batches, etc.)

 - Thinking about the developer experience - to support millions of users who leverage your work via LiteLLM's Python SDK

 - Building across LLM's, MCP's, and Agents by maintaining an excellent LLM interoperability layer, supporting a wide range of MCP Auth flows and enabling various Agent use-cases

What is our tech stack

The tech stack includes Python, FastAPI, Redis, Postgres.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 1-2 years of backend/full-stack experience with production systems

 - Passion for open source and user engagement

 - Experience working with the OpenAI api (understand the difference between /chat/completions and /responses, and can speak to API-specific nuances)

 - Strong work ethic and ability to thrive in small teams

 - Eagerness to talk to users and help solve real problems

WHY JOIN LITELLM?

 - Work directly with the founders every day.

 - Build products used by thousands of engineering teams around the world.

 - Own meaningful product decisions—not just implementation.

 - Move incredibly fast and see your work in production immediately.

 - Help define the future of AI infrastructure and developer tooling.

 - Competitive salary, equity, health, dental, and vision benefits.

ABOUT LITELLM

LiteLLM is the world's most widely adopted AI Gateway. We provide a unified API for 100+ LLM providers along with routing, authentication, budgets, observability, and governance for production AI systems. Thousands of companies rely on LiteLLM to power AI in production.

If you love talking to users, building products, and shipping software that people actually use, we'd love to meet you.

jobs.title: Founding Content Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT OFFDEAL

OffDeal is the world’s first AI-native investment bank for founder- and family-owned businesses looking to sell their life’s work. We combine experienced investment bankers with purpose-built technology to bring institutional-quality M&A advice and execution to an underserved market.

We’ve closed transactions across trades, healthcare, and business services, built a fast-growing team, raised $17M from top VCs (Radical Ventures, Y Combinator), and we’re just getting started. We have no shortage of stories worth telling, and this is the role that tells them.

See the momentum: The Wall Street Journal https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-companies-staffing-c9029343 · CNBC https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-gIqEitH6fg · Financial Times https://www.ft.com/content/9daf5c7e-e301-4b7d-809a-ff9fb336bdbc · Watch our Series A launch https://x.com/leveredvlad/status/1950192434790457849?s=20

THE ROLE

OffDeal has already earned meaningful organic attention and press, but the work has behind it has been founder-led, opportunistic, and built one asset at a time. Meanwhile, our growing volume of closed deals, client outcomes, and company milestones is creating more great raw material than we currently capture.

You will turn that momentum into a scalable trust and proof engine. Your first mandate is to make OffDeal’s success real to business owners considering a sale. The same body of work will also support buyers, partners, and future teammates.

We believe AI radically expands what one exceptional content operator can produce. You’ll use it to research, organize, draft, adapt, and systematize content across formats. You will own what AI cannot: the story, the interview, the voice, the judgment, and the taste that make the finished work worth a business owner’s attention.

This is a hands-on role for an experienced, scrappy builder. You will set the creative bar by making the work yourself and directing the partners who help bring it to life. You’ll own stories from initial concept through final delivery, working directly with the Head of GTM, senior leadership, our investment bankers, and our engineering team.

Once the credibility foundation is in place, you will also have the opportunity to identify and build new organic formats and channels for reaching business owners.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Deal and client stories: Turn closed deals and client outcomes into memorable case studies, testimonials, and stories across written, visual, and video formats. Own each story from concept and interview preparation through final delivery.

 - Production: Source and direct videographers, photographers, and other creative partners. Own the brief, production plan, handoffs, captions, on-screen text, graphics, and final cut.

 - Blog and website credibility: Own OffDeal’s blog and core website content, including case-study pages, tombstones, team content, company updates, and other proof surfaces that help business owners understand and trust OffDeal.

 - AI-native content engine: Build repeatable workflows for finding stories, organizing source material, and turning one strong asset into many distinct, channel-native formats. Maintain a content library that teams across OffDeal can easily use.

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU

 - Are an outstanding storyteller with taste. You can absorb complex raw material, find the story that matters, and make it clear, human, and memorable.

 - Love building with AI. AI is already your default way of working, not a tool you’re evaluating. You’ve built prompt systems, Skills, or AI workflows that materially multiply your output, and you can demonstrate the leverage they create. If you believe AI inherently compromises serious creative work, this isn’t your role.

 - Are a builder and owner. You’re energized by taking an idea from initial concept through production and finished output.

 - Understand owner-operators. You know that playbooks designed for corporate software buyers do not automatically translate to practical, time-constrained business owners who are skeptical of jargon. You can make complex subjects simple without talking down to the audience.

 - Can run the machine. You are highly organized and resourceful, comfortable directing outside partners and managing several productions at once.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3–6 years creating content in a marketing, editorial, agency, or startup setting, with meaningful ownership of both the process and finished work.

 - A portfolio that demonstrates strong writing and range, including at least one video, customer story, or case study you drove from concept to finished asset.

 - Experience creating content for SMB owners and owner-operators, ideally in trades, healthcare practices, industrials, or other Main Street sectors.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Familiarity with financial services or M&A, or a track record of quickly mastering unfamiliar, technical subjects.

 - Experience testing, launching, or growing an organic content format or channel.

A specific degree is not required. We weigh what you’ve built far more heavily than your credentials.

OUR HIRING PROCESS

Our process includes a live work sample: raw material in, finished asset out, using the tools you actually work with. We care about the quality of the work, the speed of execution, and the leverage you create with the tools at your disposal.

As one of our founding engineers, you won’t just build software - you’ll shape the way Elyos works, interacts with customers, and grows. jobs.title: Founding Member, Life Sciences
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARGON

The next decade belongs to biology. Bio foundation models are turning experimental guesswork into prediction, and the industry built on that science is set to produce more medicine, faster, than at any point in history.

The bottleneck for bringing these medicines to patients will be everything downstream of the science: clinical & regulatory strategy, portfolio decision making, the governance reviews, launch planning. That work is still done by smart people manually assembling context from a hundred sources, and it moves at the speed of headcount.

Argon builds the AI workforce for that layer. Our platform provides workflow automation purpose-built for biopharma commercial and portfolio teams, specialized from the data model up.

We're an early-stage YC-backed company founded in 2024, working with top-tier pharma and several of the largest life sciences consultancies. We're growing quickly, with 7-figure ARR up 5x year-to-date.

We pride ourselves on outsized output, being kind, and balancing excellence and progress. Join us if you want to be productive, move fast, and shape the future.

WHY THIS ROLE

You'd be the first industry hire on the Life Sciences team. The Life Sciences team is the group of industry experts that help bridge industry expertise with AI systems. We are looking for an expert with first-hand experience navigating pharma’s portfolio strategy, governance and commercial operations to help us bridge that critical domain knowledge with our platform.

You will help our partners get value from our software products, drive deployments, and identify use-cases and opportunities to drive our product execution.

Concretely, the split looks like:

 - 40% client-facing business development. Industry events, prospect conversations, and translating what Argon does into the specific decision VPs in Commercial teams are trying to make next quarter.

 - 40% deployment. Hands-on onboarding, training, and working sessions with new and current accounts. You own whether users get real value in the first 60 days.

 - 20% product. You're the voice of the customer in our roadmap. Surface the workflows we're not serving and the gaps between what the current version of Argon can do and what the job actually requires.

This is a founding role. There is no playbook, no established territory, and no one above you who knows this domain better. You'll write the playbook and help to build this function from the ground up.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 6+ years in commercial and portfolio strategy in biopharma. Direct biotech or big pharma experience is preferred over pure consulting.

 - Deep working knowledge of pharma's internal governance process for clinical and commercial decision-making with first hand experience seeing how decisions actually get made.

 - Experience running client-facing, multi-stakeholder engagements with real complexity.

 - Genuine comfort operating without structure. The most common way this role fails is someone excellent who needs a defined process to work inside.

 - You already use AI tools in your own work.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Drive business development efforts including attendance of industry events and leading client conversations for tailored use cases of Argon’s platform

 - Lead customer deployments with hands-on training and working sessions to help users get value from the platform quickly

 - Help shape product strategy and roadmap by deeply understanding customer workflows and the gaps in the current product

COMPENSATION

Compensation is dependent on experience and fit. We aim for a culture of competitive market salary and top 10% in equity.

 - Cash compensation: $170,000 – $240,000

 - Equity: .2% - 1%
