jobs.description:
ABOUT VERITUS

Consumer lending and collections are among the last corners of financial services that AI has not reached. The average collections team still relies on human agents in call centers, dialing as many people as possible. AI can be transformative here, but the regulatory burden makes it very hard for lending and collections teams to put generic AI to work.

Veritus is the solution. We deploy production voice and text agents for consumer lenders and collections agencies, designed from the ground up to be fully compliant and effective in highly regulated conversations. At AWA, one in five collections calls our AI agent handles ends in a payment, 67% of those customers pay on the call itself, and the agent resolves more than 70% of conversations without a human. Read the case study at veritus.com/awa-case-study http://veritus.com/awa-case-study

We are backed by Y Combinator, Crosslink, Threshold, Surgepoint and others. We’ve been growing rapidly with founder-led sales, and this is our first full-cycle sales hire.

THE ROLE

You will find your own deals and close them.

Cold calling and conferences are the two strongest channels we have. We publish content, run digital outreach and take inbound as well, but the pipeline that closes tends to start with a rep who dials collections agencies and turns up at the industry events. You will do both, and then you will run what you source all the way to signature.

Outbound. Build the target list, write the sequences, and dial. You own the top of your own funnel, and the best predictor of your success here is how many collections operators you talk to each week.

Conferences and events. RMAI, ACA, Money20/20, LendIt, plus client dinners. Lending and collections is a small world where being known is a real asset. You will work these rooms and own the follow-up that comes out of them.

The whole deal. Discovery, demo, pricing, security review, redlines, signature. The CEO joins the deals that need a founder in the room. You run the rest.

Collections agencies and midsize lenders first. These deals move in weeks rather than quarters, and they are the core of your number.

Enterprise lenders next. Large fintech lenders and credit card issuers are already Veritus clients, and that is the growth path for this role. Those deals take longer and involve more people around the table. Over time they are where your number gets large.

Product input. Every "we already use X", every compliance question you cannot answer, every reason a deal dies comes straight back into the roadmap. You will be closer to the product than anyone outside engineering.

WHO YOU ARE

Two or more years selling, including at least one closing your own deals. You do not need a long track record. You do need to have taken deals from first conversation to signature yourself. If you have only ever booked meetings for someone else to close, this is not the right seat yet. If you have been an AE with an SDR feeding you and would rather not prospect, it is the wrong job too.

You will pick up the phone. Willingly. Cold calls are still the fastest way into a mid-sized prospect.

You will travel for events. Conferences are where this industry meets, and we expect you to come back from them with pipeline.

You already use AI every day. Claude should already be doing your account research, working out who actually owns collections at a target, drafting outreach that reads like a person wrote it, and pulling apart your call recordings. Show us what you have built.

You will learn the rules. FDCPA, TCPA, CFPB, right-party contact, roll rates, recovery rate. You do not need to know any of it on day one. You do need to be the kind of person who reads the regulation instead of guessing at it, because our clients get fined when vendors guess.

You are in San Francisco, in person. You will sit next to the CEO. Early sales teams learn faster in a room together.

Low ego, high standards. Calls get reviewed candidly here, from the CEO down. You should want that.

TOOLS YOU WILL USE ON DAY ONE

Claude for account research, outreach, call transcript analysis and industry briefings. HubSpot for CRM and pipeline. Apollo for contact data and sequencing. Granola for meeting notes. LinkedIn Sales Navigator for contact discovery. Plus whatever we build internally next, which you get first access to and will help us create.

WHY THIS ROLE, RIGHT NOW

Veritus is growing quickly and there are now more deals in front of us than founder-led sales can run. We are the clear leader in this segment, and the constraint on growth is selling capacity.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
About Strada

Strada is building the agentic workforce for insurance operations.

Our agents take calls, send texts, and answer emails, then complete the work: quoting new business, servicing policies, processing claims. They connect directly into the core systems insurers already run on, which is why they finish the job instead of routing it to a human.

Backed by Y Combinator and top-tier investors, Strada already automates millions of customer interactions for national carriers, third-party administrators, wholesalers and brokers representing $20B+ in annual premiums.

It is now certain that AI in insurance operations will become a multi-billion dollar category. The question is not if, but who wins. We are already ahead in deploying AI at scale and are defining the category.

This is a career-defining role for someone who wants to sell into a trillion-dollar industry at an inflection point for AI adoption.

A Day in the Life

As an Enterprise Account Executive at Strada, you’ll own the sales process end-to-end, from discovery to close, with some of the most respected brands in the insurance space.

Your day will include:

 - Driving new business with Operations, Claims, and Transformation leaders at large insurance carriers, brokers, wholesalers, and TPAs.

 - Running discovery and consultative demos that uncover inefficiencies in claims handling, customer service, and quote intake.

 - Mapping complex org structures and building multi-threaded relationships with both technical and business leaders.

 - Collaborating with product and engineering to communicate customer feedback and influence roadmap priorities.

 - Managing a clean, high-velocity pipeline in HubSpot with precision forecasting.

 - Closing deals that help insurance leaders scale service, reduce costs, and delight policyholders.

 - Acting as a trusted advisor, not a vendor, guiding customers through the path from manual service to AI automation.

You Bring

 - 5+ years of B2B enterprise sales experience, with a proven track record of exceeding quota.

 - Experience selling technical products to operations leaders, preferably in the insurance industry.

 - A strong understanding of complex sales processes with 6-figure to 7-figure ACVs.

 - A consultative approach and meticulous attention to detail, simplifying complexity, and earning trust.

 - A growth mindset, hungry to learn, iterate, and drive to perfect your GTM strategy.

 - Grit, resilience, and the ability to navigate long cycles and multiple stakeholders.

Bonus Points For

 - Experience selling enterprise software to the insurance industry.

 - Founding sales team or early-stage startup experience.

Who You Are

 - You're a business athlete, competitive, coachable, and relentless.

 - You thrive in ambiguity and early-stage environments.

 - You're a natural relationship builder and establish rapport by understanding your prospects through diligent preparation.

Our Investment in You

 - Top-of-market salary and uncapped OTE

 - Meaningful equity stake with significant upside.

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.

 - Flexible time off and paid holidays.

jobs.title: Demand Gen Lead
jobs.description:
DEMAND GENERATION LEAD

ABOUT BLAND AI

We’re a Series C startup that has raised over $100M from Emergence Capital, Scale Venture Partners, Y Combinator, and the founders of PayPal and Twilio.

Our mission is to build the world's most human AI phone agents. Thousands of businesses rely on Bland AI to automate customer conversations while delivering an experience customers actually enjoy.

We're growing quickly, and marketing plays a critical role in that growth. Every campaign, event, product launch, and piece of content exists for one reason: generate pipeline and help enterprise companies discover Bland.

We're looking for someone to own that engine.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Marketing at Bland is entering its next stage.

We've built a strong foundation across content, brand, events, product marketing, and paid acquisition. Now we're looking for someone to own the systems, campaigns, reporting, and optimization that turn those efforts into predictable pipeline.

You'll own demand generation end-to-end—from campaign strategy and paid media to attribution, lifecycle marketing, HubSpot operations, reporting, and conversion optimization.

This isn't a role where you'll inherit a perfectly optimized machine.

We're looking for someone excited to build one.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

OWN PIPELINE GENERATION

Own our demand generation strategy with one goal in mind: generate high-quality enterprise pipeline.

Build quarterly campaign plans across paid, email, events, ABM, content, and product launches while constantly improving efficiency and conversion rates.

BUILD OUR MARKETING ENGINE

Own HubSpot and marketing automation.

Create scalable lifecycle programs, lead routing, lead scoring, nurture campaigns, attribution models, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure that gives the entire company visibility into marketing performance.

RUN PAID ACQUISITION

Manage and optimize our paid programs across LinkedIn, Google, Meta, retargeting, and emerging channels.

Constantly test messaging, audiences, creative, and landing pages to improve ROI.

DRIVE ACCOUNT-BASED MARKETING

Partner closely with Sales to build campaigns targeting high-value enterprise accounts.

Coordinate personalized campaigns across advertising, outbound, events, gifting, and content.

OWN MARKETING ANALYTICS

Measure everything.

Build dashboards that track campaign performance, pipeline creation, CAC, conversion rates, attribution, and marketing efficiency.

Identify what's working, eliminate what's not, and continuously improve performance.

OPTIMIZE THE FUNNEL

Improve every stage of the buyer journey—from first website visit through closed-won.

Experiment with landing pages, lifecycle campaigns, nurture sequences, product demos, and conversion optimization.

PARTNER ACROSS MARKETING

Work closely with Brand, Content, Product Marketing, Growth, Events, Sales, and RevOps to ensure every marketing initiative contributes to pipeline.

MUST-HAVE QUALITIES

BUILDER MENTALITY

You've built demand generation programs from scratch or significantly improved existing ones.

You enjoy creating systems as much as running campaigns.

ANALYTICAL

You love dashboards, attribution, conversion rates, and understanding why campaigns succeed or fail.

Marketing without measurement isn't interesting to you.

HANDS-ON OPERATOR

You're comfortable jumping into HubSpot, launching campaigns, building workflows, writing emails, creating dashboards, or troubleshooting automation yourself.

OWNERSHIP

You don't wait for someone else to solve problems.

You identify bottlenecks, propose solutions, and execute.

STRONG TECHNICAL MARKETING SKILLS

You understand modern B2B demand generation across paid media, lifecycle marketing, marketing automation, CRM management, attribution, and reporting.

MISSION-ALIGNED

You want to help define how enterprise companies adopt AI over the next decade.

NICE TO HAVES

 - 5–7 years of B2B SaaS demand generation experience

 - Deep HubSpot expertise

 - Experience with enterprise sales motions

 - Experience building attribution models and marketing dashboards

 - Familiarity with ABM platforms and account-based marketing

 - SQL, RevOps, or marketing operations experience

 - Experience partnering closely with Sales teams
 
 

YOU'LL THRIVE HERE IF...

You love owning metrics.

You enjoy building systems that scale.

You care about pipeline more than vanity metrics.

You're excited by ambiguity and moving quickly.

You want to work alongside ambitious people who care deeply about winning.

You want your work to directly influence company growth.

AMBITION MATTERS MOST

We care more about what you've built than where you've worked.

If you've built demand generation engines, love solving complex growth problems, and are excited about building the next generation of enterprise AI, we'd love to meet you.

COMPENSATION & PERKS

 - Competitive salary

 - Meaningful equity

 - Comprehensive benefits

 - Beautiful office in Levi's Plaza, San Francisco

 - Work alongside one of the fastest-growing AI companies in the world

jobs.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT GIGA

Giga has recently raised a $61M Series A and is working with Fortune 500 customers to deploy the next generation of customer experience - real-time AI agents that can understand emotion, resolve issues instantly, and scale across the world's largest enterprises.

Industry leaders like DoorDash trust Giga with their most complex support and operations workflows across voice, chat, and email, in high-stakes regulated environments where accuracy and compliance matter. We're at an exciting inflection point.

While we've found real commercial success, our ambitions are larger: to become the go-to AI platform for all enterprise automation, powered by our voice superintelligence. The work affects millions of people every day, and our team has the autonomy to make true impact - with brilliant founders, a clear path forward, and the kind of momentum that defines generational companies.

If being part of that resonates with you, we'd love to hear from you!

 - Voice AI startup Giga raises $61M Series A https://fortune.com/2025/11/05/voice-ai-giga-raise-61-million-customer-service-series-a/

 - DoorDash and Giga Partnership https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7391576181009018883/

 

THE ROLE

We're hiring Senior Forward Deployed Engineers as we scale our FDE organization. This is a senior individual contributor role — for engineers who want to stay engineers: you'll be the technical anchor of a pod of FDEs, own our most complex enterprise deployments, and build the tooling and practices that make every deployment after yours faster. Your impact spans the org — the systems, patterns, and standards you build become how every pod operates.

You'll operate with real autonomy — architecture decisions, live production debugging, direct engagement with customer engineering leadership. No direct reports: your leadership shows up in code, design reviews, the engineers you level up, and an FDE org that gets epsilon better every day because you're in it.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the hardest deployments end-to-end. Architect agent systems for Fortune 500 environments, build enterprise integrations, and make the scope/speed/quality trade-off calls that ship production agents on aggressive timelines.

 - Be the technical anchor of your pod. Set the engineering bar through design and code reviews, mentor FDE I/II engineers, and serve as the escalation point for the hardest live issues — real-time voice latency, telephony edge cases, integration failures, agent quality regressions.

 - Build leverage, not just deployments. Create the eval harnesses, deployment tooling, debugging infrastructure, and reusable patterns that compound across every pod.

 - Drive the product feedback loop. Turn deployment learnings into prototypes and concrete asks, and work directly with core engineering to land platform improvements.

 - Face the customer as a technical peer. Run architecture discussions with customer engineering leaders and be the person they trust when production breaks.

 

WHO YOU ARE

 - Strong engineering foundation. 5+ years of production software engineering, ideally at companies known for high engineering bars. You've shipped and operated real systems at scale.

 - Deep on the stack. Expert in Python, APIs, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD. You debug distributed systems under pressure and learn new integration surfaces quickly.

 - AI-native. Hands-on with LLM agent systems — orchestration, tool calling, evals, context engineering — and the latency budgets real-time voice demands (or the chops to ramp fast).

 - Customer-tolerant. You can sit across from enterprise stakeholders, translate ambiguity into a plan, and stay calm when production is on fire in front of them.

 - High agency. You find the highest-leverage problem and go, with limited or no guidance.

 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Prior forward deployed / solutions engineering at an AI or enterprise software company

 - Real-time voice or conversational AI experience

 - Early-stage startup experience

 

PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base + bonus + equity

 - Catered lunch daily

 - Dinner stipend

 - $300/month wellness & commuter benefit (gym, fitness classes, mental health)

 - 401(k) plan

 - Medical, dental, and vision coverage
 
 

Giga is an equal opportunity employer. We're committed to providing equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Opportunistic
jobs.description:
Interfere is building the self-healing layer of the internet: software that detects issues, diagnoses root causes, and ships fixes before anyone notices something's broken. The goal is to empower founders, product managers, and designers to understand how the product they're building actually works in the real world. Software runs civilization. When it breaks, the world stutters. We're building its immune system. This is not a normal job – it demands taste, intensity, and obsession. Difficulty wakes the genius.

THE MOMENT

AI has democratized shipping code, but excellence remains scarce. We're creating the infrastructure that makes product excellence no longer aspirational but inevitable and expected. We've raised over $5.1M from world class investors like Y Combinator, Vercel Ventures, Hummingbird, Designer Fund, and many others to turn our vision into reality. This isn't about incremental improvements, but about fundamentally changing how reliable software gets built.

THE WORK

You'll operate at the intersection of the impossible and the inevitable. This role demands:

 - Depth over breadth – You'll go deeper into problems than most think necessary, finding elegance where others accept complexity

 - Craft at velocity – Ship exceptional work quickly without compromising on quality that matters. Both form and function, never just one or the other

 - "High Standards Win" – Question everything, rebuild from scratch when needed, never accept "that's how it's done" or "good enough"

 - Ownership without borders – Your domain is whatever needs doing to make Interfere exceptional. No excuses

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Immense pride in the work you do and a desire to build the best products on earth

 - Builders with taste – You know the difference between good and great, and you can't sleep until you've achieved the latter

 - Systems thinkers – You see patterns others miss

 - Relentless learners – You dive into unfamiliar domains and emerge with either expertise or a delusional drive to acquire it

 - Clear communicators – Complex ideas seem obvious when they find their way into your hands

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with developer tools, observability platforms, or infrastructure

 - Track record of being on a team that shipped products that people love

 - Portfolio of work that demonstrates exceptionality. If you don't have one, be creative

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Founding team equity and competitive compensation

 - Complete ownership of meaningful work

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage

 - Visa sponsorship for exceptional international candidates

HOW WE WORK

We're in-person in New York City, and believe proximity accelerates everything that matters, but we'll gladly help you move here. Send us proof of exceptional work you've shipped and a note about why Interfere resonates with you. We value proof of who you can be over who you've been.

jobs.title: Founding Product Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT INTERFERE

Interfere is building the self-healing layer of the internet: software that detects broken product experiences, understands what caused them, and helps teams fix them before users notice. Modern teams have logs, dashboards, traces, and session replay. They still find out about too many problems from their users. We exist to close that gap for engineers, PMs, designers, and founders who care how their product actually works in the real world. The product surface is large. The category is still being defined. The people who join now will shape the standards and the operating system of the company. We've raised $5.1M from Y Combinator, Vercel Ventures, Hummingbird, Designer Fund, and others. We're in person in New York City.

THE ROLE

You will own end-to-end features, from data model to interface, that define how the best teams understand and fix their products. You'll architect core systems, design the surfaces engineers actually use, and decide what "excellent" means for a category that doesn't exist yet.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD AND OWN

 - Detection and diagnosis systems that reason about codebases and runtime behavior at scale

 - Developer-facing interfaces that make complex system failures legible in seconds

 - Pipelines that ingest, structure, and correlate billions of product events

 - Agentic workflows that triage issues and propose or ship fixes safely

 - APIs and integrations that meet developers inside the tools they already use

 - The internal standards (for code, design, and judgment) that the next ten engineers will inherit

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've shipped production software that real users depend on, end to end, across the stack.

 - You move comfortably between frontend behavior, backend systems, and the seams between them.

 - You can take an ambiguous product or infrastructure problem, define the next useful step, and ship without waiting for a fully specified plan.

 - You can explain complex system behavior clearly enough that engineers, designers, and PMs can make the right decision quickly.

 - You are willing to stay with hard problems long enough to understand them deeply, not just route around them.

NICE TO HAVE

 - You are fluent in TypeScript and modern web tooling (Next.js, React, Node).

 - Worked on developer tools, observability, incident response, or session replay

 - Built or operated systems handling high-throughput event data

 - Shipped agentic or LLM-powered features into production

 - Distributed systems depth, or strong eye for product and UI craft (either is a strong asset; both is rare and valuable)

STRONG SIGNALS

 - A product, tool, or system you built that other engineers chose to use

 - Open-source work, technical writing, or research with real depth

 - Took on more scope than your title suggested at a previous company

 - Started something from zero: a company, a team, a product line

 - Picked up an unfamiliar domain quickly and shipped something good in it

 - A portfolio piece (code, product, writing) where the taste is obvious in the first 30 seconds

HOW WE WORK

We're in-person in New York City. We move quickly, write clearly, and expect high ownership. We care about the difference between something that works and something that is excellent. We expect you to push back when you disagree, and to do the work to be right when you do.

COMPENSATION AND LOGISTICS

 - Founding-team equity and competitive cash compensation (specific ranges shared in first conversation)

 - Health, dental, and vision

 - Visa sponsorship for exceptional international candidates

 - We'll help you move to New York

INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. Intro conversation with a founder

 2. Technical deep-dive on past work

 3. Paid project or pairing session on a real Interfere problem

 4. Onsite with the team in New York

 5. References and offer — we move fast and tell you where you stand

HOW TO APPLY

Send us your resume or LinkedIn, plus one piece of work we should look at: a repo, a live product, a technical essay, a side project, a postmortem. We want to see how you think and build. A short note on why Interfere helps, but the work matters more.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI/ML
jobs.description:
Interfere turns a product's invisible failures into shared problems the whole team can see and fix. Every app has places where users get confused, blocked, or forced to abandon a flow, but most of those moments never make it into a support ticket. We detect those failures in real-time and provide every person responsible for the fix with the context they need. When Interfere flags a broken checkout flow, the PM uses our data to prioritize the issue, the designer sees where the experience broke down, and the engineer pulls the trace underneath. We're building the operating system for product quality, so teams can move from scattered symptoms to a shared understanding of what's actually going wrong. We're a seven-person team in New York, with $5.1M raised from Y Combinator, Vercel Ventures, Hummingbird, Designer Fund, and others. Interfere is already running in production with design partners, which means the work you ship will immediately help real teams find and fix the failures costing them users today. The category is still being defined, but the product to fill this gap is inevitable, and the company that gets there first will own how the next decade of teams ship software. We're looking for the people who will move at the speed that demands.

THE ROLE

You'll own the intelligence layer that makes Interfere work. The product is only as good as the systems that decide what's broken, what caused it, and what to do about it — and those systems live inside the agents, evals, and inference pipelines you'll build. You'll work where research meets production, shipping things that run at scale against real codebases and runtime data. Concretely, this looks like building:

 - Agents that reason about codebases, traces, logs, and runtime behavior to find and explain bugs before users hit them, including the sandboxes they run in and the browsers and web research they use to investigate

 - LLM pipelines for triage, root-cause analysis, and automated fix proposals, with the model routing that sends each job to the right model at the right cost

 - Detection systems for anomalies in product behavior, performance, and user experience across noisy real-world data

 - The evals, datasets, observability, and feedback loops that move us from "this prompt feels good" to "this system measurably works and is getting better," architecting the standards for the agentic parts of a product that is still being defined

 - The context engineering that lets a model actually understand a customer's codebase: retrieval, indexing, context construction, and the integrations into their stack

 - Systems that get sharper over time, turning every bug found and fixed into signal that improves the next detection, so continual learning is a product advantage rather than an afterthought

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've shipped ML or LLM-powered systems into production, where real users depend on the output, not just a notebook or a demo

 - You move between research and engineering comfortably, and you pick up unfamiliar tech fast. You can go from a new framework or technique on Monday, to a working prototype by Friday, to an eval that tells you whether it's actually better the following week

 - You can own something 0→1, beginning to end. You can take an ambiguous AI problem, define the next useful step, and ship without waiting for a fully specified plan

 - You treat evals as a first-class engineering problem. When the system is making decisions for users, intuition isn't a substitute for measurement

 - Experience with agent architectures, tool use, multi-step reasoning, or autonomous workflows in production

NICE TO HAVE

 - Background in code understanding, program analysis, or systems that reason over source code

 - Built retrieval, RAG, or context-construction systems against large or messy data

 - Anomaly detection, time-series modeling, or learned monitoring systems experience

 - Internalized understanding of AI/ML systems - a heightened understanding of the inner workings of the systems you'll be building

STRONG SIGNALS

 - An agentic system you built that other engineers actually chose to use, or that ran in production at meaningful scale

 - Open-source work, technical writing, or research with real depth — bonus if it shows where you disagree with the consensus

 - You've shipped agents or LLM features into production and have informed opinions about what works, what's hype, and what's still broken

 - You designed and ran evals that materially changed the trajectory of a product or research direction

 - You started something from zero, whether a research direction, a product feature, or an internal tool

 - You dropped into an unfamiliar domain, whether a new modality, a new codebase, or a new sub-field, and shipped real work in it fast

HOW WE WORK

 - We're in person in New York City. The hardest parts of building Interfere, from system design to architecture tradeoffs to taste calls on the product, happen faster and better at a whiteboard with people physically in the same room.

 - We measure work, not hours. Time at a desk is a poor proxy for whether work is getting done. But there's a lot to do and genuine urgency to being the category winners. Most people who do well here end up putting in serious hours because the problems are interesting and the upside is real.

 - We ship daily, and we ship deliberately. Speed and taste are not in tension here. Every line of code is a choice: we don't let tech debt accumulate because velocity is easier. We write the code we would want to inherit, while still pushing meaningful changes every day.

 - The roadmap is structure, not scaffolding. We plan out the week, so there's structure to what you take on. But the items on that roadmap are whole features and subsystems, each one a project in itself. If you see another problem along the way that needs solving, you own that too. It's your job to make your work into what it needs to be.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.description:
THE MISSION

America's industrial base runs on systems built in the 1980s.

Billions of dollars in critical components (F-35 parts, industrial assemblies, electronics, bolts, and hoses) still move through email threads, excel sheets, and disconnected ERPs.

We're replacing that with an AI-native platform that makes aerospace, electronics, industrial, and defense supply-chain operations nearly autonomous. Faster quoting. Faster procurement. Full visibility. Real operational intelligence for the companies our nation depends on.

QUICK FACTS

 - YC W25 company. Top 5% growth in batch

 - Raised $10M+ from investors including Paul Graham, SV Angel, Pear VC, and CRV

 - Team of 20 co-live in our Warsaw & SF Hacker Houses

 - 7 figure ARR transacting ~$50M a week through our system

Full-time, hybrid | Dallas, TX; Fort Worth, TX; Miami, FL; Los Angeles, CA; Chicago, IL; Cincinnati, OH; Cleveland, OH; Long Island, NY preferred

THE ROLE

We send you a list of company headquarters in your area. Your job is to walk in, talk your way past the front desk and into a meeting with an executive, and walk out with a follow-up meeting booked for one of our founders. That’s the whole job, and it’s harder and more valuable than it sounds.

Drive to ~5-10 locations per day; spend the rest of your hours at home doing research, phone/email follow-ups, and logging your progress (conversations had, locations visited, details on each person you spoke to) for the team. Everything is logged in our CRM before you sign off each day.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 2+ years in a professional environment. Bonus points for software sales, investment banking, private equity, VC, consulting, or tech.

 - Infectious charisma and professional presence in front of senior executives.

 - High EQ and the ability to think in second-order effects.

 - Able to be in the field minimum 3 days a week

 - Authorized to work in the United States. We do not sponsor visas for this role.

 - 21 or older.

 - Valid driver's license, reliable vehicle, and current auto insurance.

 - Comfortable walking into a building cold and talking your way into the room of whoever runs it

 - Disciplined about logging activity. No CRM entry, no credit.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in distribution, supply chain, defense, or similar fields

 - Data analysis or programming skills.

WHO YOU ARE

 - Rejection is fuel, not friction.

 - High-agency. Nobody is watching you drive between stops.

 - Sharp judgment about who the real decision-maker is and how to reach them.

 - Coachable. We iterate the playbook weekly while you help write it.

COMPENSATION

 - Base pay: local minimum wage

 - $500 per qualified meeting. $500 for every qualified decision-maker meeting (C-suite, SVP, or VP) you book that is held. Uncapped.

 - $1,000 per meeting above quota. Once you exceed monthly quota, each additional qualified meeting that is booked and held pays $1,000 in place of the standard $500 rate.

If a guaranteed salary matters more to you than upside, do not apply. This role pays based on results, not hours.

20-minute phone screen → 45-minute interview with role-play → Final interview with a founder, including a live door simulation

Our immediate priority is compliance and tax risk management . Tax planning and optimization are valuable, but secondary to strong experience in remediation, audits, investigations, tax controversy, and dealings with Mexican fiscal authorities. This is a hands-on leadership role, not a purely advisory or supervisory position. 
 
 The expected outcome: 
 This role will suit someone who is energized by the opportunity to bring order to a fast-moving environment. 
 You are naturally structured, but not rigid. You do not need every process to be mature, every responsibility to be perfectly defined, or every piece of information to arrive neatly packaged before you can make progress. You take initiative, ask the right questions, connect the dots, and turn unresolved issues into a clear path forward. 
 You are also genuinely hands-on. You can lead others, but you are equally willing to roll up your sleeves and get into the work when the situation requires it. You operate well autonomously, take ownership through completion, and see building stronger processes as part of the job, not as a reason the job cannot be done. 
 
 Lead federal and local tax compliance, including ISR, IVA, payroll taxes, withholdings, CFDI requirements, and informational filings.

 Assess tax exposures and establish clear remediation plans. 
 Develop tax policies, controls, technical criteria, and review procedures. 
 Provide practical tax guidance on products, commercial initiatives, compensation arrangements, and strategic decisions. 
 Support the tax implications of Baubap’s potential transition to a SOFIPO. 
 Manage external tax advisors, auditors, and legal counsel. 
 Improve tax processes through automation, ERP capabilities, and stronger data validation. 
 Lead and develop the tax team while remaining directly involved in execution. 
 Identify compliant tax planning opportunities once core compliance priorities are under control. 
 
 
 Preferred Additional Qualifications and Experience: 
 
 Substantial experience managing Mexican tax compliance . 
 Deep knowledge of ISR, IVA, payroll taxes, withholdings, CFDI requirements, and applicable local taxes. 
 Proven experience managing tax audits, fiscal authority requests, investigations, disputes, and tax controversy. 
 Direct experience interacting with SAT and other Mexican fiscal authorities. 
 Strong understanding of tax accounting, reconciliations, provisions, filings, payments, and CFDI information. 
 Ability to identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective actions. 
 Hands-on experience reviewing calculations, filings, reconciliations, and technical positions. 
 Experience leading a tax function and coordinating cross-functional teams. 
 Ability to work autonomously in a remote and fast-moving environment. 
 Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Tax Law, Law, Finance, or a related field. 
 Strong communication skills in Spanish and English. 
 
 
 What Makes Someone Exceptional For This Role: 
 
 Experience in a Big Four firm or another recognized tax advisory or audit firm. 
 Experience in a complex, high-volume, or rapidly changing organization. 
 Experience with ERPs, tax platforms, and automation tools. 
 Experience developing tax controls, policies, and compliance processes. 
 Experience managing external tax advisors, auditors, and legal counsel. 
 Experience in financial services, SOFOMs, SOFIPOs, fintechs, or another regulated business. 
 Experience supporting regulatory or accounting transformations 
 
 
 What we can offer: 
 
 Being part of a multicultural, highly driven team of professionals 
 20 vacation days / year + 75% holiday bonus (Prima Vacacional) 
 1 month (proportional) of Christmas bonus (Aguinaldo) 
 Food vouchers 
 Health & Life insurance 
 Competitive salary

jobs.title: Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
About Bland AI

Bland AI is the voice AI platform built for enterprises with high-volume, complex call center operations. Bland started by solving the core infrastructure problem that made voice AI unusable for business: latency, reliability, and the inability to handle real-world complexity. Where early voice AI took 7 seconds to respond and could only handle basic FAQs, Bland built the entire stack from scratch.

 

Today, Bland's platform fully resolves up to 65% of inbound calls autonomously – handling not just FAQs, but multi-step workflows, authentication logic, business-rule-based routing, and live data lookups. For large call center operators, each percentage point of resolution Bland drives is worth $500K–$1M+ per year in savings. Bland's biggest technical differentiator: they own and operate the entire voice AI stack in-house – transcription, LLM, and TTS – rather than relying on third-party API providers. This is a deliberate architectural choice that enables the uptime guarantees, data security standards, and customization depth that regulated industries require.

 

Why This Role Matters

We are roughly 80 people today and operate with a very lean internal team. There is currently one person in finance. This role exists because the company needs someone who can help build the financial and operational foundation as we grow.

This is not the most glamorous role and it is not narrowly defined. You will do a lot of everything. The work is foundational, sometimes repetitive, and often unstructured. It is also one of the best ways to learn how a startup actually works.

 

Role Overview

Day to day, this role requires strong organization and comfort working in low context environments. Often, you will be given problems, not instructions. You will regularly need to figure out what the right next step even is before executing.

Much of your time will be spent supporting compensation plans and commissions, building reporting and dashboards, analyzing bookings and revenue trends, helping with budgeting and forecasting, and improving the systems the company uses to make decisions. You’ll partner closely with accounting, sales, and operations to ensure leadership has accurate data and actionable insights.

You will work across teams and functions and will regularly interact with leadership. Because the finance function is largely unbuilt, there is direct visibility into how decisions are made and how the business operates. You will see the full picture earlier than most people in their careers.

Over time, as you build trust and ownership, this role can expand significantly. You may take on larger projects, help define processes, or move into more strategic finance or operations work.

Ideal Candidate Profile / Role Requirements

This role is for someone early in their career who wants responsibility and learning over polish and prestige.

You should have some exposure to finance, accounting, operations, consulting, or a related field, but deep experience is not required. What matters more is that you care, you are capable, and you follow through.

You should be comfortable with ambiguity. Startups are chaotic. Things change. Systems are imperfect. You should be energized by that rather than frustrated by it.

You should have strong problem solving instincts and be willing to do unglamorous work well. The people who succeed here are the ones who treat small details seriously and take pride in making things work.

 

Must-Have Experience

• Bachelors degree in Finance, Economics, or a related track

• Strong financial foundation, including comfort in Power BI, Excel, and other tools

• Highly self-directed — does not need heavy management or a fully built playbook to be effective

 

Nice-to-Have Experience

• 1+ years experience in IB (Tech focus preferred), in a finance role at a high growth start-up, or an equivalent role

• Experience with accounting, FP&A, and revenue recognition

• Experience with M&A or strategic financial projects

 

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary range is 80,000 to 135,000 dollars depending on experience.

 - Equity range is 50,000 to 150,000 dollars.

 - Health insurance, dental, vision, and a 401K is provided.

 - Unlimited PTO.

This is a role for someone with energy, curiosity, strong technical instincts, and a real give a f*ck factor who wants to build something real and grow fast while doing it.

This is a full-time, in-person role based in San Francisco. Candidates must already be authorized to work in the United States.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff
jobs.description:
MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF

Inference performance depends on how efficiently models use the underlying hardware. Techniques across kernels, compilers, runtimes, and serving systems can dramatically improve latency and throughput, but these optimizations are difficult, hardware-specific, and slow to reproduce across new accelerators. And none of it counts until it is running in a customer's production traffic.

At Wafer, we are building AI systems that automatically optimize inference workloads across silicon. The goal is fungible token capacity. Any accelerator optimized toward serving inference most efficiently.

Wafer is well funded and serves trillions of tokens a month for mission critical workloads. We serve the highest performance inference to fast-growing AI startups.

Members of Technical Staff build the systems that make that possible and own the customers running on them. There is no separate solutions team, and no layer between you and the workload.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Develop and optimize high-performance computing kernels, and work across inference engine internals and serving infrastructure

 - Develop AI agents to do autonomous inference engineering

 - Design, deploy, and operate heterogeneous clusters across vendors

 - Own customer accounts end to end. Sales gets the first meeting. From there you decide what to prove, you build it, you keep it running in production, and you carry the relationship

 - Win the technical evaluation. Prove Wafer on the customer's own workload rather than a synthetic benchmark, and be the person who can explain the result to their engineers

 - Own production for your accounts. When latency moves or error rates climb, you find it, you fix it or route it, and you are who the customer hears from

 - Inform product roadmap. You sit closer than anyone to how Wafer behaves under real load, and the engineering team builds against what you report

 

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You are an exceptional engineer. You have shipped and operated production systems, and you can still open a profiler, read a trace, and find the problem yourself. Inference experience helps, but it matters more that you can be handed an unfamiliar system and own it inside a week.

 - You have owned a customer relationship. You can name an account that was yours, say what was going wrong, and describe what you personally did about it.

 - You are credible in a room full of engineers. You can take a skeptical ML team through a benchmark, defend the methodology, and concede the point when they are right.

 - You work without a spec. The problem arrives half-defined from a customer who does not yet know what they need, and you come back with a scoped answer rather than a list of questions.

 

HOW WE EVALUATE

We score every candidate on seven values:

 1. Infinitely Resourceful

 2. Exceptionalism

 3. Unreasonable Standards

 4. Company Over Self

 5. High EQ

 6. Learns Quickly

 7. First Principles Thinker

 

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - $250K + generous equity.

 - Fully covered medical, dental, and vision insurance.

 - Daily lunch and dinner, unlimited PTO, and parental leave.

 - $1K/month housing stipend (post-tax) if you live within walking distance (0.5 miles) from the office.

 - Covered Uber/Waymo from/to office.

 - Relocation allowance and benefits.

 - Visa sponsorship available.

 

HOW WE WORK

On-site in San Francisco, five days a week. Small team with massive surface area and ownership. You operate with complete autonomy of how to solve problems. We don't see engineers as code writers, but as problem solvers. You will work across the stack to build a company scaling extremely quickly.

This is not a role that lives in meetings. Nearly all of your time is engineering. What makes it different is who that engineering is for: you are responsible for a named set of customers, their workloads run on what you build, and you are the person they hear from when it matters.

You'll work at the intersection of clinical expertise, quality assurance, and AI. Rather than reviewing a handful of patient charts each day, you'll help build systems that review thousands correctly.

This is not a bedside or utilization review position. It's an operations and quality role for a nurse who enjoys finding edge cases, improving processes, and translating clinical judgment into scalable automation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

AUDIT CLINICAL QA PERFORMANCE

Review charts processed by our clinical automation platform for accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Validate whether documentation supports services, identify incorrect classifications, and investigate why automation errors occurred.

IMPROVE CLINICAL AUTOMATION LOGIC

BUILD CLINICAL REVIEW STANDARDS

SUPPORT CUSTOMER IMPLEMENTATIONS

WHY THIS ROLE

Influence the product. Work side-by-side with engineering to shape how AI understands home health and hospice documentation.

jobs.title: Compliance Lead
jobs.description:
tl;dr: We’re automating compliance for banks and fintechs with AI agents that work on existing systems like human analysts. We’re looking for someone who understands both compliance and product management, someone who can turn regulatory workflows into scalable systems that help define how our AI agents reason, decide, and learn.

BACKGROUND

If you’ve worked in compliance, you’ve seen it firsthand: the endless reviews, duplicate alerts, and outdated systems that make even simple controls take hours. The rules make sense; the systems don’t.

Sphinx is fixing that. We build AI analysts that work inside browsers and internal systems just like humans — automating AML, KYC, KYB, and transaction monitoring end-to-end.

Instead of replacing judgment, our agents replicate it – learning from analyst feedback, explaining their reasoning, and improving over time. The result: faster onboarding, fewer false positives, and compliance teams that focus on decisions, not data entry.

Banks and fintechs across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and LatAm use Sphinx agents to handle 90% of their manual work and cut costs by 4x.

WHY JOIN SPHINX

 1. Redefine compliance: Banks spend $50B a year hiring thousands of analysts to manage compliance operations. You’ll design how financial crime prevention works in the age of AI – replacing checklists and manual reviews with robust reasoning systems that explain their logic.

 2. Work directly with clients: You’ll collaborate with banks, fintechs, and MSBs to deploy automation that meets real-world standards.

 3. Build at the frontier: You’ll work with engineers to design interpretable, auditable, and explainable AI systems that regulators can trust.

 4. We have never lost a deal to a competitor: Yes you heard that right, we’ve won every RFP we’ve been in.

 5. Small team, big surface area: Our co-founders previously sold an AI company & have built ML systems that scaled to millions of users and closed deals with major banks. The rest of our team in SF includes PhDs, industry experts, and competitive coders.

WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

Define how our agents think. That means turning complex regulations into structured, machine-readable logic – and ensuring it works across jurisdictions, languages, and edge cases.

Partner with customers to understand how their compliance processes are actually done, then design products that remove the bottlenecks: mapping workflows, refining alerts, improving output quality & accuracy, and building transparency into every decision.

You’ll collaborate with engineering to make sure every product decision is explainable and compliant by design – ensuring regulatory adherence, technical precision, and customer success.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You bring real compliance experience: You’ve spent 3–5 years in AML, risk, or compliance roles at a bank, fintech, or regtech – and you know how investigations, onboarding, and escalations actually work.

 - You bridge compliance and product: You can translate regulatory logic into product requirements engineers can act on – turning policies, SOPs, and edge cases into automated workflows.

 - You think in systems: You know how to deconstruct manual review processes, identify leverage points, and design scalable automation.

 - You care about false-positives: you know how to use metrics to understand issues, and love diving deeper to find a pattern.

 - You’re impact-obsessed: You want to see your work move the company forward – every day.

jobs.title: Growth Marketer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

We’re building the infrastructure that powers the procurement and disposition of assets across America’s essential industries, automating everything from discovery and payments to freight, warranty, and financing. Today, Garage operates in cities and towns across all 50 states and has surpassed $100M+ in annualized transaction volume on the platform.

If you move fast, hold a high bar, and want meaningful ownership in building a category-defining company, Garage is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a strong marketing generalist to be a key driver of organic growth. You'll find creative and cost-efficient ways to acquire customers, grow our audience, and build our brand across a variety of surfaces, including but not limited to organic social, partnerships, press, and SEO/AEO. This is a versatile role on a lean team, and you'll need a deep understanding of what actually drives impact and a bias to action and experimentation.

 - Take leveraged swings. Collaborate across marketing, sales, and engineering to find plays that drive outsized, compounding growth.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

NICE TO HAVE

OUR VALUES

 - Take Big Swings. We are here to transform an overlooked industry—not make small improvements around the edges. We set ambitious goals, take calculated risks, and push through setbacks. We never trade lasting impact for short-term comfort.

 - Customers Come First. Our customers operate in an industry burdened by slow, expensive, and outdated processes. We attack the problems that cost them the most and measure our success by the time and money we give back to them.

 - Play For the Front of the Jersey. We put the mission ahead of ourselves. We challenge each other directly, support each other relentlessly, and step up whenever the team needs us. We win together, and we have fun doing it.

Why Join Garage?

 - Help shape the company. Join as one of our first 40 employees and work directly alongside the founders.

 - Build from a strong foundation. We’ve raised $18M, including a $13.5M Series A, from Y Combinator, Initialized Capital, Infinity Ventures, FJ Labs, and other leading investors.

 

WHAT WE OFFER

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Humaans is building the next generation of infrastructure for the workplace; software designed for companies that are scaling fast, operating globally, and pushing into new boundaries.

What started as a system of record has evolved into a broader platform for operating people globally. With Athena, our agentic AI layer, Humaans moves beyond data management into intelligent orchestration, connecting workflows across HR, IT, Finance, and Operations so organisations can act faster and with greater confidence, redefining how work gets done.

We work with ambitious teams across Europe and the US, from AI-native companies like Lovable, Poolside, Fyxer AI, and Tandem Health, to established, high-growth organisations scaling internationally and through acquisition, including Quantexa, Sellpy, Manychat, Gigs, Croud, and Threecolts. These teams don’t buy software for features,they buy leverage. The ability to run faster, cleaner, and with more control as complexity compounds.

To date, we’ve raised $20m in venture funding from some of the most respected founders, operators, and funds in technology: Lachy Groom (Physical Intelligence), Stewart Butterfield (Slack), Tobias Lütke (Shopify), Dylan Field (Figma), Jeff Weiner (LinkedIn), Claire Johnson (Stripe), Oliver Jay (OpenAI), Jay Simmons (Bond) as well as Y Combinator, Moonfire, Frontline Ventures, Pathlight Ventures, and Exor.

If you have massive ambition and want to work on a hard problem, with a small team that moves fast, at a moment when the category is genuinely up for grabs - this is it.

THE ROLE

Revenue teams used to scale by adding people. Increasingly, they scale by building better systems. We’re looking for a GTM Engineer to own the infrastructure behind how Humaans finds, engages and converts customers, turning our go-to-market strategy into automated systems that can operate at scale.

This is a builder role, not a reporting role. You’ll sit across RevOps, Sales and Marketing and own the connective tissue between them: data pipelines, enrichment, buying signals, lead scoring, routing, AI agents and outbound infrastructure. These systems determine which accounts we pursue, what we know about them and what happens next.

When a process is manual, slow or dependent on an individual rep, you’ll look for a better way to build it. Your impact should scale beyond your own output because the systems you create keep working, learning and improving.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the foundations of our GTM data, keeping HubSpot trustworthy through automated enrichment, hygiene routines and clear ownership rules

 - Build enrichment and scoring workflows that turn raw firmographic, behavioural and signal data into ranked, ready-to-action target accounts

 - Design signal-based plays that identify meaningful buying signals and trigger the right action at the right moment

 - Own cold email as a core outbound channel, including sending infrastructure, deliverability, inbox health, personalisation and monitoring

 - Deploy AI agents for research, personalisation, CRM updates and other repetitive GTM workflows, with guardrails that protect quality and our brand

 - Connect GTM tools through APIs, defining sources of truth and designing how data moves reliably between systems

 - Launch new outbound campaigns continuously, run structured experiments and feed what you learn back into the system

 - Treat copy as a testable variable, systematically experimenting with subject lines, opening angles, messaging and CTAs, then incorporating what works into templates and agent prompts

 - Partner closely with SDRs, AEs and leadership to identify bottlenecks and ship solutions in days rather than waiting for lengthy projects

 - Design experiments with clear success metrics, stop investing in what underperforms and scale what works

 - Operate at volume, managing thousands of leads moving through our systems without compromising data quality or targeting

 - Continuously look for places where automation, AI or better infrastructure can give the GTM team more leverage

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A systems mindset paired with strong commercial instincts. You care about elegant workflows, but ultimately judge them by whether they help us create and close more revenue

 - Hands-on experience with a modern GTM stack, including tools such as Clay, HubSpot or Salesforce, enrichment providers and sequencing platforms

 - Strong understanding of outbound, including ICP definition, targeting, lead scoring, deliverability and what effective outreach actually requires

 - The ability to write effective outbound copy and improve it through testing, using reply and positive-reply rates rather than vanity metrics to understand what works

 - Enough SQL and Python or JavaScript to solve problems independently, alongside confidence reading API documentation, handling authentication and connecting systems

 - Fluency with AI coding and automation tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, n8n or Zapier, with the ability to build, test and ship workflows end to end

 - An experimental mindset. You define what success looks like, test assumptions, measure results and use feedback loops to make systems better

 - A bias towards building. You learn by tinkering, shipping and seeing what happens rather than waiting until you know everything

 - Strong attention to detail, particularly around data quality, automation reliability and the downstream consequences of changes you make

 - A track record of building systems that revenue teams actually use. Your background could be SDR, RevOps, Growth, Product or something else entirely

YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You’re more interested in reporting on GTM performance than building the systems that change it

 - You prefer administering tools and processes rather than questioning how they work and rebuilding them when there’s a better approach

 - You need requirements to be fully defined before you start building

jobs.title: R&D Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARIBOU

International Tax is a rigged system. Tax rules get ever more complicated, compliance gets more expensive, and the Big Four controls the expertise. They charge fees that only giant companies can afford, while smaller businesses are left flying blind.

Caribou is a tax platform designed to make international tax accessible to every global business. We're fixing Transfer Pricing first, where one million businesses are in need, but only ten thousand experts exist. R&D relief is our next product.

Our backers include Y Combinator, Accel, Lakestar and angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies in London and San Francisco.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Caribou is building a new R&D tax offering at the intersection of transfer pricing and innovation funding — and we're looking for a Senior Manager to own it end-to-end.

This isn't a pure advisory role. You'll be working alongside our engineering team to productize the service: systematising claim processes, building tooling, and turning what used to be manual consulting work into something scalable. The mix of hands-on R&D tax advisory with product instinct is what makes this different from a standard tax consultancy position. We're looking for someone who's been in the trenches with HMRC and/or the IRS on R&D claims, with a passion for building things that don't exist yet.

You'll report directly to our Head of Tax, James Boreham, and have real ownership of the vertical from day one.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Liaise directly with customers to assess R&D eligibility and understand their business.

 - Own the end-to-end claim process, from notification of intent to claim through advance assurance, drafting, submission, and defending claims under enquiry.

 - Translate your real-world claims experience into rules, checklists, and logic that can be built into an automated product.

 - Identify what proof and documentation a claim actually needs to withstand scrutiny, and work with the team to design data capture that gets it right the first time.

 - Explain R&D concepts to non-specialists, ranging from founders to operations leads, to accountants.

 - Coordinate with a customer's other advisors, including bookkeepers, lawyers and other tax experts.

 - Shape the R&D product itself - pricing, scope, and what should be automated versus handled by a specialist.

 - Determine a customer's reporting obligations and build the workflows that generate the necessary documents.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

 - Meaningful hands-on experience with HMRC and/or IRS R&D claims, including defending claims under enquiry

 - Deep practical understanding of what proof and evidence a tax authority actually requires, beyond the written guidance

 - You take ownership and enjoy driving multiple projects involving a wider range of stakeholders

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment with ambiguous and rapidly evolving priorities

BONUS POINTS

 - Experience across both UK and US R&D regimes

 - Startup experience

PERKS & BENEFITS (FOR UK-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES)

 - Competitive salary

 - Generous EMI options

 - 100% book subsidy

 - Pension

 - Health Insurance

 - Custom WFH equipment setup
 

London-based, hybrid.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Payments
jobs.description:
We are making travel effortless. Join us.

Whether it's to visit the people closest to us, starting an exciting adventure, or a career-defining business trip, travel is an essential part of our lives. Yet we've all experienced the aches and pains of getting to our destination. Today, more than 4 billion airline passengers rely on technology that hasn't kept up with the expectations of the modern connected traveller.

That's why we've started to rebuild the infrastructure that underpins the travel industry. We're on a mission to unravel travel, simplifying systems and building the tools that will make the future of travel effortless.

We were part of Y Combinator S18's cohort and we are backed by Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures and Kima Ventures, a fantastic set of investors that has helped build some of the world's largest companies.

Payments at Duffel

Our Payments team looks after the infrastructure that powers our travel operations: payment acceptance, supplier settlement, reconciliation, commission tracking and payouts, billing, and more. These are some of the hardest and most interesting challenges Duffel is facing as we operate as a global travel platform.

About the role

As the Product Manager for Payments, you'll own the roadmap for the operational backbone of our Payments product. The role is largely internal. You'll work closely with Finance, Engineering, and Operations to optimise settlement, billing, commissions and reconciliation, and to build the platform services that other Duffel teams, and eventually external partners, rely on. There's a customer-facing dimension too, but the bulk of the work is making the inside of the product as well-engineered as the outside.

You'll spend most of your time with engineering, define the weekly goals and milestones for the product squad, work closely with internal stakeholders (Finance especially), and bring real depth to a team that values getting the detail right. You'll own the overall Payments roadmap, to shape where your areas go next, including parts of the product we've barely touched yet.

What we're looking for

 - You're fluent in payments without being wedded to the rails. You understand how money moves (settlement, reconciliation, commissions, FX, chargebacks) but you're more energised by building great internal product on top of that than by optimising payment rails for their own sake.

 - You're a builder. Most of what this team needs, we build rather than buy. You like designing the systems, automated commission flows, supplier reconciliation, billing, that Finance, Operations and eventually external partners rely on.

 - You translate between worlds. A big part of this job is sitting between Finance and Engineering: turning finance narratives into technical requirements, technical realities into language Finance and Ops can act on, and getting both sides to genuinely understand each other.

 - You prioritise ruthlessly. This is a small, in-demand team (three engineers) constantly trading internal needs against customer-facing work. You're good at deciding what matters now and saying no to the rest.

 - You sweat the detail. Reconciliation logic, commission edge cases, audit trails: this is the kind of work that energises you rather than drains you.

 - You shape product direction. You can take a roadmap area, work out where it should go and why, and drive it.

 - You've got commercial instinct. You can spot when something we've built for ourselves (like reconciliation) could become a product customers would pay for.

 - You're API-literate. You don't need to write code, but you can have a meaningful conversation with engineering about how systems actually work.

 - You handle ambiguity, breaking complex, undefined problems into a clear way forward, and use both quantitative and qualitative analysis to back your calls.

 - You think being challenged on your assumptions makes you better, and that challenging others helps them grow.

 - Nice to have: exposure to travel-specific payments (BSP, IATA, virtual cards, agency settlement). Useful, not essential.

Some reasons why you’ll love working here:

🏡 Work From Anywhere - work abroad for part of the year

🛩️ Duffel Travel Allowance - because building in travel should come with travel perks

🍼 Enhanced parental leave

🧘 Sabbatical options - proper time to recharge

🪩 A Shoreditch office near Liverpool Street + regular team socials

💰 Competitive salary + potential equity

 

You’ll join a smart, kind, ambitious team building something meaningful in travel with real ownership, autonomy, and the chance to shape how we hire as we scale and we think that’s pretty exciting.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Founding Community Lead
jobs.description:
This role is full-time, in-person, in NYC.

WHO WE ARE

At Ploy, we’re building the first growth automation software with your website at its core. We serve innovative operators at growth and marketing agencies, tech start-ups, and some traditional industries as well.

They build their website with Ploy’s agents, and then those agents automatically research the landscape and business context, identify winning strategies for account based personalization, SEO/AEO, conversion rate optimization, and ship dozens of on-brand, on-strategy web pages in seconds to drive traffic and conversions.

Our vision is to completely re-define the concept of a marketing website in today’s agentic world.

And tear-down the broken, archaic low-code tech stacks of the last generation of website builders. With agents, we can unburden a world of story-tellers from manual work, long timelines, and being blocked by internal and external resourcing, and return them to a world of, “yes, and” + “let’s just do it”.

It’s a big, scary ambitious vision, but our team is uniquely positioned to do it.

Some of the best design engineers and growth engineers in the world.

World-class investors.

And one of our co-founders is Bryant Chou, the former co-founder and CTO of Webflow. (Yes, uniquely positioned)

And last but not least, hopefully you, the one reading this 😄

ABOUT THE ROLE

From our experience at Webflow and other category-defining companies, we believe deeply in the power of community and want to invest in this channel from day 1 to cultivate growth, engagement, and connection.

Ploy is hiring its first Community Lead to own everything that this involves. You'll be the reason our users go from lurkers to power users, and from power users to believers.

This role sits at the intersection of growth and community. That means converting free and low-usage accounts into high-usage ones through education, activation, and genuine connection. And it means turning our most engaged users, creators, and partners into evangelists who pull others into the ecosystem.

Agencies get special focus here. Each one is a force multiplier with its own roster of clients and its own audience, so a big part of this role is turning them into partners who run their own events and create their own content under the Ploy umbrella.

You'll be the connective tissue between Ploy's product, vision, and the marketers and agencies who are redefining what it means to build for the web.

This is a high-ownership, cross-functional role at an early-stage startup. You'll be building from zero: the programs, the platforms, the rituals, and the culture. That means you'll have real influence over how one of the most exciting categories in AI-powered growth takes shape — not just inside Ploy, but across the broader ecosystem of AI-pilled GTM operators who are hungry for a place to learn, share, and grow together.

What you'll own:

 - Community platform & presence — Launch and run Ploy's community hub, creating a space where growth managers, in-house operators, and agency builders want to spend time

 - Agency partner programs — Build Ploy's agency program from zero: recruit and onboard partner agencies, then equip them to become force multipliers. Give them the playbooks, co-branded assets, and support to run their own events — workshops, client sessions, local meetups — and create their own content — case studies, tutorials, social — that grows their business and the Ploy ecosystem at the same time

 - Education & enablement — Develop content, playbooks, webinars, and tutorials that help our ICP get more out of Ploy and stay ahead of the curve on agentic GTM strategy

 - Member growth & engagement — Design and run programs that drive community growth, deepen retention, and turn power users into advocates

 - Events & activation — Organize both digital and in-person moments that bring the community to life — AMAs, roundtables, launch events, and more

 - Cross-functional partnership — Work closely with product, marketing, and sales to surface community insights, close feedback loops, and amplify launches

The ideal candidate has:

 - 2 - 4 years experience leading community efforts at fast-growth B2B

 - Bonus points for experience building partner, agency, or ambassador programs — you know how to turn a partner into a self-sustaining engine of events and content

 - Hands-on experience in managing online community programs, including stellar written and verbal communication skills to build positive relationships 1:1 and at scale

 - Strong understanding of what motivates and engages online communities, and the ability to systemize and operationalize those levers

 - A genuine pulse on the modern GTM and growth marketing landscape — you know who the AI-pilled operators are, you follow the conversations, and you might already be one of them

 - An educator's mindset — you love breaking down complex ideas and making people feel capable and excited

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration skills

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward building — this is a zero-to-one role

jobs.title: Founding Growth Manager

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ploy is hiring its first Growth Manager to own everything that happens after a deal closes. You'll be the reason customers launch fast, see impact immediately, and become long-term Ploy advocates.

This is a high-ownership, cross-functional role at an early-stage startup. You'll be equal parts project manager, onboarding specialist, and marketing practitioner — someone who can sit across from a customer's growth team and immediately earn their trust.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Your goal is to shorten the path to value for Ploy customers. To achieve this goal, you'll own account strategy, implementation, onboarding, training and support for Ploy customers.

Key responsibilities:

 - Lead customer onboarding end-to-end: kickoff, requirements, setup, launch, and handoff

 - Configure and validate the customer’s setup in Ploy:
 
 - Design system / brand system setup
 
 - Knowledge base setup (structure + initial content hygiene)
 
 - Core integrations setup and verification
 
 - Initial “ploybooks” configuration and scheduled ploys that match the customer’s goals

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Customers launch on time with a working, correct setup (brand system, KB, integrations, initial ploys)

 - Customers reach “first value” quickly (they can point to a tangible outcome in the first week or two)

 - Fewer onboarding escalations and less founder/engineering involvement over time
